# The Evaluating Self: rules, theses and claims

Author: Abhinav Gautam. Every statement below is one sentence a reader can check against its source; the chapters are at https://abhinavgautam.in/.

## Rules
- Once a person or a model is scored on a measure, the measure stops meaning what it named. (Whoever is scored learns to raise the score, so it drifts away from the goal it stood for. Before you trust a score, find out what behaviour it paid for.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#r-a-measure-scored-on-stops-measuring
- What a person or a system is doing inside cannot be read from what it produces. (The same output can come from understanding or imitation, from care or neglect. Arguments about what is inside end up settled by the definition each side chose, not by evidence.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#r-the-inside-is-not-readable-from-the-outside
- A tool that removes the beginner's share of a job leaves nobody able to do the expert's share later (The machine rarely takes the expert's work; it makes the beginner optional, and the beginner's work was how competence got built. If you hand over the routine and the unpolished parts, keep a named share of them in the hands of whoever is learning, on real cases, with someone watching.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#r-remove-the-junior-and-lose-the-expert
- A score answers the question its test asked, which is almost never the question your decision is asking (A number is only ever about the quantity someone chose to measure, on the cases they chose, with the comparison they chose, and any of those three can make an accurate score useless to you. Before you let a score decide anything, write down the quantity your decision actually needs and ask whether the test measured that on cases like yours.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#r-a-score-answers-its-own-question
- You cannot examine what you are identified with from inside it; it changes only when something makes it an object. (A role, a skill or a belief that you take to be yourself cannot be weighed while it is you. Something has to set it apart first, and letting go of it needs your worth to rest on something else.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#r-what-you-are-identified-with-is-invisible-from-inside
- Accuracy comes from many small revisions, so count how often you revise and how often you explain something away (Being right is a habit of correction rather than a quality of the first answer, and a wrong belief stays alive because each detail that does not fit gets a small cheap excuse that nobody keeps count of. Date your answers, revise them in small steps as evidence arrives, and keep a tally of the excuses, because the tally is the only thing that makes the pattern visible.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#r-small-revisions-beat-being-sure
- Neither a person nor a system records why it acted, so every account of its reasoning is built afterwards. (The explanation is produced later, by a process meant for telling others, and it can be sincere and wrong. Treat a stated reason as a story about the act, not a record of it.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#r-reasons-are-reconstructed-after-the-fact
- How easy, hard or certain a situation feels is made inside you and tells you about you, not the situation. (The feeling of ease, difficulty or confidence is produced by the mind separately from the facts. Read it as a sign of your own state, and check the situation by other means.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#r-how-it-feels-is-evidence-about-the-person
- Nobody who built the tool can explain it or answer for its output, so both fall to you (The designers are not present, the picture in their heads was never shared, and nothing inside a working system records why its parts are there. You learn the tool only from what it does in front of you, and you are the only person answerable for what you send out.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#r-nobody-who-built-the-tool-is-here
- How sure you feel is no test of being right, and only practice at the task itself corrects it (The sense that an answer is good is built by a separate machinery from the one that produced the answer, so it can rise while accuracy stays put or falls. The repair is not resolve or humility but minutes of real training in the thing being judged, which moves the self-estimate by moving the ability under it.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#r-judging-your-own-answer-is-a-skill
- An assistant's voice and its agreement were trained by other people, so neither says anything about the answer (How it sounds, how sure it seems and whether it goes along with you were set by a small paid group and by whatever text was on the web, not by your question. State the audience, the conventions and the form you want, because everything you leave unstated you take from them.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#r-the-manner-came-from-somebody-else
- Skill arrives long before understanding, so work that comes out right proves nothing about understanding (Competence is put together out of parts that understand nothing, and the account of what was done turns up late and is written for somebody else. A person or a machine can do the thing well and hold no picture of how. Test the work, and treat any explanation as a separate product to be tested on its own.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#r-skill-arrives-before-understanding
- You can direct work you could not do yourself by comparing finished attempts early rather than watching the doing (Choosing between two results is much easier than producing one, and watching a process as it runs catches almost nothing. Ask for rough versions early, choose between them and say why, set how closely you look by the person's experience at that particular task, and make one named person answerable for the finished result.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#r-direct-by-comparing-not-by-watching
- Work goes to a machine where the surroundings can be controlled and written down, not where it looks easy (The line between what a machine takes and what a person keeps runs through the setting, not through the difficulty of the task. Before you hand anything over, ask what it would cost to make its surroundings predictable and to say exactly what a good result is, and treat that cost as part of the price.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#r-a-controlled-setting-is-what-gets-automated
- How a model was trained decides what it can do, and its size does not (The gains that matter came from what the training text was and what the training rewarded, not from more parameters. When you choose a model, or hear that a new one is larger, find out what its training aimed at and expect nothing outside that.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#r-a-bigger-model-is-not-better
- The line between you and your tools is drawn by feeling, so it cannot settle who worked (What counts as part of you is decided by warmth and familiarity, and that boundary moves in a minute or over a career. Asking whether the work happened inside you or inside the tool therefore has no fixed answer. Use a test that does not depend on how the tool feels.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#r-where-you-end-is-set-by-feeling
- The feeling of having done it is added afterwards, so say in advance who is answerable (The sense that you were the one who did something is built separately from the doing, and it can be present when you did not act and absent when you did. Nothing inside a person reports authorship, so who owns a piece of work is a thing people agree on beforehand, not a thing anyone discovers afterwards. Name the answerable person while the work is being set up.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#r-authorship-is-assigned-not-felt
- You lose a state by watching how it comes and goes, not by attacking it (Going at an unwanted state directly costs more than the state and tends to keep it in place, while turning it into something you can look at loosens it without being asked to. Effort clears the ground and gets a person ready; it does not manufacture the result. So make the state an object of attention and stop trying to remove it.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#r-watching-a-state-beats-attacking-it
- What you read the work with decides what you find, so name the frame before you trust the finding (Nothing arrives raw. A living thing computes an answer and then treats it as a property of the world, an editor's choice of how to read a text decides what the text is taken to claim, and an instrument finds whatever its concepts told it to count. The finding is worth what the frame behind it is worth, so state the frame first and ask what result it could not have produced.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#r-the-frame-decides-what-you-find
- Judgement fails far downstream of attention, so guard what you dwell on rather than the decision (By the time a judgement goes wrong the chain that produced it started several steps earlier, with what the person kept turning over. What a person repeatedly attends to is also what they become, which is why an industry built to capture attention takes something that cannot be handed back. Put the controls on what gets your attention, not on the moment of deciding.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#r-guard-attention-not-the-decision
- No tool, technique or amount of supervision helps in itself; each fits one level of skill and harms another. (The help that carries a beginner holds back an expert, and the reverse. Set the amount of help per task and per person instead of adopting one policy for everyone.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#r-nothing-helps-in-itself-it-has-to-fit-the-receiver
- Standing, style and agreement say nothing about an answer, so test the answer against the thing it is about (Almost everything that makes an answer feel checked is a fact about where it came from rather than about whether it is true, and every one of those signs can be produced without the truth behind it. Keep the test on the thing itself, something in the world that could come out against you, and treat the source's rank, manner, fluency and readiness to agree as carrying no information.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#r-test-the-answer-not-the-source
- Arguments about who is really doing the work turn on the definition, so fix that before gathering evidence (Whether a person is free, whether a self is real, whether a machine understands or feels anything, each of these is decided by the meaning the arguers picked, and no experiment reaches a definition. Two people with the same evidence and different definitions will never converge. Agree what the word has to mean, and what would count as failing it, before anyone collects a result.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#r-the-definition-settles-the-argument
- Every account of how the work is going passes through someone with a stake, so smooth news is filtered news (Once you hand work over, what reaches you is a report, and each person it passes through has a reason to round off the bad parts. Get the work itself read by someone with nothing invested in it, ask the person directly and say their answer back to them, and treat an unusually clean report as a reason to go and look.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#r-a-smooth-report-is-filtering
- A check is worth only what the person checking could have produced on their own (Looking over an answer you could not have produced yourself is not checking, it is agreeing more slowly. Before you accept the job of checking something, ask whether you could get to the answer without it; if you could not, either build that ability or stop calling the step a check.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#r-a-check-needs-the-skill-it-checks
- A hunch is worth only what the field taught it, so trust it where the work answers back quickly (A hunch is a memory being recognised, so it carries information only where the situations repeat and the world tells you soon enough that you were wrong. Judge the field before you judge the person: in a field that repeats and corrects, take the hunch seriously and dig out the cue behind it; in one that does not, credentials and years buy nothing.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#r-a-hunch-is-worth-its-feedback
- An explanation makes people accept an answer more often without helping them tell good answers from bad. (Explanations feel like evidence, but in the studies they raised acceptance and left error-finding unchanged. Treat an explanation as persuasion until it has helped you catch a mistake.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#r-an-explanation-moves-agreement-not-judgement
- A failure shows up where it lands, not where it starts, so the complaint about the tool usually points upstream. (The tool gets blamed because that is where the error becomes visible. Most of the time the fault is in the specification, the data or the design, and fixing the tool leaves it in place.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#r-the-failure-shows-downstream-of-its-cause
- Ask the same person or model the same question twice, because the gap between the answers is a measurement (You usually cannot find out whether an answer is right, but you can always find out whether it is stable, and an unstable answer cannot be mostly right. Re-ask the same case on another day, in another wording, or of another qualified person, and treat the spread you get as the first number you know about the answer.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#r-ask-the-same-question-twice
- People do what their setup makes easy, so change the setup instead of asking them to be more careful. (The procedure, the display and who answers for the outcome shape behaviour more than instructions do. Telling someone to be careful changes nothing; changing what is easy does.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#r-change-the-arrangement-not-the-person
- Everything you find out about a model has a date on it, so write the date down (Models are replaced, published tests get trained on, and the language inside one is frozen at the moment its text was collected. Record the date beside every limit you find, and run the failing case again when the model changes.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#r-everything-you-learn-about-it-expires
- Telling a person their work is wrong threatens their standing, so settle that first or the correction does not land (The check you owe handed-over work costs something a machine never charges you: the person defends themselves instead of taking it in, and arguing harder makes it worse. Steady what they are worth outside the thing under question, keep the question on the work and its conditions, and say who is answerable without naming a culprit.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#r-correction-lands-on-the-person
- A person whose standing is in question defends it, so steady that from elsewhere before you criticise (When a person's sense of being good and capable is under threat, they spend the moment protecting it rather than taking in what was said, and better arguments do not get through. What does get through is a reminder of something they value in another part of life, given before the bad news and without being explained. Steady the person first, then deliver the finding.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#r-a-threatened-person-defends-instead-of-learning
- A model answers a rare fact as confidently as a common one, so supply the rare facts yourself (The smoothness of the wording is produced separately from whether the thing is true, and the errors concentrate on whatever the training text saw once. Put the names, dates and numbers into the prompt instead of asking the model to remember them.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#r-most-fluent-where-it-knows-least
- The better a machine works, the less anyone watches it, so the check has to be scheduled, not triggered. (Nothing punishes inattention while the machine is right, so attention fades, and nobody is watching at the moment it is wrong. A fixed schedule of independent checks catches what a trigger never will.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#r-reliability-removes-the-check
- How much mind you see in a person or machine comes from you and decides how you treat them (Whether something strikes you as having a mind is settled at your end, by resemblance, nearness, loneliness and the words you happen to use, and it varies steadily from person to person. The same reading that grants a machine a mind takes mind away from people you cannot read. Watch what your own attribution is doing, because it decides what you owe the thing and what you expect of it.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#r-how-much-mind-you-grant-is-your-decision
- What you lose by handing work over depends on which part went, but people hand over whatever feels hard. (Offloading the routine part and offloading the judging part cost different things, and neither cost shows at the time. Choose what to hand over by what you need to keep, not by what feels effortful.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#r-which-part-of-the-task-went-decides-what-is-lost
- A famous result gets used far beyond the sample, the control and the measure that produced it. (The finding is quoted; the study's limits are not. Before acting on a claim, find the study design behind it and check that it covers your case.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#r-a-result-outruns-the-design-that-produced-it
- Handing work over gives up the claim to be its author; the work and the answerability stay where they were. (Delegation moves the doing, not the responsibility. What hurts in handing over is losing authorship of the result, and that is also what keeps a person answerable for it.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#r-the-claim-on-the-result-is-what-binds
- What keeps you working is your conditions and work that waits for you, not more of what you want (Wanting is manufactured inside a person on its own schedule, so getting more of what was wanted never delivers the state that was being aimed at. What does hold a person to work is a setting that meets their needs and a piece of work outside them that will not get done otherwise. Arrange the conditions and point at the unfinished thing instead of raising the reward or the exhortation.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#r-conditions-and-unfinished-work-keep-you-going
- What an expert acts on cannot be taught in a course or got by asking, so choose someone practised (Some of what a job needs is recognition built up over years of particular cases, and neither a briefing, a written procedure nor an interview about method transfers it. Match the work to someone who has met that kind of case before and seen how it came out; where nobody has, hand over a smaller piece and keep the judgement.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#r-some-of-the-job-cannot-be-taught
- You keep only the skills you keep practising with feedback; whatever you hand to a tool decays unnoticed. (Delegated skill fades, and your own sense of the skill does not register the loss. If you will need to check a tool's work, keep doing some of that work yourself.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#r-skill-lives-only-where-it-is-exercised
- Whichever answer you meet first becomes your answer, so commit to your own before the machine's or the group's appears. (An anchor, a suggestion or a majority view moves where a judgement ends, and the judge cannot feel it happening. Write your own answer down first; then look at theirs.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#r-the-first-answer-becomes-the-answer
- Whatever you hand over comes back as checking, so count the checking before you count the saving (The making of the thing moves; the answering for it does not, so verification stops being a stage and becomes the work. Budget that time openly, give it to somebody who has nothing else to do at that moment, and measure what was actually saved rather than what it felt like.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#r-handing-over-returns-as-checking
- Whether the tool helps depends on the task, and only trying it on your own work shows where (There is a real line between the work the tool improves and the work it damages, and the line is unmarked and not where people expect it. Published scores and other people's experience will not locate it for you, so keep a small set of cases from your own work and score them yourself.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#r-only-your-own-task-finds-the-edge
- No technique turns a confusing situation into a problem, so state the problem and the test yourself (The model answers the question you actually asked, and building that question out of a mess is the one step nothing performs for you. Write the problem in a sentence, and write what would make an answer wrong, before you start asking.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#r-no-method-sets-the-problem-for-you
- Some failures are built into how the model reads and was scored, and no wording reaches them (A prompt arrives after the input has been chopped into pieces and after the training has fixed what gets rewarded, so there are errors the prompt cannot touch. When a failure survives two honest rewordings, stop rewording and change the input, the tool, or the way the job is divided.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#r-some-failures-sit-below-the-prompt
- A person reshapes whatever job you hand them, and their reason for doing it predicts how long it lasts (What you hand over is a description, and the person turns it into a job of their own making, which is why two people under one description do different work. You cannot order the reshaping or the reason, so hand over the result you want with room in how it is reached, and find out what the person makes of it.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#r-people-reshape-the-job-you-hand-them

## Theses
- An appearance does no harm, the error is how it is taken, and the teaching is a way of looking (Sarvapriyananda says the whole apparatus of witness, veil and three selves is a way of teaching rather than a list of things that exist, and reading it as a list is the error the texts warn against. The Drig-Drishya Viveka makes the point at verses 13 and 15, where what gets hidden is never the rope but its being a rope, so the appearance itself does no damage until a difference is forgotten. Easwaran's Upanishads and the Pañcadaśī are read the same way, as procedures with one part of ignorance producing the grief. All of it is illustration, and the move insulates the teaching, since anything that fails can be called method rather than doctrine.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#t-an-appearance-does-no-harm-the-error-is-how-it-is-taken-and-the-teaching-is-a-wa
- Made-up facts come from how a model is trained and scored, not from a fixable bug (Kalai and his co-authors prove a floor. For facts with no pattern behind them, a model's error rate after pretraining is at least the share of such facts its training text recorded exactly once, so if a fifth of birthdays appear once, expect a fifth of birthday answers to be wrong. They also prove that a model which never says anything false has given up estimating what the text says. Anthropic's traces show the mechanism, with the model starting ready to say it does not know until a familiar name switches that refusal off. Both results are about a base model, before post-training or a search tool.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#t-made-up-facts-come-from-how-a-model-is-trained-and-scored-not-from-a-fixable-bug
- A study with no control group cannot rule out the opposite reading, so finding nothing is not finding safety (Jost's one null result, asking a model to explain a coding problem, was a rank correlation of -0.201 on thirty-two students, with p at 0.135 and an interval running from -0.523 to +0.220. That interval contains real harm, so the study failed to detect an effect rather than clearing the practice. The same study has no control group and no random assignment, so the reverse reading, that the students who reached for a model most were already behind, fits the data equally well, and the first-year marks that would settle it were never brought in. Hagendorff makes the same complaint about tests of models. Three of the six claims here are themselves contested.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#t-a-study-with-no-control-group-cannot-rule-out-the-opposite-reading-so-finding-no
- How closely to supervise depends on the person's experience at that task and drops back when the task changes (Readiness to work unsupervised belongs to a task rather than to a person, so a proven worker needs close direction again when the job or the pace changes. Grove sets the dial by the delegate's experience at that particular task and says none of the three styles is kinder than the others, and he advises checking at the rough draft, where a mistake costs least. Dreyfus reports the same fall for experts whose field changes under them. Only one claim counts as evidence, Hadfield-Menell's proof that a machine unsure of its user's goal checks before acting. Grove's own support is two anecdotes, and nine managers in ten judged themselves more hands-off than their people did.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#t-how-closely-to-supervise-depends-on-the-person-s-experience-at-that-task-and-dro
- Minutes of training in a skill corrects how well people judge their own work at it (Kruger and Dunning randomly assigned 70 of 140 participants to a ten-minute training packet, and the worst performers' view of their own work came right while the untrained bottom quarter moved the wrong way over the same interval, from 5.8 to 6.3. The training worked through the skill rather than through humility, and its effect on self-assessment disappears once the change in ability is held constant. Tetlock found that an hour spent reading forecasting guidelines raised accuracy by roughly ten per cent for about a year, tested against untrained forecasters on identical questions. Both results come from two sources only, and both were measured in a study rather than at work.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#t-minutes-of-training-in-a-skill-corrects-how-well-people-judge-their-own-work-at-
- Good forecasters change their minds on new evidence, while a wrong belief survives by explaining away each awkward detail (Tetlock's best forecasters revise often and in small steps: Tim Minto made thirty-four revisions on one question, averaging three and a half points, and willingness to change your mind predicted accuracy about three times as strongly as intelligence did. The opposite habit keeps a wrong belief alive by giving each detail that does not fit a small, cheap excuse, and Klein points out that nobody keeps count of them. Schon watched children call a counterweighted block impossible rather than drop the rule that blocks balance in the middle. Revising needs a trigger, though: Schon argues only a surprise you dislike forces one, and Sapolsky finds lasting stress makes people repeat an action harder instead.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#t-good-forecasters-change-their-minds-on-new-evidence-while-a-wrong-belief-survive
- Most of the thinking left to a worker using an AI tool is checking and fixing its output (Lee asked 319 knowledge workers what critical thinking they had done with a generative tool. Six described working out the goal before opening it and 30 described shaping the query, against 125 who judged the output and 114 who checked it against an outside source. Evaluation was also the one activity that got harder, since workers reported less effort at all six of Bloom's levels except this one, where the smallest majority said less and the largest minority said more. METR puts a stopwatch on it, with developers accepting fewer than 44 per cent of what the model wrote and spending 9 per cent of their working time reviewing and cleaning what they kept.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#t-most-of-the-thinking-left-to-a-worker-using-an-ai-tool-is-checking-and-fixing-it
- A tool that lets experts work without juniors removes the work that made juniors able to check it (The machine does not take the expert's job, it makes the junior optional, and the junior's work was how competence got built. Beane watched ninety-four operations across five hospitals: residents did surgical work for almost the whole of an open procedure and ten to twenty times less of a robotic one, where the surgeon sits alone at a console. Mollick makes the same point about entry-level work in law and software. All eight claims lean one way and none is filed against, but the evidence is one speciality, observed rather than randomised. Beane's bomb-disposal teams, who put the controller in a trainee's hands, show that deployment decides this and not the machine.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#t-a-tool-that-lets-experts-work-without-juniors-removes-the-work-that-made-juniors
- The first number or starting point a judge sees moves the final answer without them noticing (Two claims sit here. Kahneman's is that people judge an outcome as a gain or a loss measured from a starting point rather than as a level of wealth, and that a loss feels about twice as heavy as a gain of the same size. Tetlock turns the same fact into a working order, to ask how often such things happen in general before looking at the particular case, because whichever number you meet first is where your estimate settles. Neither half is strong alone. Tetlock's ordering has never been tested against the reverse, and the endowment effect that follows from Kahneman's kink does not appear among experienced traders.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#t-the-first-number-or-starting-point-a-judge-sees-moves-the-final-answer-without-t
- The design of these models has barely changed since 2017 and only the amount of training text grew (Vaswani's layer has kept its shape since 2017 while its details moved. Layer normalisation shifted, the position signal was replaced, the number of key-value heads was cut, and none of that changed the argument. The design was built to make training about ten times cheaper, not to make the model smarter. Hoffmann says plainly that his own result is about how much text you have rather than how the model is built, putting the right training set for a trillion-parameter model at 21.2 trillion words. Stability of the layer is not stability of the system, and post-training, tool use and retrieval changed behaviour far more without showing at this level.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#t-the-design-of-these-models-has-barely-changed-since-2017-and-only-the-amount-of-
- How much a person likes hard thinking is a steady trait apart from ability, and it predicts behaviour weakly (Cacioppo and Petty's measure correlates .24 with verbal intelligence and -.03 with abstract reasoning, so liking hard thought is not the same as being good at it. The eighteen-item questionnaire measures one thing, since the short form takes 37 per cent of the variance on its first factor and the one serious attempt to split it into three failed. The behavioural differences are real and small, about a fifth to a half of a standard deviation across recall, information seeking and enjoyment. Paying people for hard thinking reduces it in exactly the people who liked it. Against it, low scorers do examine an argument when the speaker is untrustworthy, and the note rests on one source.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#t-how-much-a-person-likes-hard-thinking-is-a-steady-trait-apart-from-ability-and-i
- The same expert judging the same case twice gives two different answers (A professional is not the same measuring instrument on two occasions. Wine judges scored 18 per cent of the same wines identically on a second tasting, software developers estimating the same task on two days differed by 71 per cent, and opioids were prescribed more often late in the day across nearly seven hundred thousand primary care visits. Two underwriters at one insurer, pricing the same file, differed by a median of 55 per cent, against the 10 per cent their executives had predicted. Sapolsky adds that the frontal cortex tires first, so timing shifts judgement, but that mechanism is listed as contested and controlling sleep and time of day does not drain the spread.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#t-the-same-expert-judging-the-same-case-twice-gives-two-different-answers
- Knowing which group someone belongs to tells you little about how they will act (Group membership predicts conduct poorly, and reading an individual off their category misses the person in front of you. Frankl says knowing whether a man was a guard or a prisoner told you almost nothing, since one camp commander bought medicine with his own money and a senior prisoner was harder than any guard. Epley supplies the mechanism: a mind you cannot read is treated as smaller rather than as unknown, so distant groups are judged less able to feel shame or remorse and their apologies count for less. Only two claims and two sources, and Frankl's half is an observation from a single extreme setting.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#t-knowing-which-group-someone-belongs-to-tells-you-little-about-how-they-will-act
- A hunch is recognition of something already met, so it is reliable only in a field the person has practised (Kahneman and Klein agree that intuition is recognition and nothing more, since a cue in the situation reaches a memory and the memory supplies the answer. Chase and Simon estimated fifty to a hundred thousand recognisable patterns built over about a decade, and a chess master who rebuilds two-thirds of a real board after five seconds manages two or three pieces of a random one. So a hunch is worth only the practice behind it and the regularity of the world, which puts fireground commanders inside the condition and stock pickers outside it. Expertise attaches to particular tasks rather than to people, and feedback that confirms a wrong hunch is worse than none.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#t-a-hunch-is-recognition-of-something-already-met-so-it-is-reliable-only-in-a-fiel
- A person whose worth is under threat defends themselves instead of learning, and argument does not change that (Cohen and Sherman's review shows the defensive response produced at will across unrelated domains, from rationalising a trivial choice to partisans refuting contrary evidence, and shows what is being defended is a broad sense of being a good and capable person rather than being good at the thing under attack. That is why writing about a value from an unrelated part of life calms the threat while affirming inside the threatened domain makes it worse. Chatterjee and Shankara read the same pattern in Arjuna's collapse, and Krishna's reply replaces his way of seeing rather than arguing with it. Several of the laboratory effects have come back smaller or absent in larger replications, and Chatterjee's version is not falsifiable.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#t-a-person-whose-worth-is-under-threat-defends-themselves-instead-of-learning-and-
- Everything a person does has causes behind it, and people who drop blame for that reason do not behave worse (Every action has a history behind it, and letting go of blame on that ground does not make people worse. Sapolsky's Determined argues that randomness is not freedom, that chaos removes predictability without leaving anything free, and that willpower is brain tissue shaped by luck. The strongest number is a 2022 meta-analysis of 145 experiments, 95 of them unpublished, finding no consistent effect of weakened free-will belief on ethical behaviour, and society has twice dropped blame without falling apart. Two claims stand against: Sapolsky defines free will as a cause with no cause, which settles the argument before evidence arrives, and Seth counts free will as a real skill.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#t-everything-a-person-does-has-causes-behind-it-and-people-who-drop-blame-for-that
- Training and size improve only what they were aimed at and leave toxicity and bias where they were (Chinchilla beat Gopher on a truthfulness test, 43.6 per cent against 29.5, and its average toxicity did not fall at all. Ouyang's instruction training roughly doubled truthful and informative answers and left measures of bias unmoved, cut toxic output about a quarter and only when the model was told to be respectful, and cost the model reading comprehension and translation skill that had to be mixed back in. Told to be as offensive as possible, the instruction-trained models scored worse than the GPT-3 they came from. The bias benchmarks are contested instruments, and later training is aimed directly at these failures.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#t-training-and-size-improve-only-what-they-were-aimed-at-and-leave-toxicity-and-bi
- Skill comes before understanding, and understanding is a late product of a process that has none (Dennett's case is that design fills the living world without anyone understanding anything, so skill comes first and understanding arrives late. Ristau's plover, tested in the 1980s with a remote-controlled buggy carrying a stuffed raccoon, tracks where the predator is looking and performs harder when it loses interest, without holding the plan. Agüera y Arcas ran 64-byte random strings together in a soup and after millions of interactions they began copying themselves, with nothing selected for and mutation switched off. All four supporting claims carry measurements rather than argument. Against them stands the argument that predicting the next word well requires knowing how the world works.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#t-skill-comes-before-understanding-and-understanding-is-a-late-product-of-a-proces
- AI help slows experienced people most on work they know best while it still feels faster to them (Measured time and felt time move apart. In METR's randomised trial, sixteen experienced developers fixing real issues in codebases they had worked on for years took about nineteen per cent longer with AI help than without, while writing forty-seven per cent more code per hour, and the slowdown was largest where their own knowledge ran deepest. Economists and machine-learning researchers asked to predict the result guessed thirty-eight to thirty-nine per cent faster. Sixteen people is a thin base, the confidence interval reaches close to no effect, and the participants were picked for exactly the deep familiarity the authors name as the cause, which most work does not have.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#t-ai-help-slows-experienced-people-most-on-work-they-know-best-while-it-still-feel
- People keep going for something outside themselves that waits to be done, and it is never finished (What holds a person up is something outside them that is waiting, and it is a direction rather than an arrival. Frankl argues people endure more when a person needs them or work is left that only they can finish, and he turned back two prisoners who meant to kill themselves this way. He also saw the control case: with no known end date a person stops aiming at the future, and a day in the camp felt longer than a week. Hayes says the same from the clinic, that a value is a direction you never finish reaching. Frankl's evidence comes only from survivors.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#t-people-keep-going-for-something-outside-themselves-that-waits-to-be-done-and-it-
- Whether you see a mind in a machine depends on you, not on the machine (Whether a mind appears in an object is decided at the viewer's end. Waytz, Cacioppo and Epley found this is a steady trait people differ on rather than something everyone does equally, and that resemblance, distance and loneliness move both it and the refusal to grant minds to people. Reeves and Nass found that people apply politeness and taking sides to computers on the slightest cue without believing for a moment the machine is a person. Seth adds that language does most of the work, and that calling a model's mistake a hallucination already grants it a mind. Two of the seven claims are contested.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#t-whether-you-see-a-mind-in-a-machine-depends-on-you-not-on-the-machine
- An expert recognises what kind of situation this is, and the action comes with the recognition (Klein interviewed experienced fire commanders under time pressure and found they do not weigh options against each other. They recognise the kind of situation they are in, and the action to take arrives with the recognition, tested if at all by imagining that one option play out and watching for what goes wrong. Dreyfus puts it as skill growing by dropping rules rather than collecting them. Three of the five claims here are contested. The interviews were coded by the researchers who ran them, Klein's count of about three moving parts has never been replicated, and his 2009 settlement with Kahneman narrows all of it to fields with valid cues and a fair chance to learn them.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#t-an-expert-recognises-what-kind-of-situation-this-is-and-the-action-comes-with-th
- Judgment fails at the end of a chain that begins with what you dwell on, not at the decision (Gita 2.62 and 2.63 set out a sequence with seven steps: dwelling on something leads to attachment, then desire, then anger, then delusion, then confused memory, and only at the end the loss of judgment. The practical point is that the place to intervene is the first step, not the last. One verse pair from one source carries it, and nothing is measured. These are states a person can notice in themselves, offered as a causal chain, with no evidence that the links run in that order or that breaking an early one prevents the later ones.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#t-judgment-fails-at-the-end-of-a-chain-that-begins-with-what-you-dwell-on-not-at-t
- Beyond competence people improve by reorganising what they know rather than adding rules, and courses cannot take them there (Past the stage the Dreyfus brothers call competence, a learner stops collecting rules and starts responding to whole situations, and that cannot be handed over in a course. Klein's fireground study is the strongest number: of 156 decision points from non-routine incidents, 127 were recognitional and only 18 involved comparing options, and half the comparisons came from one fire staffed by novices. Papert's conservation result makes the same point about children, whose largest step adds no new skill, only a better way of managing old ones. Three of the nine claims are contested and Klein's is also filed against. Sweller keeps explicit instruction all the way up, with randomised trials behind him.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#t-beyond-competence-people-improve-by-reorganising-what-they-know-rather-than-addi
- A person cannot see the errors in his own work, but someone with nothing at stake can (Attachment to your own work hides its faults, so the reading has to come from someone with nothing invested in it. Weinberg's founding case is one afternoon of colleagues reading his code: seventeen errors in thirteen instructions, and no further error in nine years across a dozen installations. He claims the gain shows up as delivery dates that vary less rather than as work finishing faster. Beane adds that expertise narrows what anyone notices, since eighty-three per cent of radiologists hunting for lung nodules missed a picture of a gorilla forty-eight times larger. Only one of the four claims counts as evidence, and the gorilla is a search task rather than a professional judgement.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#t-a-person-cannot-see-the-errors-in-his-own-work-but-someone-with-nothing-at-stake
- Trying harder to read another person raises your confidence but not your accuracy (Epley's evidence is that confidence in reading another mind far outruns accuracy, and that longer acquaintance raises only the confidence. Dating partners predicted each other's answers 44 per cent of the time and believed they had got 82 per cent right. Imagining yourself in someone's position does not help and can hurt, because it runs your own mind inside a stereotype. People who switched to the method that halved their errors felt no more confident than before, so confidence cannot tell you which method is working. Support is weak at one source, and the accuracies are modest rather than zero, so the gap is the finding rather than a failure of mind reading.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#t-trying-harder-to-read-another-person-raises-your-confidence-but-not-your-accurac
- A habit you keep failing to break is protecting you, and small tests of the fear behind it work (Kegan and Lahey argue that repeated failure to change is not weak willpower but a second commitment the failure serves, so the way out is to find the fear behind it and run small, safe tests of it. Their coaching cases show people with the same goal and behaviour having entirely different hidden commitments, and a humanities department that had tenured nobody in eleven years moved only once someone said aloud what it was protecting. The evidence is selected cases from their own practice with no controls, the opening one-in-seven heart-patients figure carries no citation, and the rule that a first answer is a cover cannot be tested from inside the method.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#t-a-habit-you-keep-failing-to-break-is-protecting-you-and-small-tests-of-the-fear-
- Awareness is what everything is known by, and it stays through waking, dream and sleep while their contents drop out (Whoever does the knowing cannot be found among the things known, and these texts test that across waking, dream and sleep, where contents drop out and something stays to report. The Panchadasi argues that nobody could remember an empty sleep without having been present for it. The Mandukya says the fourth is what waking, dream and sleep are made of, and in the Upanishads light means what you see by, not brightness. Nine opinion claims from four contemplative sources. Three stand against, including Rahula's no thinker behind the thought, Gaudapada treating his own teaching as a ladder to throw away, and the warning that the match with information theory turns on one word.) - Guessing the next word well requires knowing how the world works, so there is no shortcut (Agüera y Arcas argues that doing the prediction properly means solving general intelligence rather than dodging it. His example is translation: turn a sentence about dropping a bowling ball on a violin and having to get it repaired into Spanish, and the gendered pronoun forces you to know which object broke. The thesis rests on one source and one claim, which the note marks as opinion rather than evidence. Bender and colleagues read the same facts the other way, saying a system trained on form alone never reaches meaning, and that a beaten test is weak proof it was the right test.) - When a job asks for a different kind of mind, training and new skills cannot supply it (Training works on what a mind holds, while some demands are about how it is organised, and adding skills leaves that untouched. Kegan and Lahey give a test anyone can run, that a behaviour returning after honest effort is doing a job for the person. Their case is Peter, whose ten pounds stayed off for four years while the softened tone he had worked on came back, plus seven per cent, against an average dieter who regains 107 per cent of what was lost. Two claims from two books carry the whole thesis. The test is also backward-looking, and Ericsson holds that much of what is called a difference in kind yields to structured practice.) - AI lifts the weakest workers most, so the work looks alike and no longer shows who made it (If the tool raises the floor more than the ceiling, a finished piece stops telling you what its author can do. Dell'Acqua's consultant experiment found the gap between best and worst narrowing from twenty-two per cent to four, and Mollick reports call-centre workers in the bottom tenth gaining thirty-five per cent against almost nothing for experienced ones. His recommendation letter is the same point about signalling, since the hours it stood for were the message. Three of the four claims are marked contested. The homogenisation finding was dropped from the published version of Dell'Acqua's paper, and the levelling reversed among Kenyan entrepreneurs, where the strongest gained and the weakest did worse.) - Waking life and science are each checked only from inside themselves, so neither reaches reality directly (Nothing checks waking except more waking, and nothing checks science except whether it works for people like us. Gaudapada's Mandukya Karika argues that waking is worth no more than dreaming and that a thing missing before and after is missing in between. The Yoga Vasistha's King Lavana shuts his eyes in court for under an hour and comes out having lived seven years, so felt duration measures nothing outside itself. Thompson pushes the same move onto science. All five claims are opinion or contested, from three sources with no evidence, and Thompson's step is disputed and hard to hold without losing the ground to state it.) - How much of a mind something has is a matter of degree, and how much it is owed follows (Hofstadter argues that having a soul is a question of how much rather than whether, with beings sitting at different points on one scale, and he accepts the consequence that they differ in how much consideration they are owed. The unit of measurement is his own invention and he says so; there is no procedure for placing anything on the scale, so it cannot be shown wrong about any case. One source carries the whole claim, marked contested, with nothing recorded against it. Over's 2021 argument cuts against the use it is usually put to, that people who treat others cruelly understand perfectly well how human their victims are.) - A striking result about a model usually comes from the measure chosen, not from the model (Schaeffer's arithmetic is explicit. A per-token probability of 0.6 scores 0.08 across five tokens while 0.9 scores 0.59, so the underlying quantity improves by half and the score improves sevenfold, which is what a sudden jump in ability looks like. Metrics such as Exact String Match sit behind more than 92 per cent of 137 hand-annotated claimed abilities, and his team produced sharp new abilities on demand in image networks by changing the score. Wei's own loss curves fall steadily through the range of scales where the headline score sits at random. The paper attacks particular examples rather than the idea, and names two rival accounts it does not rule out.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#t-a-striking-result-about-a-model-usually-comes-from-the-measure-chosen-not-from-t
- What an expert acts on is missing from the textbooks and cannot be got by asking about method (Klein found that experts can name the signs they act on, but only if you ask about particular past cases rather than about their method. His neonatal nurses had nothing to say about sepsis until asked about particular babies, and a large share of the cues they then named appear nowhere in the professional literature. Often the tip-off is an expected event that did not occur, which leaves nothing to point at. Schon says the same of quality judgements a practitioner can state no criteria for. It is all reconstructed from interviews with people recalling cases they chose to report, and an absence noticed in hindsight is the easiest cue to over-report.) - Every level of a reporting chain strips out bad news, so a smooth report shows the filtering (Each reviewer removes the extreme items on the way up, and the extremes are the only ones carrying news, so smoothness is what filtering looks like. Weinberg worked the dates backwards on one reporting chain and found a team's monthly submission fell due four days before the month it described began. His other case is the meeting where every leader reports being on schedule until one admits he is behind and the rest follow. Brooks supplies the structural version, since half a project's time goes on testing and the slip surfaces only then. Of three claims one counts as evidence, and Brooks later withdrew the schedule model his rule sits inside.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#t-every-level-of-a-reporting-chain-strips-out-bad-news-so-a-smooth-report-shows-th
- Knowing whether your answer is right is a separate skill and a machine needs it built in (Fleming's evidence is the core. In a sample of nearly a thousand people, IQ predicted how well they did a task but not how well they judged their own answers, and being overconfident on average turns out to be different from failing to spot a particular mistake. Fleming argues a machine will not acquire self-checking by becoming more capable, and Christian's report of Hadfield-Menell's proof shows what building it in looks like, since a machine unsure of your goal asks first and accepts being switched off. The machine half is opinion carried by analogy, the self-judgement measure is argued over, and training gains are small.) - The argument about free will is decided by how each side defines it, not by any experiment (Each side reaches its answer from the meaning it picked rather than from a result. Sapolsky requires free will to be a cause with nothing causing it, which settles the question before evidence arrives and is why the philosophers he argues against were unmoved. He grants that Libet leaves free will standing and says it does not matter, since forty years of work measured the last few hundred milliseconds before a movement when the question is where the intention came from. Seth picks a different meaning, how well you keep your options open, and counts it real because brain damage takes it away. Three claims, two sources, one contested.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#t-the-argument-about-free-will-is-decided-by-how-each-side-defines-it-not-by-any-e
- Whatever notices a feeling is not itself in it, and you can see this while the feeling lasts (Whatever notices a state is not itself in that state, and the shift can be made while the state is still running. Drig-Drishya Viveka's line is that whatever notices fear is not afraid, its meditations keep pointing back to whoever is having the experience rather than to the experience, and it says enlightenment does not stop pain but changes who is watching it. Hayes reaches the same position from therapy, calling the observing self a viewpoint rather than one of your thoughts. Four opinion claims from two sources, nothing measured, and the evidence for the shift is a report of the kind these texts elsewhere distrust.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#t-whatever-notices-a-feeling-is-not-itself-in-it-and-you-can-see-this-while-the-fe
- You cannot tell from what a system does whether it feels anything, because being smart is not being conscious (Behaviour does not settle whether there is anything it is like to be the system. Seth argues intelligence and consciousness need not travel together, that making a machine smarter does not move it toward feeling, and that a simulated brain is conscious only if consciousness turns out to be computation, which he doubts because a brain has no software separate from its biology. Metzinger offers the one criterion that is not behavioural, saying a machine matters morally once it has a self-model. Eight claims from four sources, none of them evidence and three contested, and the information account admits at its own ending that it never reaches felt experience.) - People treat what others believe as evidence, especially when unsure, and one person disagreeing restores their own answer (Asch's experiment is the core evidence. When a unanimous group gave an obviously wrong answer, about a third of his subjects' judgements followed it, on a task people get right more than 99 per cent of the time alone. Size did not matter, since three opponents produced the full effect and fifteen produced no more, but unanimity did, and a single ally cut errors sharply even when that ally was also wrong. Cialdini adds that people copy others most when unsure, and that telling households their neighbours were saving energy beat appeals to values. Two claims stand against it. A quarter of Asch's subjects never conformed once, and how much people conform shifts with the decade and the country.) - AI helps on the tasks it suits and hurts on the rest, and nobody can tell which is which (Dell'Acqua's consultants working on tasks that suit the tool did better, faster and more completely, all at once. On a task built to defeat it, the same tool dragged them down. Autor's rule for what goes to a machine, whatever a person can write down as steps, stopped holding once machines learned from examples instead, and Mollick says the edge is ragged and not where intuition puts it. Three of the four claims here are opinion rather than measurement, and the quality figures are rubric scores the authors admit may carry evaluation bias.) - People reshape their own jobs to suit themselves and a manager can only make it likelier, never require it (Changing the shape of your own job is done for the worker, not the employer, and a line worker who changes tasks may raise the quality of the work or wreck the flow of it. The one lever Wrzesniewski can show working is meaning, since hospital cleaners used the stated mission to frame cleaning as care. Room to do it depends on the setting, so a cleaner or hairdresser has plenty and a closely watched telemarketer almost none. All four claims come from that single paper, three as opinion, so it stands on thin evidence. The follow-up studies are self-reported at one moment and cannot show which way the cause runs.) - Your explanation of why you decided something is produced by a separate part built for telling other people (Dennett takes the mechanism from McFarland: communicating is the only behaviour that requires an organism to monitor its own control system, so looking inward returns an edited summary built for reporting, not a view of the machinery. Agüera y Arcas adds that the narrating voice is aimed at a listener, since you already know what you are thinking and they do not. Dunbar's measurements in the 1990s, cortex rising with group size and more steeply in apes than monkeys, are the only numbers here. A troop-size correlation fits several stories, and nothing offered separates this account from the simpler one that explaining yourself is just useful.) - A working system does not record why its parts are there, so any account is worked out backwards (Dennett's point is that the reasons a design works are explicit while it is being built and only implicit once it runs, and in anything that evolved they were never written down at all. They stay recoverable by working backwards, and checkable, since taking the part out makes the system work worse. Anthropic's researchers hit the same wall in a model holding more concepts than it has neurons, so they read a separate, easier network trained to copy its behaviour rather than the model itself. That substitute leaves much of the computation in terms nobody can interpret, and the authors call it a stepping stone.) - People examine an argument when they have a reason, a middling demand, and no stress (Cacioppo and Petty's review supplies the shape. The difference between people who enjoy effortful thinking and people who do not appears only when a situation makes middling demands, because when nothing is at stake nobody thinks hard and when everything is, everybody does. Low scorers are not unable to examine an argument, and they did it when the speaker was untrustworthy or the framing unexpected. Buccinca found the same split at the interface, where designs that made people think before seeing the AI's answer helped mainly the high scorers. Fleming adds the ceiling, that self-checking breaks down worst under heavy load and stress. The persuasion work is undergraduates with low stakes.) - A model's test score depends on the wording, the answer order and what it has already read (Hagendorff's point is that a low score may mean the model was asked badly rather than that it cannot do the task, since multiple-choice formats cut reasoning off before it starts and answer order should be shuffled. Binz and Schulz's model answered the taxi problem with 0.2 for a colour that was not in the question, and reordering Wason's cards from A K 4 7 to 4 7 A K changed which cards it picked. Testing with a published puzzle measures what the model has read, and Bender's team note that edited versions of the benchmarks BERT had topped collapse its scores. Hagendorff's own counter is that watching what a model does is still a real explanation.) - The self is a pattern the brain makes by watching itself, built from parts that contain no self (Hofstadter's account is that a self appears when a system watches itself closely enough to build symbols about itself, and that it cannot see the machinery underneath. He takes Gödel as the formal result: any system able to describe patterns ends up containing statements about itself, even where the designers tried to rule that out. He also argues that a machine with no memory and no imagination has no self, and that a pattern rather than its parts can be the real cause. One source and five claims, four of them opinion, and the Gödel step is an analogy rather than a proof about brains.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#t-the-self-is-a-pattern-the-brain-makes-by-watching-itself-built-from-parts-that-c
- The brain builds a picture of itself and cannot see that it is a picture, so the self feels real (Metzinger argues the brain builds a picture of itself and hides the building, because hiding it is cheaper than showing it, and whatever falls inside that picture arrives feeling like yours. The rubber-hand illusion moves the boundary in sixty to ninety seconds, and Lenggenhager, Metzinger and Blanke moved where people felt themselves to be a couple of metres across a room by filming a back being stroked and showing it ahead. Thompson stands against the conclusion twice: every illusion is a construction but not every construction is an illusion, and the no-self result holds only if a self must be single and unbuilt.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#t-the-brain-builds-a-picture-of-itself-and-cannot-see-that-it-is-a-picture-so-the-
- Good judgement depends on whether the field gives feedback, not on credentials or years of experience (Tetlock scored 284 professionals on some 28,000 dated predictions and found the average no better than chance, with credentials, access and politics separating nobody. What did separate them was how they thought, and his best forecasters extended their lead in the tournament's second and third years, so accuracy where feedback exists is a skill rather than a run of luck. Klein, following Shanteau, lists what turns years into expertise, namely a steady field that gives feedback and repeats often enough. The limits are real. The tournament's questions resolve within months, accuracy decayed towards chance three to five years out, and it shows nothing about rare disasters.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#t-good-judgement-depends-on-whether-the-field-gives-feedback-not-on-credentials-or
- An editor's choice of how to read a scripture decides what the scripture is taken to claim (Easwaran presents Krishna as the Self within and the battlefield as the mind, and says openly that this is his choice rather than the only reading; chapters 16 and 18, with their duty and social order, resist it. Shankara, a millennium earlier, applies the same kind of rule, reading each line for the job it is doing before what it plainly says, so a verse written to praise a lesser practice cannot be used to abolish a greater one. Both principles are unfalsifiable, since any awkward verse can be reclassified. Traditions that take the war as a war have read the same verses for as long, and Easwaran's only reply is to practise it and see.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#t-an-editor-s-choice-of-how-to-read-a-scripture-decides-what-the-scripture-is-take
- An outside store counts as part of your mind only under conditions most stores fail to meet (Clark and Chalmers list four conditions for counting an outside store as memory: it is there when needed, easy to get at, taken as true when retrieved, and put there by you in the first place. Otto's notebook holds what Otto wrote; the Internet, and anything else you did not fill and have never endorsed, fails the test. The list is the authors' own, offered as a way of sorting cases rather than as a criterion, with no weighting and no scale, and they weaken the fourth condition themselves. Whether the endorsement conditions are needed at all is still disputed, and one paper carries the whole case.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#t-an-outside-store-counts-as-part-of-your-mind-only-under-conditions-most-stores-f
- People do not use information just because someone puts it in front of them (Two studies sit behind this. Dennett reports that people told not to use a briefly flashed word obey when the word is shown for half a second, but at fifty milliseconds and masked they say they saw nothing and are more likely to give that very word. Buccinca and colleagues find the same thing at the screen, where people read an AI's explanation as a sign the machine knows its job rather than reading the explanation itself, which is why a better explanation does not produce a better decision. That second half is inferred from the pattern of results rather than observed, and a 2023 study found explanations do cut over-reliance where checking is cheaper than deferring.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#t-people-do-not-use-information-just-because-someone-puts-it-in-front-of-them
- An accurate answer is still useless when the thing measured is not the thing the decision needs (Narayanan and Kapoor's 1997 pneumonia model found that asthma lowered the risk of death, because asthmatics with pneumonia were rushed to intensive care, and acting on it would have sent them home. Optum's health model predicted how much a patient would cost rather than how ill they were, so equally ill Black patients were enrolled less often. Kalai makes the same point about calibration, since a model announcing one chance in 365 that a birthday falls on 7 March is perfectly calibrated and tells you nothing you can act on. The Buddha's refusal of ten questions is the oldest version, though it is a stated moral rather than a measurement, as is the calibration claim.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#t-an-accurate-answer-is-still-useless-when-the-thing-measured-is-not-the-thing-the
- The role you give a system and the style it answers in change its output and your judgement (Mollick says telling a model what kind of person to be is part of the instruction, not decoration. Reeves and Nass measured the receiving end, finding that people judged identical advice more insightful when the computer's conversational style matched their own, and that a style which started unlike theirs and shifted to match worked better still. Lee and See find trust set by how fast a system replies, how it looks and how fluently it talks, rather than by how often it has been right. Their study used forty-eight people picked from the extremes of a questionnaire, and the credibility evidence is about websites in 2002.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#t-the-role-you-give-a-system-and-the-style-it-answers-in-change-its-output-and-you
- People push work out of their heads when it feels hard, not when it is, and the world holds it (Risko and Gilbert's review is the main source. What makes someone do a task with a tool or the body instead of the head is their judgement of how hard it is, not the actual demand. Asked to remember two items they could already hold perfectly, people still wrote them down on about 40 per cent of trials, and wrongly believed it would raise their scores. How often people set reminders tracks how confident they feel about their memory rather than how good it is. Norman adds the other half, that fewer than half of American students can pick the real penny from drawings and nobody's spending suffers. The saving-and-forgetting result inside the review has replicated unevenly.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#t-people-push-work-out-of-their-heads-when-it-feels-hard-not-when-it-is-and-the-wo
- How a person or a model handles not knowing follows the scoring rule, not anything inside them (Kalai's argument is arithmetic. Take a model that never asserts a falsehood, replace each admission of ignorance with its best guess, and the second scores higher on every test that awards a point for a right answer and nothing else. Nine of the ten evaluations the field actually reads do exactly that. Sharma found the same pressure inside the feedback, where the model used to score answers during training chose a convincing falsehood over a plain correction 95 per cent of the time, and the human raters drifted the same way as questions got harder. Tetlock is the human case, with no rule written down at all. The GPT-4 calibration evidence is one figure from one system card.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#t-how-a-person-or-a-model-handles-not-knowing-follows-the-scoring-rule-not-anythin
- A living thing works out what it senses and then treats its own answer as a fact about the world (An organism does not read properties off the world. It computes an answer and then treats that answer as a property of what it sensed. Aguera y Arcas shows a bacterium working out concentration as an average over separate molecules arriving at its receptors, with the length of the averaging window the thing it has to get right, and pain tracking the brain's guess about damage rather than the damage. Dennett adds that there is no sweetness in glucose, only properties that provoke a response, and the response is read back into the sugar. Three evidence claims from two sources with none against, but the range runs only from a bacterium to a taste.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#t-a-living-thing-works-out-what-it-senses-and-then-treats-its-own-answer-as-a-fact
- What feels warm and yours counts as part of you, so belongings come in and old selves drop out (James puts the edge of a self wherever feeling reaches. A man's clothes and property are counted in, he has one social self for every group whose opinion matters to him, and a past self is his only where warmth and continuity still reach. The evidence is Reverend Ansel Bourne, who drew money in Providence on 17 January 1887 and vanished, then on 14 March woke in Norristown as a shopkeeper of six weeks trading as A. J. Brown and would not believe two months had passed. One source, four claims, three of them opinion, and a single dissociation case carries the weight.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#t-what-feels-warm-and-yours-counts-as-part-of-you-so-belongings-come-in-and-old-se
- A few dozen paid raters and whoever wrote the web set how an assistant talks (Ouyang's paper puts a number on the first population: about forty screened contractors, agreeing with one another only about three-quarters of the time, alongside the researchers who wrote their instructions, the customers whose prompts were used, and a waitlist seeded by employees. Bender and colleagues supply the second: text scraped from the web narrows the population at every step of collection, and a model keeps the words in use at the moment its data was frozen. The corpus figures are from 2021, the demographic survey covers nineteen people and is self-reported, and half these claims are argument rather than measurement.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#t-a-few-dozen-paid-raters-and-whoever-wrote-the-web-set-how-an-assistant-talks
- How right an answer feels depends on how easily it came to mind, not on the evidence (Kahneman argues that confidence tracks how neatly the story hangs together rather than how good the evidence is, and participants who heard one side of a legal case, knowing it was one side, were surer than those who heard both. Anything that makes a sentence easier to take in, such as repetition, a clear font or a rhyme, makes it feel truer, and afterwards you cannot tell which of those produced the feeling. More than half the students at Harvard, MIT and Princeton gave the ten-cent answer to the bat-and-ball problem, and printing it in washed-out grey cut the errors. Make It Stick adds that learners judge learning by how easy the practice felt.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#t-how-right-an-answer-feels-depends-on-how-easily-it-came-to-mind-not-on-the-evide
- How much a person suffers depends on how they see it, not on the size of what happened (Frankl says suffering behaves like a gas, filling whatever space it is given, so a small trouble can take up as much of a person as a great one. His second observation runs the same way: numbness protected prisoners rather than damaging them, and what still reached a man through it was not physical pain but being treated unjustly, the blow in the bread line hurting less than its unreasonableness. Both come from one observer recording his own reactions in the camps, with nothing measured. The comparison also undoes itself, since if size is entirely relative then no suffering can be measured against another, including the comparisons the book invites.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#t-how-much-a-person-suffers-depends-on-how-they-see-it-not-on-the-size-of-what-hap
- Finding someone to blame ends the inquiry that would have prevented the next failure (Naming a culprit answers the question the investigation was asking, so the asking stops before it reaches the conditions that produced the failure. Norman's case is the 2010 F-22 crash, where the Inspector General raised oxygen deprivation and the Air Force restated pilot error. Edmondson shows the size of the habit: managers say one to four per cent of their organisation's failures are truly blameworthy, and that seventy to ninety per cent get treated that way. None of the four claims counts as evidence, and Edmondson's figures come from polling her own audiences rather than from records. Norman adds that asking why implies one cause where complex events have many.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#t-finding-someone-to-blame-ends-the-inquiry-that-would-have-prevented-the-next-fai
- You cannot tell whether someone checked from what they looked at or what they produced (Duley laid the automated engine display over the manual tracking task, so that every look at the tracking task also fell on the automated one, and tracking stayed as good as before while the rate of missed malfunctions did too. What the operator withdraws is attention, not gaze. In the same review about 43 per cent of operators missed a first wrong diagnosis, and half of those had looked at every reading and spent no extra time on the one that did not fit. Lee's authors make the other half of the argument, that an unchanged output may be the result of a careful decision that nothing needed changing. Half of these claims are argument rather than measurement.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#t-you-cannot-tell-whether-someone-checked-from-what-they-looked-at-or-what-they-pr
- A tool weakens the skill it replaces while the person's own estimate of that skill stays put (Risko and Gilbert's model has two arrows, one from offloading to the skill and one from offloading to the judgement of the skill, so reliance grows with nothing in the person's own report registering the loss. Turn-by-turn navigation makes the journey better and the driver worse. People who searched online about one subject credited themselves with more knowledge of a different subject, a transfer that only an inflated self-estimate explains. Shen and Tamkin found the group using an AI assistant fell furthest behind on debugging questions, which is the fault-finding that checking a tool needs. That breakdown was exploratory rather than planned, and two of the four claims are contested.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#t-a-tool-weakens-the-skill-it-replaces-while-the-person-s-own-estimate-of-that-ski
- The texts tell you to watch how a state comes and goes rather than remove it, and watching removes it (The instruction is to know how something arises and passes, and the removal follows from the knowing rather than being asked for. The Satipatthana Sutta tells you to know a state rather than get rid of it, treats a restless mind as the material, has you watch other people too, and adds five instructions in its refrain that the exercises never give, including putting aside wanting and resisting. Gaudapada's rope is the same shape, since not seeing the rope is the whole of the snake mistake. In the Panchadasi the tenth man stops weeping the instant he is told, though the cut he made still takes a month. Seven opinion claims, three sources, nothing measured.)
