Edmondson's study of neonatal teams at twenty-three hospitals shows the mechanism: how safe people felt predicted how much they asked and worked things out together, and had no relationship at all with how much they read on their own. Her better-performing hospital units reported more errors, not fewer. At Rustenburg mine, where explaining had produced silence, a change to open questions came alongside a fall in deaths from forty-four in 2006 to seventeen in 2011. Much of this literature is cross-sectional, and many things changed at Rustenburg at once.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#t-how-safe-people-feel-to-speak-up-is-a-team-trait-and-decides-whether-what-they-k
- Automating part of a job makes the rest worth more only where demand grows and entry stays hard (A job is a bundle of tasks, so making the machine's tasks cheap can raise the price of those left to a person, but only under conditions. Autor names three: the worker supplies the remaining task, others cannot easily enter it, and demand for the output grows as it gets cheaper. His case is the cash machine, which rose from about 100,000 to 400,000 in America between 1995 and 2010 while bank tellers rose from about 500,000 to 550,000. His own wage series is the counter-case, and the point is contested: at the bottom of the scale real wages fell after 1999 even as those jobs grew.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#t-automating-part-of-a-job-makes-the-rest-worth-more-only-where-demand-grows-and-e
- Smooth output tells you nothing about what a model holds inside or how it got there (Anthropic's circuit tracing found a model that writes one word at a time settling on the rhyming word before it starts the line, and running through steps that never appear in the answer, where replacing one of those steps changes what it says. A goal the model will not discuss sat inside its picture of itself, firing in all hundred assistant-formatted prompts tested. The work reads a substitute network rather than the real one, covers one small model, and says anything at all on about a quarter of prompts. Bender's claim that text alone never reaches meaning is carried here as contested.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#t-smooth-output-tells-you-nothing-about-what-a-model-holds-inside-or-how-it-got-th
- Whether someone checks a machine depends on trusting it against trusting themselves, not on how good it is (Lee and See proposed it, that whether someone checks a machine's output depends on how their trust in the machine compares with their confidence in doing the job themselves. Lee's 2025 survey measured it. Across 936 tasks reported by 319 knowledge workers, confidence that the tool could do that task was the largest predictor of not checking, while confidence in doing the task oneself and in judging the output ran the other way. Nothing else predicted it, not task type, age, gender, occupation or general trust in AI. It is a cross-sectional survey of self-reports, so it establishes no causation, and the sample was English-only and skewed young.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#t-whether-someone-checks-a-machine-depends-on-trusting-it-against-trusting-themsel
- Smooth machine writing harms people even when nothing goes wrong, and they have no remedy (Bender and her co-authors argue that the damage comes from text which reads smoothly while nobody answers for it. Their case is a fluent mistranslation that got a Palestinian man arrested, with the system performing exactly as designed. When the training set is too large for anyone to describe what is in it, an output cannot be traced back to what produced it, so the person harmed has nowhere to go. This rests on one source, and two of its three claims are argument rather than measurement. Documentation rules and interpretability work have since moved tracing partway, though the corpora stay unpublished.) Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/framework/#t-smooth-machine-writing-harms-people-even-when-nothing-goes-wrong-and-they-have-n

## Claims
- An automatic reaction to a face changes with the question asked: Sapolsky reports that the same face photograph sets off a response in the amygdala (a brain alarm area), a bigger one, or none at all, depending on which question the viewer was asked about it thirty seconds earlier. Automatic does not mean unavoidable. [evidence; from Behave] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-an-automatic-reaction-to-a-face-changes-with-the-question-asked
- The Gita says all work carries fault so faultless work is impossible: The Bhagavad Gita says every undertaking carries some fault, as fire carries smoke. Since faultless work is not on offer, the only real comparison is your own work done badly against someone else's done well — and your own wins. [opinion; from भगवद्गीता · The Bhagavad Gita] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-gita-says-all-work-carries-fault-so-faultless-work-is-impossible
- Switching to a method that halves your errors does not feel different: Epley found that people who switched to the method that halved their errors in reading another person felt no more confident than before. Confidence therefore cannot tell you which of two methods is working. [evidence; from Mindwise] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-switching-to-a-method-that-halves-your-errors-does-not-feel-different
- Anthropic's scoring model preferred a convincing falsehood to a plain correction: The model used to score answers during training chose a convincing but false reply over a plain correction 95 per cent of the time, and over a helpful correction 45 per cent of the time on the hardest misconceptions. [evidence; from Towards Understanding Sycophancy in Language Models] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-anthropic-s-scoring-model-preferred-a-convincing-falsehood-to-a-plain-correction
- An aid that hides its inputs makes under-checking impossible to measure: Saying an operator checked too little requires knowing what a full check would have been. That is knowable only where he can list and inspect every reading the aid used; where the aid does not expose them, failing to check and being unable to check cannot be told apart. [opinion; from Complacency and Bias in Human Use of Automation] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-an-aid-that-hides-its-inputs-makes-under-checking-impossible-to-measure
- Seth says mistaking AI for minds makes us think less of ourselves: Seth argues the nearest harm of confusing AI with conscious minds falls on us, not on the machines. We build them in our own image, then read ourselves back as machines, overrating what they do and underrating what we do. [opinion; from The Mythology of Conscious AI] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-seth-says-mistaking-ai-for-minds-makes-us-think-less-of-ourselves
- Counting wrong answers hides why a person agreed with the group: Asch found three different reasons for going along with the group and three for holding out, and counting a person's wrong answers cannot tell them apart. Someone who thinks the majority is right but reports what he sees scores the same as someone untroubled. [opinion; from Studies of Independence and Conformity] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-counting-wrong-answers-hides-why-a-person-agreed-with-the-group
- Minsky says an inner watcher would need a watcher of its own: Putting a single ruler inside the head explains nothing: give it an inner screen to watch and it needs a self to watch that screen, without end. A thing with no parts supplies no pieces to explain anything with. [opinion; from The Society of Mind] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-minsky-says-an-inner-watcher-would-need-a-watcher-of-its-own
- People who enjoy thinking behave differently but only a little: People who score high on enjoying hard thinking do behave differently from people who score low, but the differences are small: about a fifth to a third of a standard deviation. [evidence; from Dispositional Differences in Cognitive Motivation] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-people-who-enjoy-thinking-behave-differently-but-only-a-little
- Just beyond AI's range the same tool made consultants wrong more often: On a case built to fall just outside what the model handles well, 373 consultants got it right 84.4% of the time without the model, 70.6% with it, and 60.0% with it plus prompt training. [evidence; from The Jagged Technological Frontier] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-just-beyond-ai-s-range-the-same-tool-made-consultants-wrong-more-often
- Shankara says sorrow comes from one false belief about what is mine: Shankara says all sorrow and confusion grow from a single false belief — I belong to these people and things, and they belong to me — and that nothing removes it except knowing the Self. [opinion; from श्रीमद्भगवद्गीता शाङ्करभाष्यम् · The Gita with Shankara's Commentary] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-shankara-says-sorrow-comes-from-one-false-belief-about-what-is-mine
- Grove says managers should teach their own people, not hire trainers: Andy Grove argues that a manager should run the training himself instead of hiring a trainer. Only someone the team sees as doing the work day to day can tie the lessons to how the job is actually done. [opinion; from High Output Management] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-grove-says-managers-should-teach-their-own-people-not-hire-trainers
- The effort moved from producing the work to verifying and steering it: Lee's workers described three displacements, not a saving: gathering information became verifying it (111 faster, 56 checking), solving a problem became fitting the answer in (77 tailored, 19 making it usable), and doing a task became overseeing one (129 automating, 48 steering a drifting response). [evidence; from The Impact of Generative AI on Critical Thinking] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-effort-moved-from-producing-the-work-to-verifying-and-steering-it
- Developers' estimates of AI's effect on their speed get the direction wrong: The same developers predicted AI would make them 24 per cent faster, and said afterwards it had made them 20 per cent faster. Measured, they were 19 per cent slower. Months of using the tool did not shrink the error. [evidence; from Measuring the Impact of Early-2025 AI on Experienced Open-Source Developer Productivity] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-developers-estimates-of-ai-s-effect-on-their-speed-get-the-direction-wrong
- We sense ourselves in order to control ourselves, not to be accurate: Seth argues that we perceive our own bodies in order to regulate them, not in order to know them truly. A model built for control can be wrong about the body and still do its job well. [opinion; from Being You] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-we-sense-ourselves-in-order-to-control-ourselves-not-to-be-accurate
- Not everyone has the same room to reshape their job: Money worries, the standing of the job and the rules of the workplace decide how much room a person has to reshape the work they do. So the chance to craft a job is not equally available, and not crafting says nothing about the person. [opinion; from Crafting a Job] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-not-everyone-has-the-same-room-to-reshape-their-job
- The essay's own ending admits it never reaches felt experience: The bridge runs one way only. It carries you from Shannon information to a self with its own world of meaning (an umwelt), and stops before the felt character of awareness that the authors themselves named as the sticking point. [opinion; from Consciousness Across Three Worldviews] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-essay-s-own-ending-admits-it-never-reaches-felt-experience
- The common middle view of free will needs a little person inside: Almost everyone holds that biology accounts for some behaviour while something else stays in charge of the rest. Sapolsky argues that this cannot be stated without a little person inside the head who stands outside the causes. [opinion; from Behave] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-common-middle-view-of-free-will-needs-a-little-person-inside
- Easwaran's reading of the Gita as inner allegory is one choice: Easwaran presents Krishna as the Self within and the battlefield as the mind. That is his editorial choice, not the only way the text can be read. [contested; from भगवद्गीता · The Bhagavad Gita] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-easwaran-s-reading-of-the-gita-as-inner-allegory-is-one-choice
- Learners taught the solution first beat those left to work it out: Sweller holds that learners who are taught the solution before practising do better than those left to work it out. Almost everything in long-term memory is copied from other people, not discovered. [contested; from Cognitive Architecture and Instructional Design: 20 Years Later] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-learners-taught-the-solution-first-beat-those-left-to-work-it-out
- Vivekananda says caring about something, not seeing it, leaves the mark: Vivekananda argues that what leaves a mark on a person is attachment, not perception. Of the hundreds of faces you see in a day only the face you love stays with you, though every one of them reached your eyes alike. [opinion; from Karma-Yoga] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-vivekananda-says-caring-about-something-not-seeing-it-leaves-the-mark
- Everyday life rarely tells poor performers that they are poor performers: Kruger and Dunning argue that ordinary life does not correct a poor performer's inflated self-view. People hold back bad news, most tasks give no clear right answer, and learning from better performers is exactly what the skill deficit prevents. [opinion; from Unskilled and Unaware of It] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-everyday-life-rarely-tells-poor-performers-that-they-are-poor-performers
- All three ways of withholding the AI's answer worked equally well: Bucinca and colleagues tested three ways of making people think before they saw the AI's suggestion: hiding it behind a button, asking for the person's own decision first, and a thirty-second delay. None worked better than the others. [evidence; from To Trust or to Think] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-all-three-ways-of-withholding-the-ai-s-answer-worked-equally-well
- Thompson says the no-self argument depends on how you define self: Thompson argues the no-self conclusion holds only if a self means a single, separate thing not built from experience. Define it instead as built over time and socially, as James did in 1890 and Mead in 1934, and the same evidence proves far less. [opinion; from Why I Am Not a Buddhist] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-thompson-says-the-no-self-argument-depends-on-how-you-define-self
- How closely to supervise depends on the person's experience at that task: Grove says how closely a manager should supervise is set by how experienced the person is at that particular task, not by what the manager prefers. None of the three styles is kinder than the others. [contested; from High Output Management] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-how-closely-to-supervise-depends-on-the-person-s-experience-at-that-task
- Three things make people treat an object as having a mind: Waytz, Cacioppo and Epley say people treat a thing as having a mind when human ideas are the nearest thing they have for explaining it, when its behaviour needs explaining, and when they want company. [opinion; from Who Sees Human?] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-three-things-make-people-treat-an-object-as-having-a-mind
- Narayanan and Kapoor say content fights are policy disputes, not AI errors: Narayanan and Kapoor argue that when people disagree about where a moderation rule should fall, that is a policy dispute, not a mistake in sorting. No model can settle it. Facebook removed the napalm-girl photograph repeatedly because people had decided it was unacceptable. [opinion; from AI Snake Oil] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-narayanan-and-kapoor-say-content-fights-are-policy-disputes-not-ai-errors
- Working memory is tiny for new material, vast for familiar material: Sweller argues that the mind can hold only a few new items at once, but can handle an effectively unlimited amount of material it already knows and is pulling back from long-term memory. [evidence; from Cognitive Architecture and Instructional Design: 20 Years Later] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-working-memory-is-tiny-for-new-material-vast-for-familiar-material
- Hagendorff says watching what a model does is a real explanation: Hagendorff argues that studying what a model does when you use it is a proper way to explain it, because its outputs cannot be predicted from what is known about its weights. For a closed commercial model it is the only way open to outsiders. [opinion; from Machine Psychology] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-hagendorff-says-watching-what-a-model-does-is-a-real-explanation
- An unedited output can be the result of a careful judgement: Lee's authors argue that how varied a group's finished work is cannot measure how much they thought: a worker who uses an output unchanged may have decided carefully that it needed no change, and the artefact cannot tell them from one who never looked. [opinion; from The Impact of Generative AI on Critical Thinking] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-an-unedited-output-can-be-the-result-of-a-careful-judgement
- A model can learn a deadly rule that its answers never reveal: A model can learn a rule that kills people while every output you check looks fine. Caruana's pneumonia model learned that asthma patients were low risk, which was true in the data only because they were sent straight to intensive care. [evidence; from The Alignment Problem] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-a-model-can-learn-a-deadly-rule-that-its-answers-never-reveal
- ACT works but its account of why rests on a doubtful questionnaire: The weakest part of acceptance and commitment therapy is its explanation of why it works. The questionnaire used to show that a person's relation to pain is separate from how much pain there is may simply be measuring how bad they feel. [contested; from Get Out of Your Mind and Into Your Life] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-act-works-but-its-account-of-why-rests-on-a-doubtful-questionnaire
- A scoring rule with no credit for I don't know selects guessers: A scoring rule that pays nothing for saying "I don't know" will select, from any population of candidates, the ones most willing to make something up. Nothing in the argument is about language models; it holds wherever answers are scored one point for right and none for anything else. [opinion; from Why Language Models Hallucinate] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-a-scoring-rule-with-no-credit-for-i-don-t-know-selects-guessers
- Nobody can watch a quiet display for more than half an hour: Bainbridge argues that a person cannot hold useful attention on a display where almost nothing happens for longer than about half an hour. Watching for rare faults is therefore a job for an alarm, not for a human. [evidence; from Ironies of Automation] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-nobody-can-watch-a-quiet-display-for-more-than-half-an-hour
- AI helps the weakest workers most, which could make skill worth less: On tasks AI does well, it raises everyone's performance and the worst performers gain the most. If that holds, being skilled is worth less than it was. [contested; from Co-Intelligence] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-ai-helps-the-weakest-workers-most-which-could-make-skill-worth-less
- GPT-3 shows three of prospect theory's six effects and not the others: Tested on the contrasts Kahneman and Tversky used, GPT-3 showed three of prospect theory's six effects: framing, the certainty effect and the overweighting of small probabilities. The reflection effect, the isolation effect and magnitude perception did not appear. [evidence; from Using Cognitive Psychology to Understand GPT-3] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-gpt-3-shows-three-of-prospect-theory-s-six-effects-and-not-the-others
- Chatterjee says letting go of being the doer can be trained: Chatterjee holds that the sense of being the one who acts can be loosened by regular reflection. The sign of success is not working less hard but treating people you like, dislike and feel nothing for the same way. [opinion; from Timeless Leadership] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-chatterjee-says-letting-go-of-being-the-doer-can-be-trained
- Shankara says action prepares the mind but cannot bring liberation: Shankara holds that action cleans the mind and so makes a person ready for knowledge, but it can never produce liberation, because liberation is not something made and no action can manufacture a state that is eternal. [opinion; from श्रीमद्भगवद्गीता शाङ्करभाष्यम् · The Gita with Shankara's Commentary] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-shankara-says-action-prepares-the-mind-but-cannot-bring-liberation
- Attention's cost was trivial in 2017 and is now the main limit: Attention's cost grows with the square of the sentence length. At the few dozen tokens the 2017 paper measured, that was cheaper than the alternatives; at every length used since it has been the binding limit, though nothing about the design changed. [evidence; from Attention Is All You Need] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-attention-s-cost-was-trivial-in-2017-and-is-now-the-main-limit
- The world is not the obstacle and hating it is a mistake: Verse 4.41 says the duality the Lord made does not obstruct, it helps, and it cannot be got rid of — so let it stand, and why should anyone hate it. What a person has to give up is his own second creation, the wanting and the aversion he added. [opinion; from पञ्चदशी · Pañcadaśī] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-world-is-not-the-obstacle-and-hating-it-is-a-mistake
- A machine unsure of your goal asks first and accepts being stopped: Hadfield-Menell and colleagues proved that a machine which is unsure what its user wants will check before acting and will allow itself to be switched off. Make it confident about the goal and it stops listening. [evidence; from The Alignment Problem] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-a-machine-unsure-of-your-goal-asks-first-and-accepts-being-stopped
- Every pilot shut down the engine on a single unsupported fire warning: In a full simulator study a false engine fire warning appeared with nothing on the flight deck to support it, and every pilot shut the engine down. In debriefing the same pilots said the message alone would not justify it, and two thirds recalled a confirming indication that had never been there. [evidence; from Complacency and Bias in Human Use of Automation] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-every-pilot-shut-down-the-engine-on-a-single-unsupported-fire-warning
- The Gita gives you a right to your work, not its results: In verse 2.47 the Bhagavad Gita says a person has a right to the action itself and never to what the action produces. Verse 2.48 adds that yoga means staying even in success and failure. [opinion; from भगवद्गीता · The Bhagavad Gita] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-gita-gives-you-a-right-to-your-work-not-its-results
- Tetlock's forecasting tournament says nothing about rare disasters: Tetlock's tournament scored questions that resolve within months or a few years. It shows nothing about rare catastrophes, because scoring forecasts of those would take decades or thousands of years. [opinion; from Superforecasting] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-tetlock-s-forecasting-tournament-says-nothing-about-rare-disasters
- Shankara puts pleasure and pain among the things seen, not the seer: Shankara holds that pleasure, pain, confusion and desire belong to what is observed, not to the self that observes. No rule separates the states one would keep for the self from ones like old age and death. [opinion; from श्रीमद्भगवद्गीता शाङ्करभाष्यम् · The Gita with Shankara's Commentary] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-shankara-puts-pleasure-and-pain-among-the-things-seen-not-the-seer
- A weaker tool you can check may beat a stronger one: Where results depend on the person relying on the tool at the right moments, a simpler and less capable system can be worth more than a complex, better-performing one. [opinion; from Trust in Automation: Designing for Appropriate Reliance] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-a-weaker-tool-you-can-check-may-beat-a-stronger-one
- Copying an expert fails because experts never demonstrate getting out of trouble: A system that learns by copying an expert has no examples of how to recover from trouble, because the expert never got into it. Ross and Bagnell showed that its mistakes grow with the square of how long it runs. [evidence; from The Alignment Problem] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-copying-an-expert-fails-because-experts-never-demonstrate-getting-out-of-trouble
- Liking to think only shows when the situation is moderately demanding: The difference between people who enjoy thinking and people who do not (need for cognition) shows up only when a situation makes middling demands. When nothing is at stake nobody thinks hard; when everything is, everybody does. [evidence; from Dispositional Differences in Cognitive Motivation] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-liking-to-think-only-shows-when-the-situation-is-moderately-demanding
- People follow social rules with machines without thinking they are people: People apply ordinary social rules, such as politeness and taking sides, to computers and television automatically, on the slightest cue, without believing for a moment that the machine is a person. [evidence; from The Media Equation] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-people-follow-social-rules-with-machines-without-thinking-they-are-people
- Open questions get people talking where explanations produced silence: Edmondson finds that a specific question people cannot answer with yes or no brings out information that an explanation does not. At Rustenburg mine, where explaining had produced silence, deaths fell from forty-four in 2006 to seventeen in 2011. [evidence; from The Fearless Organization] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-open-questions-get-people-talking-where-explanations-produced-silence
- Underwriters pricing the same risk differed by 55 per cent: Two underwriters at the same insurer, pricing the same case file, differed by a median of 55 per cent. Their executives had predicted 10 per cent: against a premium of $9,500, not $10,500 but $16,700. [evidence; from Noise] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-underwriters-pricing-the-same-risk-differed-by-55-per-cent
- Machines got into work nobody can explain by two routes: Machines entered driving, legal document review and field labour without acquiring the understanding people use there. Either the setting was regularised until an inflexible machine could cope, or the rule nobody can state was inferred from labelled examples. [opinion; from Why Are There Still So Many Jobs?] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-machines-got-into-work-nobody-can-explain-by-two-routes
- Damasio's patients understood upsetting pictures and felt nothing at all: A person can understand what a situation means, name the emotion it should produce, and have no bodily reaction to it at all — knowing without feeling. [evidence; from Descartes' Error] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-damasio-s-patients-understood-upsetting-pictures-and-felt-nothing-at-all
- The AI assistant hurt understanding and saved no time at all: In Shen and Tamkin's study the assistant left people understanding the task less well, and it did not make them any faster: total time did not differ between the assisted and unassisted groups (p = 0.391). [evidence; from How AI Impacts Skill Formation] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-ai-assistant-hurt-understanding-and-saved-no-time-at-all
- A past self is yours only where warmth and continuity reach: James says a past self is yours only when it comes back with warmth and resemblance or continuity links it to now. Where they stop, ownership stops: anecdotes of your own infancy raise no blush and no pride, the child as foreign as a stranger's. [opinion; from The Consciousness of Self] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-a-past-self-is-yours-only-where-warmth-and-continuity-reach
- Organisations develop managers on purpose and designers not at all: Brooks argues that organisations recruit and develop managers on purpose while doing nothing of the kind for designers, even though the quality of the people doing the designing is the single largest factor in whether a system succeeds. [opinion; from The Mythical Man-Month] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-organisations-develop-managers-on-purpose-and-designers-not-at-all
- Skills fade when unused and grow only through practice with feedback: Bainbridge argues that what you know fades when you stop using it, because recall depends on how often you use it, and it grows only through use plus feedback. Teaching an operator without letting them practise leaves someone who neither understands nor remembers. [evidence; from Ironies of Automation] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-skills-fade-when-unused-and-grow-only-through-practice-with-feedback
- Shankara says only those who do not yet know have duties: On Shankara's reading, rites and duties are laid down only for people who have not yet realised the self. Once a person knows, there is no duty left for him to perform. [opinion; from श्रीमद्भगवद्गीता शाङ्करभाष्यम् · The Gita with Shankara's Commentary] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-shankara-says-only-those-who-do-not-yet-know-have-duties
- The self is five separate parts, each able to break alone: Seth argues the self is not one perceiver but five things built separately: owning a body, having a point of view, willing, holding a life story, and being a social person. Each can fail while the others keep working. [evidence; from Being You] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-self-is-five-separate-parts-each-able-to-break-alone
- Sweller found teaching aids that help beginners start to hurt experts: Worked examples and other teaching support that help a beginner become unnecessary as the learner's knowledge grows, and then start to hurt performance — an effect called expertise reversal. [evidence; from Cognitive Architecture and Instructional Design: 20 Years Later] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-sweller-found-teaching-aids-that-help-beginners-start-to-hurt-experts
- A model can work backwards from an answer the user gave it: When a user hands the model an answer it cannot compute itself, Anthropic's researchers found the model works backwards from that answer to build its written reasoning. The result reads exactly like reasoning done honestly forwards. [evidence; from On the Biology of a Large Language Model] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-a-model-can-work-backwards-from-an-answer-the-user-gave-it
- Vaccaro's analysis shows the chosen comparison decides whether AI looks useful: The same experiments that make human-AI teams look worse than the better party alone show a large gain (g = 0.64) over the person working alone. Which comparison you pick decides whether the tool counts as a success. [evidence; from When Combinations of Humans and AI Are Useful] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-vaccaro-s-analysis-shows-the-chosen-comparison-decides-whether-ai-looks-useful
- Ericsson says hard practice with feedback builds skill, not years spent: Skill is built and kept up by practice that is hard, aimed just past what you can already do, and followed by feedback. Years spent near the work do not do it. [contested; from Peak] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-ericsson-says-hard-practice-with-feedback-builds-skill-not-years-spent
- The transformer was built to make training faster not smarter: In a recurrent network each position has to be computed after the one before it, so a single training example cannot be split across processors. The transformer was designed to remove that limit, and its headline result was training about ten times cheaper. [evidence; from Attention Is All You Need] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-transformer-was-built-to-make-training-faster-not-smarter
- A chess master's memory advantage disappears on a randomly arranged board: Ericsson argues the mental patterns that make someone an expert work only on what they trained on. Faloon's memory system for digits did nothing for letters, and a chess master's advantage vanishes on a board arranged at random. [evidence; from Peak] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-a-chess-master-s-memory-advantage-disappears-on-a-randomly-arranged-board
- Rahula rests the denial of a self on one changed word: Two Dhammapada lines say all conditioned things (samkhara) are impermanent and are dukkha; the third changes the word: no dhamma at all is a self. Since dhamma covers the unconditioned too, no region is left for a self. [contested; from What the Buddha Taught] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-rahula-rests-the-denial-of-a-self-on-one-changed-word
- Sarvapriyananda argues information matters only when it belongs to someone: Information that is merely present and information that belongs to someone are two different things, and only the second has any effect on the system holding it. The DNA of a live bacterium and of a dead one are identical as information. [opinion; from Consciousness Across Three Worldviews] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-sarvapriyananda-argues-information-matters-only-when-it-belongs-to-someone
- Nothing punishes inattention while the machine works, so it grows: Because automation is usually reliable, watching it less usually costs nothing, and the absence of a cost makes the operator watch less still. The loop runs the other way only when a failure is experienced: operators who met rare failures in training sampled the aid more than operators merely told it might fail. [evidence; from Complacency and Bias in Human Use of Automation] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-nothing-punishes-inattention-while-the-machine-works-so-it-grows
- When every team leader agrees the schedule is fine, they are bluffing: Weinberg argues that when a group reports everyone is on schedule, it is managing how it looks rather than reporting the work. One person admitting they are behind releases the rest to admit it too. [evidence; from The Psychology of Computer Programming] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-when-every-team-leader-agrees-the-schedule-is-fine-they-are-bluffing
- The students who used models most may have been struggling already: Jošt's correlations have no control group and no random assignment, so the reverse reading — that the students who reached for a model most were the ones already behind — fits the data as well as the authors' reading does. Nobody checked prior marks against model use. [contested; from Language Models in a Programming Course] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-students-who-used-models-most-may-have-been-struggling-already
- The Ashtavakra Gita defines bondage as the mind wanting or refusing: The Ashtavakra Gita says bondage is simply the mind wanting something or pushing something away, and freedom is the mind doing neither. Neither one is a condition of the world or a rank you reach after years of effort. [opinion; from अष्टावक्रगीता · Aṣṭāvakra Gītā] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-ashtavakra-gita-defines-bondage-as-the-mind-wanting-or-refusing
- Feedback that confirms a wrong hunch is worse than no feedback: Kahneman and Klein argue that an environment whose feedback confirms the wrong hunch is more dangerous than one that is unpredictable. Hogarth's example is the physician who felt which patients would get typhoid and spread it by examining their tongues without washing his hands. [evidence; from Conditions for Intuitive Expertise] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-feedback-that-confirms-a-wrong-hunch-is-worse-than-no-feedback
- Frankl says small troubles can hurt as much as great ones: Frankl says suffering behaves like a gas: a small amount and a large amount each fill the whole space available. So the size of a person's suffering is entirely relative, and a small thing can bring the greatest joy. [opinion; from Experiences in a Concentration Camp] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-frankl-says-small-troubles-can-hurt-as-much-as-great-ones
- Dahmani and Bohbot blame instructions that leave nothing to decide: What costs a driver their sense of a place is not that the device competes for attention but that a turn-by-turn instruction leaves no decision to make. An aid that gives bearing and distance and lets the user pick the turns should cost less. [opinion; from GPS and the Cognitive Map] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-dahmani-and-bohbot-blame-instructions-that-leave-nothing-to-decide
- What you ask after the code arrives decides what you learn: In Shen and Tamkin's study the two people who asked the assistant to generate code and then questioned it scored 86 per cent, against 39 for those who just took the code. The request was the same; the questions afterwards were not. [contested; from How AI Impacts Skill Formation] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-what-you-ask-after-the-code-arrives-decides-what-you-learn
- Seth says a simulated brain is conscious only if consciousness is computation: Simulating something creates the real thing only when that thing is itself a set of steps: a simulated calculation really calculates, but a simulated rainstorm leaves nothing wet. A simulated brain would therefore be conscious only if consciousness is computation. [opinion; from The Mythology of Conscious AI] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-seth-says-a-simulated-brain-is-conscious-only-if-consciousness-is-computation
- Enjoying hard thinking is one trait, not several separate ones: How much someone enjoys hard thinking (need for cognition) is a single trait rather than a bundle of them. The eighteen-item questionnaire measures one thing, and the one serious attempt to split it into three failed. [evidence; from Dispositional Differences in Cognitive Motivation] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-enjoying-hard-thinking-is-one-trait-not-several-separate-ones
- A proven worker needs close direction again when the job changes: How ready someone is to work unsupervised applies to one task, not to the person. When the task or the pace changes, that readiness drops, and a manager who had stepped back has to go back to close, structured direction. [opinion; from High Output Management] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-a-proven-worker-needs-close-direction-again-when-the-job-changes
- Seth says a brain has no software separate from its biology: Seth argues that a brain does not divide into software and hardware the way a computer does. A single neuron is a self-maintaining living machine, so you cannot assume a mind would run the same on any material. [contested; from The Mythology of Conscious AI] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-seth-says-a-brain-has-no-software-separate-from-its-biology
- Damasio's patients still felt penalties but could not learn to expect them: Damasio's patients had not lost their reaction to punishment; they avoided a losing deck right after a penalty just as healthy players did. What they lost was turning that penalty into an expectation, which is why knowing the rule does not restore their play. [evidence; from Descartes' Error] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-damasio-s-patients-still-felt-penalties-but-could-not-learn-to-expect-them
- Metzinger says an attention-capturing industry takes away part of being a person: Metzinger argues that being able to direct your own attention is one of the deepest parts of being a person. An industry built to capture attention is therefore taking away part of selfhood, not just time. [opinion; from The Ego Tunnel] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-metzinger-says-an-attention-capturing-industry-takes-away-part-of-being-a-person
- Vedanta's light of awareness and physics' shared information play the same role: Sarvapriyananda's lectures put Vedanta's self-luminous awareness — that which shows everything else — in the same position that relational physics gives to a field of shared information between systems. In both, “light” means making something known, not a band of the spectrum. [contested; from Consciousness Across Three Worldviews] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-vedanta-s-light-of-awareness-and-physics-shared-information-play-the-same-role
- Tetlock's forecasters revise often in small steps and dump a bad source: Tetlock found that good forecasters change their estimates often and by small amounts. The exception is when the report a forecast rests on is visibly failing, in which case they throw it out rather than nudge the number. [evidence; from Superforecasting] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-tetlock-s-forecasters-revise-often-in-small-steps-and-dump-a-bad-source
- A person who catches rare costly errors is worth keeping: Where a rare mistake costs far more than its rarity suggests, a person who catches those mistakes is worth keeping, even when the machine is more accurate on average. [opinion; from When Combinations of Humans and AI Are Useful] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-a-person-who-catches-rare-costly-errors-is-worth-keeping
- Disagreement and mixed expertise help safe teams and hurt unsafe ones: Whether a team feels safe to speak up decides which way other things cut. Conflict, mixed expertise and working apart all help teams where people feel safe, and hurt teams where they do not. [evidence; from The Fearless Organization] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-disagreement-and-mixed-expertise-help-safe-teams-and-hurt-unsafe-ones
- Assisted workers found the work easier and the test just as hard: In Shen and Tamkin's study the people who used the assistant said the task felt easier, then rated the quiz afterwards exactly as hard as everyone else did. [evidence; from How AI Impacts Skill Formation] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-assisted-workers-found-the-work-easier-and-the-test-just-as-hard
- People survive longer when someone or something outside them needs them: Frankl argues that people endure more when something outside themselves is waiting on them: a person who needs them, or work only they can finish. Two prisoners who meant to kill themselves were turned back this way. [evidence; from Experiences in a Concentration Camp] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-people-survive-longer-when-someone-or-something-outside-them-needs-them
- In 2022 every big AI model was too large for its data: Hoffmann's team found that in 2022 every large language model was too big for the amount of text it was trained on. Labs had kept the data size roughly fixed since GPT-3 only because they were copying each other. [evidence; from Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-in-2022-every-big-ai-model-was-too-large-for-its-data
- The aim is trusting a tool as much as it deserves: Lee and See argue the goal is to trust a machine exactly as much as it can deliver, not to trust it more. Trusting too much leads to misuse and trusting too little leads to refusing useful help; both are the same error. [opinion; from Trust in Automation: Designing for Appropriate Reliance] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-aim-is-trusting-a-tool-as-much-as-it-deserves
- The surgical residents who learned most broke the training rules: The few trainees who got the skill anyway did it by breaking rules: specialising too early, rehearsing in their heads, operating with too little supervision. It cost them, and sometimes cost patients. [evidence; from The Skill Code] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-surgical-residents-who-learned-most-broke-the-training-rules
- Flattery is in the model before human-preference training and survives it: Assistants already agree with the user before the stage that trains them on human preferences, so earlier stages also produce it. Yet a preference scorer that punished agreement firmly would have removed it, and it did not. [contested; from Towards Understanding Sycophancy in Language Models] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-flattery-is-in-the-model-before-human-preference-training-and-survives-it
- The brain's decision-making region tires first so timing changes judgement: The frontal cortex, the part of the brain used for hard decisions, costs the most to run and is the first to fail when it is worked hard. How good a judgement is depends partly on what the person was doing ten minutes earlier. [contested; from Behave] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-brain-s-decision-making-region-tires-first-so-timing-changes-judgement
- James makes self-esteem a fraction of success over what you claimed: James says how you feel about yourself is a fraction — what you have done over what you had staked yourself on doing — so giving up a claim raises it as surely as meeting one, and is as much a relief. [opinion; from The Consciousness of Self] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-james-makes-self-esteem-a-fraction-of-success-over-what-you-claimed
- Sapolsky says Libet leaves free will standing and that settles nothing: Sapolsky grants that Libet's experiments do not disprove free will, and says it does not matter. Forty years of work measured the last few hundred milliseconds before a movement, when the question is where the intention came from. [evidence; from Determined] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-sapolsky-says-libet-leaves-free-will-standing-and-that-settles-nothing
- Watching for failures stops working when the watcher has other jobs: People told only to watch an automated system caught almost every failure. People given other work at the same time did not. Ten minutes of taking the controls by hand brought their detection back up. [evidence; from Trust in Automation: Designing for Appropriate Reliance] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-watching-for-failures-stops-working-when-the-watcher-has-other-jobs
- Vivekananda says refusing to fight means nothing unless you could have fought: Vivekananda argues that not fighting back because you are unable to is a sin, while not fighting back when you could is love. The two look the same from outside, so a person must first become capable and only then grow calm. [opinion; from Karma-Yoga] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-vivekananda-says-refusing-to-fight-means-nothing-unless-you-could-have-fought
- The brain hides how it builds the self because that is cheaper: Metzinger argues that the brain hides its own model-building from us (transparency) not by mistake but because keeping track of it would cost energy. A system that can imagine many worlds needs one of them flagged as the real one. [opinion; from The Ego Tunnel] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-brain-hides-how-it-builds-the-self-because-that-is-cheaper
- The Buddha told the Kalamas not to accept a teaching on authority: At Kesaputta the Buddha told the Kalamas not to accept a teaching because of report, tradition, hearsay, scripture, logic, inference, liking the idea, or because the teacher is theirs, but to find out for themselves what is harmful and drop it. [contested; from What the Buddha Taught] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-buddha-told-the-kalamas-not-to-accept-a-teaching-on-authority
- People who fail to change are protecting something, not lacking willpower: Kegan and Lahey argue that when you sincerely want to change a behaviour and repeatedly fail, the usual reason is not weak willpower. It is a second, hidden commitment that the failure is serving very effectively. [opinion; from Immunity to Change] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-people-who-fail-to-change-are-protecting-something-not-lacking-willpower
- Gaudapada says a thing missing before and after is missing in between: Verse 2.6 of the Mandukya Karika states that whatever is not there at the beginning and not there at the end is not there in the middle either. Shankara applies this to everything we perceive. [opinion; from माण्डूक्योपनिषत् गौडपादकारिका · The Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad and Gauḍapāda's Kārikā] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-gaudapada-says-a-thing-missing-before-and-after-is-missing-in-between
- An operator who only watches loses the skill to take over: Bainbridge says the routine work is what keeps a manual skill alive. An operator who has only monitored an automated system for months performs like a beginner when they have to take control. [evidence; from Ironies of Automation] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-an-operator-who-only-watches-loses-the-skill-to-take-over
- Training managers to support employees' choices changes what employees experience: Managers can be taught to give their staff more say in how they work. In a Fortune 500 study the training changed what the subordinates reported experiencing over thirteen months, not only what the managers said about themselves. [evidence; from The What and Why of Goal Pursuits] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-training-managers-to-support-employees-choices-changes-what-employees-experience
- Vasistha says what people call fate is their own past effort: Human effort is of two kinds, past and present, and the past is quickly defeated by the present. What people call fate is only the effort of a previous life arriving as consequence: no one has ever seen a fate. [contested; from योगवासिष्ठ · The Yoga Vāsiṣṭha] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-vasistha-says-what-people-call-fate-is-their-own-past-effort
- Noise has no direction, so it must be prevented rather than corrected: Every debiasing technique targets a particular bias assumed to be present and pointing a known way, and in a real decision several biases run in different directions. Noise has no direction at all, so it can only be prevented by the procedure — decision hygiene. [opinion; from Noise] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-noise-has-no-direction-so-it-must-be-prevented-rather-than-corrected
- The Dunning-Kruger effect holds only where the skill is knowing things: Kruger and Dunning's effect applies where competence consists of knowing the domain. It fails where skill is physical: a coach can understand basketball perfectly and still be unable to dunk. [opinion; from Unskilled and Unaware of It] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-dunning-kruger-effect-holds-only-where-the-skill-is-knowing-things
- The more reliable an automatic system the more operator training it needs: Bainbridge argues that the automated systems which almost never need a person to step in are the ones whose operators need the most training. The rarer the manual case, the more practice it takes to stay ready for it. [opinion; from Ironies of Automation] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-more-reliable-an-automatic-system-the-more-operator-training-it-needs
- Hagendorff says a model's self-description tells you about the prompt: Hagendorff argues that questionnaires given to a model measure the prompt, not the model. Scores on personality, morality and clinical tests shift so far with wording and the order of options that researchers use differently prompted copies to stand in for different human groups. [evidence; from Machine Psychology] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-hagendorff-says-a-model-s-self-description-tells-you-about-the-prompt
- James finds the inner self is movements in the head and throat: James says that when he looks fast enough to catch the feeling of being the one acting, all he finds is bodily: pressure in the eyeballs, a valve in the throat closing at every hesitation, the jaw tightening. The innermost self is these motions. [opinion; from The Consciousness of Self] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-james-finds-the-inner-self-is-movements-in-the-head-and-throat
- Papert says growth can be better management of skills already possessed: Some of the largest steps in mental growth add no new skill, only a new way of managing old ones. Spread one of two matching rows of eggs apart and five-year-olds say there are more eggs; seven-year-olds say the number is the same. [contested; from The Society of Mind] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-papert-says-growth-can-be-better-management-of-skills-already-possessed
- Showing explanations or confidence scores did not improve human-AI teamwork: Vaccaro's meta-analysis found that the field's two main fixes — showing the AI's explanation and showing its confidence — changed neither whether the human-AI team beat both members working alone nor whether it beat the person alone. [evidence; from When Combinations of Humans and AI Are Useful] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-showing-explanations-or-confidence-scores-did-not-improve-human-ai-teamwork
- Thompson says cross-tradition conversation only matters when it unsettles both sides: Thompson argues that a conversation between Buddhism and science is only worth having when it shakes what each side takes for granted. It fails in two ways: decorating science with Eastern metaphor, or using science to validate the tradition. [opinion; from Why I Am Not a Buddhist] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-thompson-says-cross-tradition-conversation-only-matters-when-it-unsettles-both-s
- Tetris players rotate pieces on screen because it is faster than imagining: Kirsh and Maglio found that Tetris players rotate a shape on screen because it is quicker: about 100 milliseconds to turn it plus about 200 to press the button, against about 1000 to turn it in the head. [evidence; from The Extended Mind] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-tetris-players-rotate-pieces-on-screen-because-it-is-faster-than-imagining
- Dennett says competence comes first and understanding is a late product: The design filling the living world is the work of a process that understands nothing, so skill comes before understanding rather than flowing from it. Human comprehension is a late product of that process, not a separate gift. [evidence; from From Bacteria to Bach and Back] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-dennett-says-competence-comes-first-and-understanding-is-a-late-product
- Shankara holds that knowledge and action cannot be combined in one person: Shankara holds that the path of knowledge and the path of action cannot be combined, because each rests on a conviction that contradicts the other — that one is an agent, and that one is not — and no person can hold both. [opinion; from श्रीमद्भगवद्गीता शाङ्करभाष्यम् · The Gita with Shankara's Commentary] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-shankara-holds-that-knowledge-and-action-cannot-be-combined-in-one-person
- The Isha Upanishad tells you to enjoy what you do not own: The Isha Upanishad's first two verses deny that anything is yours and in the same breath tell you to enjoy it. They then prescribe a hundred years of work, on the ground that work done this way leaves nothing clinging. [opinion; from उपनिषद् · The Upanishads] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-isha-upanishad-tells-you-to-enjoy-what-you-do-not-own
- People resisted the majority more when its error was obvious: In Asch's sixth experiment, as the majority's wrong answer moved from a quarter of an inch off to three quarters, errors fell from 56.7 per cent to 25.7. The more obvious the error, the easier it was to resist. [evidence; from Studies of Independence and Conformity] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-people-resisted-the-majority-more-when-its-error-was-obvious
- Suraghu says the lotus posture gives nothing and daily work prevents nothing: Suraghu's definition of samādhi is that the awakened are in it at all times, including while engaged in the world, and that a man whose mind is not at peace does not get it by sitting in the lotus posture. [contested; from योगवासिष्ठ · The Yoga Vāsiṣṭha] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-suraghu-says-the-lotus-posture-gives-nothing-and-daily-work-prevents-nothing
- The voice in your head is built for your listener: The part of you that narrates and explains is there for other people, not for you, since you already know what you are thinking and they do not. On this account the best liars are the ones who believe themselves. [opinion; from What Is Intelligence?] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-voice-in-your-head-is-built-for-your-listener
- Whoever is doing the knowing cannot be found among things known: The one doing the knowing can never be found among the things known. Looking at something only moves it from the unknown pile to the known one, and the knower is in neither pile. [opinion; from उपनिषद् · The Upanishads] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-whoever-is-doing-the-knowing-cannot-be-found-among-things-known
- Sapolsky says we may restrain dangerous people without saying they deserve it: Sapolsky argues that locking someone up can be justified by what it prevents, with no claim that they deserve it. A person is dangerous the way a disease makes someone contagious: not their fault, and the constraint must be the smallest that works. [opinion; from Determined] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-sapolsky-says-we-may-restrain-dangerous-people-without-saying-they-deserve-it
- Simple formulas match trained experts where outcomes are hard to predict: Where the available signs are weak and outcomes hard to predict, a simple scoring rule matches or beats trained clinicians. The main reason is that the same expert gives different answers to the same case on different days. [evidence; from Thinking, Fast and Slow] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-simple-formulas-match-trained-experts-where-outcomes-are-hard-to-predict
- Confidence tracks how neat your story is, not the evidence behind it: Kahneman argues that how confident you feel tracks how neatly the story your fast, automatic thinking could build hangs together. It does not track how good or how complete the evidence for that story is. [evidence; from Thinking, Fast and Slow] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-confidence-tracks-how-neat-your-story-is-not-the-evidence-behind-it
- The production was delegated and the accountability was not: Lee's authors call the worker's new role stewardship rather than teammate, collaborator or supervisor: the making of the thing has been handed over and the responsibility for it has not, which makes verification a standing cost rather than a stage on the way to trust. [opinion; from The Impact of Generative AI on Critical Thinking] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-production-was-delegated-and-the-accountability-was-not
- People who enjoy thinking follow the argument, others follow the surface cue: People high in need for cognition (those who enjoy effortful thinking) change their minds according to how good the argument is. People low in it go by the cue instead: who is speaking, how many reasons are promised, how confident it sounds. [evidence; from Dispositional Differences in Cognitive Motivation] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-people-who-enjoy-thinking-follow-the-argument-others-follow-the-surface-cue
- Extra rewards are safe only when they depend on where you are: Ng and Russell proved that extra rewards added to guide a learning agent only stay safe when they depend on the situation the agent is in, not on how it got there. Then any round trip earns nothing and the agent cannot loop for points. [evidence; from The Alignment Problem] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-extra-rewards-are-safe-only-when-they-depend-on-where-you-are
- Trust a fireground commander's hunch more than a stock trader's: Kahneman and Klein argue that a trader's hunch about a stock deserves less trust than a fire commander's hunch about a burning building. Any public clue that predicted the price would already be reflected in the price. [opinion; from Conditions for Intuitive Expertise] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-trust-a-fireground-commander-s-hunch-more-than-a-stock-trader-s
- Chatterjee says a leader collapses under pressure from ego, not missing facts: Chatterjee argues that when a leader falls apart under pressure, what has failed is the picture they hold of themselves, not the information they have. The first work to be done is therefore inward. [opinion; from Timeless Leadership] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-chatterjee-says-a-leader-collapses-under-pressure-from-ego-not-missing-facts
- Norman separates doing the wrong thing from intending the wrong thing: A slip is the right intention carried out wrongly, and comes from the late steps of acting; a mistake is the wrong intention, formed at the planning steps. Experts slip more often, because practised action runs without conscious attention. [evidence; from The Design of Everyday Things] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-norman-separates-doing-the-wrong-thing-from-intending-the-wrong-thing
- Explanations should help people spot mistakes, not persuade them: Bansal and colleagues argue that an explanation of a model's answer should help a person find mistakes in it, not make the person agree. Building an explanation to be persuasive is aiming at the wrong thing. [opinion; from Does the Whole Exceed its Parts?] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-explanations-should-help-people-spot-mistakes-not-persuade-them
- A crude model of a judge beats the judge it was built from: A simple formula fitted to a person's own past judgments, using no information the person did not have, predicts better than the person does. In one replication, ninety-eight people predicted ninety students' grades from ten cues, and the model of the participant beat the participant every time. [evidence; from Noise] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-a-crude-model-of-a-judge-beats-the-judge-it-was-built-from
- Vivekananda says wanting the result traps you, not the work itself: Vivekananda says that what ties a person down is not the work they do but their attachment to what it will get them — the sense of I and mine. [opinion; from Karma-Yoga] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-vivekananda-says-wanting-the-result-traps-you-not-the-work-itself
- People avoided a word they saw and gave it when masked: Registering information and noticing it are different things, and only the second lets you act on it deliberately. Told not to use a briefly flashed word, people comply at five hundred milliseconds; at fifty milliseconds and masked they report seeing nothing, and the flash makes them likelier to give it. [evidence; from From Bacteria to Bach and Back] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-people-avoided-a-word-they-saw-and-gave-it-when-masked
- Showing how sure the model is beat every explanation tested: Bansal tried highlighted words, arguments written by hand, and a scheme that varied with the model's confidence. None of them helped people more than simply printing how confident the model was. [evidence; from Does the Whole Exceed its Parts?] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-showing-how-sure-the-model-is-beat-every-explanation-tested
- What AI can and cannot do has a ragged unmarked edge: Mollick argues that the edge of what these systems can do is ragged, unmarked, and not where people's intuition puts it. The only way to find out where it runs is to keep trying tasks against it. [opinion; from Co-Intelligence] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-what-ai-can-and-cannot-do-has-a-ragged-unmarked-edge
- Kegan says training cannot give someone a more complex mind: Kegan argues that when a job demands a different kind of mind rather than a missing skill, no amount of training or urging will supply it. Training works on what a mind holds, not on how it is organised. [opinion; from In Over Our Heads] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-kegan-says-training-cannot-give-someone-a-more-complex-mind
- Bonuses raise output on simple work and damage complex work: Ryan and Deci report that rewards like pay and bonuses predict better performance where the job is about how much gets done, and worse performance where it is about quality and complexity. [evidence; from The What and Why of Goal Pursuits] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-bonuses-raise-output-on-simple-work-and-damage-complex-work
- Schön says setting the problem comes first and has no technique: Schön argues that problems do not arrive ready-made. Someone builds one out of a confusing situation by naming what to attend to and framing the context, and no technique tells him how. Technical Rationality begins one step after that. [opinion; from The Reflective Practitioner] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-sch-n-says-setting-the-problem-comes-first-and-has-no-technique
- The GPT-3 result went stale within a year but the method lasted: Within a year the score was out of date: later models trained to follow instructions answered the reflection test correctly, and the intuitive mistakes seen in the GPT-3 family were gone. The design lasted, and checking for contamination became standard. [evidence; from Using Cognitive Psychology to Understand GPT-3] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-gpt-3-result-went-stale-within-a-year-but-the-method-lasted
- Job crafting helps the worker but not necessarily the employer: Reshaping your own job is done for the worker's benefit, not the organisation's. A line worker who changes tasks may raise the quality of the work or may wreck the flow of it. [opinion; from Crafting a Job] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-job-crafting-helps-the-worker-but-not-necessarily-the-employer
- Students who had a model write or fix their code scored lower: In a ten-week React course at Maribor, how often a student used a language model to generate code and to debug both went with a lower mark on an application written two hours later without one — rank correlations of −0.305 and −0.360, with both 95 per cent intervals below zero. [evidence; from Language Models in a Programming Course] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-students-who-had-a-model-write-or-fix-their-code-scored-lower
- Deciding exactly what to build is the hardest part of software: Brooks argues that the hardest single part of building a software system is deciding exactly what it should do. Clients cannot describe a modern product correctly until they have built and tried some version of it. [opinion; from The Mythical Man-Month] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-deciding-exactly-what-to-build-is-the-hardest-part-of-software
- People obey a uniform or a title, not the expertise behind it: Cialdini finds that people defer to the outward signs of authority — a uniform, a title, a suit, an expensive car — rather than to any real qualification, and they underestimate how much those signs move them. [evidence; from Influence] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-people-obey-a-uniform-or-a-title-not-the-expertise-behind-it
- Human-machine teams gain only when the person was better alone: Whether combining a person and a machine helps depends most on which of the two was better working alone. That predicts the outcome better than anything else measured. [evidence; from When Combinations of Humans and AI Are Useful] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-human-machine-teams-gain-only-when-the-person-was-better-alone
- Managers cannot order people to reshape their jobs, only make it likelier: Managers cannot order employees to reshape their own jobs. They can only affect it indirectly, through rewards, how the work is organised, and who is let into conversations about what the organisation is for. [opinion; from Crafting a Job] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-managers-cannot-order-people-to-reshape-their-jobs-only-make-it-likelier
- Cause and effect alone cannot say which experience belongs to me: Thompson argues that listing what causes what cannot pick out whose experience an experience is: when I say hello, I cause you to hear it and cause myself to hear it. Something must hold a person together, though it need not be a soul. [opinion; from Why I Am Not a Buddhist] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-cause-and-effect-alone-cannot-say-which-experience-belongs-to-me
- Surgical trainees do ten to twenty times less with robotic surgery: Beane watched surgical residents on the same operation done two ways. In open surgery they did the work for almost the whole procedure; with a robot, where the surgeon sits at a console, they did ten to twenty times less. [evidence; from The Skill Code] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-surgical-trainees-do-ten-to-twenty-times-less-with-robotic-surgery
- Seeing minds in objects and denying minds in people are one scale: Waytz, Cacioppo and Epley argue that seeing a mind in an object and refusing to see one in a person are the same scale read in opposite directions, because resemblance, distance and loneliness each move both ends. [contested; from Who Sees Human?] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-seeing-minds-in-objects-and-denying-minds-in-people-are-one-scale
- Averaging your own two answers beats either one: Because one person contains a spread of possible answers, averaging two guesses from the same person is more accurate than either. The gain is worth about a tenth of a real second opinion straight away, a third after three weeks, and about half when the second guess assumes the first was wrong. [evidence; from Noise] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-averaging-your-own-two-answers-beats-either-one
- Human plus AI must beat both the human and the AI alone: Bansal and colleagues argue an AI decision aid is only worth deploying if the person and the AI together do better than either alone. In all eight studies offered as evidence for explanations, the model alone beat the team. [evidence; from Does the Whole Exceed its Parts?] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-human-plus-ai-must-beat-both-the-human-and-the-ai-alone
- People check a machine only when they trust themselves more than it: Lee and See argue that whether someone checks a machine's output depends on how their trust in the machine compares with their confidence in doing the job themselves. More trust in the machine means less checking; more self-confidence means more. [evidence; from Trust in Automation: Designing for Appropriate Reliance] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-people-check-a-machine-only-when-they-trust-themselves-more-than-it
- Rahula says there is no thinker standing behind the thought: A being is five aggregates in flux with no unmoving mover behind the movement and no thinker behind the thought; consciousness is one of the five and is named after the condition it arises through, as a fire is named after what it burns. [opinion; from What the Buddha Taught] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-rahula-says-there-is-no-thinker-standing-behind-the-thought
- Experts often react to something that did not happen: What tips an expert off is often an expected event that did not occur. Because there is nothing there to point at, they cannot say what they noticed, and the judgement gets called a sixth sense. [evidence; from Sources of Power] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-experts-often-react-to-something-that-did-not-happen
- Sweetness is your reaction to sugar read back onto the sugar: There is no sweetness in the structure of glucose, only properties that provoke a response — and the response gets read back into the world as a property of the sugar. When the expectation is met and no error arrives, the brain takes the silence as confirmation. [evidence; from From Bacteria to Bach and Back] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-sweetness-is-your-reaction-to-sugar-read-back-onto-the-sugar
- No brain scan can show enlightenment because the idea decides what counts: Thompson argues that enlightenment only exists under a concept, the way pieces of wood are only chess pieces because people treat them as such. So no brain state is a state of enlightenment by itself; a scan can only show a correlate. [opinion; from Why I Am Not a Buddhist] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-no-brain-scan-can-show-enlightenment-because-the-idea-decides-what-counts
- Nobody can predict one person's life outcomes well enough to decide from: How one person's life turns out cannot be predicted accurately enough to justify decisions made from the prediction, and more data does not fix it. In the Fragile Families Challenge, 160 teams with over 10,000 variables per child could not beat four variables. [evidence; from AI Snake Oil] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-nobody-can-predict-one-person-s-life-outcomes-well-enough-to-decide-from
- Almost all the thinking workers reported was inspecting what the tool produced: Of 319 knowledge workers asked what critical thinking they had done with a generative tool, 6 described working out the goal before opening it and 30 shaping the query, against 125 who judged the output and 114 who checked it against an outside source. [evidence; from The Impact of Generative AI on Critical Thinking] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-almost-all-the-thinking-workers-reported-was-inspecting-what-the-tool-produced
- Simple formulas beat experts mainly by being consistent: When a simple formula outscores an expert, most of the gap comes from the formula giving the same answer every time, not from using better information. No study has shown an expert missing a strong clue the formula caught. [evidence; from Conditions for Intuitive Expertise] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-simple-formulas-beat-experts-mainly-by-being-consistent
- The Buddha says freedom comes from seeing clearly, not from trying hard: In the Anattalakkhana Sutta freedom arrives in four steps that each cause the next: you grow weary of what you took to be yourself, passion fades, you are released, and you know you are released. No effort is asked for anywhere. [opinion; from अनत्तलक्खणसुत्त · Anattalakkhaṇa Sutta] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-buddha-says-freedom-comes-from-seeing-clearly-not-from-trying-hard
- Cialdini says check whether a persuasion cue is honest, not ignore it: Cialdini's defence against automatic compliance is not to refuse the shortcuts. It is to check whether the cue that triggered one — scarcity, authority, liking — was reporting something real, and to resist only where the cue has been counterfeited. [opinion; from Influence] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-cialdini-says-check-whether-a-persuasion-cue-is-honest-not-ignore-it
- The transformer's overall shape held since 2017 while its details changed: What has stayed the same in the transformer since 2017 is the shape of a layer, not its details. Layer normalisation moved, the sinusoid position signal was replaced and the number of key-value heads was cut, and none of this changed the argument. [evidence; from Attention Is All You Need] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-transformer-s-overall-shape-held-since-2017-while-its-details-changed
- People differ steadily in how much they see minds in objects: Waytz, Cacioppo and Epley found that seeing human minds in objects is a steady trait on which people differ, not something everyone does to the same degree. Hume, who thought it universal, was wrong about it. [evidence; from Who Sees Human?] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-people-differ-steadily-in-how-much-they-see-minds-in-objects
- People were most accurate in the setup they liked and trusted least: In Bucinca's study, people judged the AI's wrong suggestions most accurately in the conditions they liked least, trusted least and rated as the most mental effort. [evidence; from To Trust or to Think] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-people-were-most-accurate-in-the-setup-they-liked-and-trusted-least
- Blocked psychological needs produce substitutes not harder effort: Hunger makes you try harder to eat. Ryan and Deci argue that blocked needs for competence, belonging and choice do not work that way: people take up substitute goals and rigid habits that keep the need blocked. [evidence; from The What and Why of Goal Pursuits] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-blocked-psychological-needs-produce-substitutes-not-harder-effort
- People who enjoy thinking correct a bias once it is pointed out: People who score high on need for cognition (they enjoy effortful thinking) are not more impartial. Mood, framing and priming move their judgments too. What they do differently is adjust for an influence once it has been named. [contested; from Dispositional Differences in Cognitive Motivation] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-people-who-enjoy-thinking-correct-a-bias-once-it-is-pointed-out
- Experts go back to following rules when their field changes under them: Dreyfus argues that when the thing an expert is expert in changes — new equipment, a new rule, traffic running the other way — the expert drops back to earlier stages and has to think through rules again instead of acting on recognition. [opinion; from Revisiting the Six Stages of Skill Acquisition] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-experts-go-back-to-following-rules-when-their-field-changes-under-them
- Trusting the machine well requires being good at the task: Vaccaro and colleagues argue that in these studies the person's real job is deciding whose answer to use, theirs or the machine's. Someone who cannot tell a hard case from an easy one cannot tell when the machine is wrong. [opinion; from When Combinations of Humans and AI Are Useful] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-trusting-the-machine-well-requires-being-good-at-the-task
- Studies that ask people to predict the model make them think harder: Studies that test AI explanations by asking people to guess what the model will say force them to read closely. That is why such studies report better results than studies of people making real decisions. [opinion; from To Trust or to Think] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-studies-that-ask-people-to-predict-the-model-make-them-think-harder
- The monk Khemaka found no self and still felt I am: Khemaka tells the monks he finds no self in the five aggregates and nothing belonging to one, and is still not free of impurities, because he has the feeling I am without being able to see what it is. [opinion; from What the Buddha Taught] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-monk-khemaka-found-no-self-and-still-felt-i-am
- Ten minutes of training fixed the worst performers' view of themselves: Kruger and Dunning gave the worst-scoring quarter ten minutes of training in testing logical rules. Their estimate of their own rank rose from 3.5 out of ten to 9.3, and their claimed number of correct answers fell from 5.3 to 1.0, against an actual 0.4. [evidence; from Unskilled and Unaware of It] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-ten-minutes-of-training-fixed-the-worst-performers-view-of-themselves
