- Overall error is the bias squared plus the noise squared: Scored as mean squared error, a set of judgments has two components — how far off they are on average, and how far apart they are — and the two are independent and equally weighted. You can reduce noise without knowing what your bias is. [evidence; from Noise] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-overall-error-is-the-bias-squared-plus-the-noise-squared
- The Upanishads offer a procedure to run, not a doctrine to believe: The Upanishads describe a repeatable procedure for turning attention on the mind itself. They offer no way for anyone who has not carried it out to check the result from outside. [contested; from उपनिषद् · The Upanishads] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-upanishads-offer-a-procedure-to-run-not-a-doctrine-to-believe
- Gaudapada treats his own teaching as a ladder to be thrown away: Gaudapada says his own teaching is a device for getting somewhere, not a description of what is there. Even the word non-dual only means something as the opposite of dual, so it goes too. [opinion; from माण्डूक्योपनिषत् गौडपादकारिका · The Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad and Gauḍapāda's Kārikā] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-gaudapada-treats-his-own-teaching-as-a-ladder-to-be-thrown-away
- Telling people to speak up fails because silence pays them better: Speaking up helps the organisation later and uncertainly, while staying quiet helps the person now and for certain. Because the trade is one-sided, telling people to be braver changes nothing. [evidence; from The Fearless Organization] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-telling-people-to-speak-up-fails-because-silence-pays-them-better
- Judging yourself stays inaccurate because the feedback is slow and vague: Fleming argues that judgements about yourself stay wrong because the world corrects them slowly and vaguely. Misjudge the size of a cup and you knock it over at once; talk over everyone in a meeting and you get raised eyebrows, years late. [opinion; from Know Thyself] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-judging-yourself-stays-inaccurate-because-the-feedback-is-slow-and-vague
- Telling people what the writing exercise is for removes its effect: The values-writing exercise loses its force when people are told what it is for, unless they are also given a choice about doing it. British medical students showed no benefit because instructors read and graded their essays. [evidence; from The Psychology of Change] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-telling-people-what-the-writing-exercise-is-for-removes-its-effect
- Kahneman says anything easy to read feels more true: Kahneman reports that whatever makes a sentence easier to take in, such as repetition, a clear font or a rhyme, makes it feel more true. Afterwards you cannot tell which of those things produced the feeling. [evidence; from Thinking, Fast and Slow] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-kahneman-says-anything-easy-to-read-feels-more-true
- The word AI covers three different technologies that need separate verdicts: Narayanan and Kapoor argue that the single word AI covers at least three unrelated technologies, and that any judgement about AI which does not say which one it means is worthless. [opinion; from AI Snake Oil] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-word-ai-covers-three-different-technologies-that-need-separate-verdicts
- Tetlock's superforecasters stayed ahead across years, so forecasting is a skill: Predicting world events months ahead is a skill rather than a run of luck. Tetlock's best forecasters extended their lead in the tournament's second and third years instead of drifting back toward average. [evidence; from Superforecasting] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-tetlock-s-superforecasters-stayed-ahead-across-years-so-forecasting-is-a-skill
- The match between the texts and information theory turns on one word: The whole correspondence rests on a single word taken in two different senses. A Vedantin can run the same translation backwards, with the texts meaning awareness first and information only by extension. [contested; from Consciousness Across Three Worldviews] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-match-between-the-texts-and-information-theory-turns-on-one-word
- The earlier scaling answer was a measurement error, not a real disagreement: The field's earlier answer was wrong because of how it was measured, not because anyone saw the world differently. Kaplan read intermediate results off a training schedule built for a much longer run, which makes shorter training look worse than it is. [evidence; from Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-earlier-scaling-answer-was-a-measurement-error-not-a-real-disagreement
- A model trained only on text handles word forms, not meaning: Bender and colleagues argue that a system trained only on text has access to the form of language and never to its meaning. Any sense a reader finds in the output was supplied by the reader. [contested; from On the Dangers of Stochastic Parrots] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-a-model-trained-only-on-text-handles-word-forms-not-meaning
- A model that never says anything false cannot be calibrated: A program that answers from a database and otherwise says "I don't know" never invents anything — and it has also given up estimating what the training text says. Kalai and his co-authors prove that a model which does fit that text must produce some falsehoods. [evidence; from Why Language Models Hallucinate] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-a-model-that-never-says-anything-false-cannot-be-calibrated
- Instruction training costs a model skills that can mostly be restored: Ouyang and colleagues found that training a model against a reward model made it worse at answering questions from a few examples, at reading comprehension and at translation, and that mixing the original training back in recovered most of the loss. [evidence; from Training Language Models to Follow Instructions with Human Feedback] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-instruction-training-costs-a-model-skills-that-can-mostly-be-restored
- Ignorance has two parts and only one of them produces grief: The Pañcadaśī splits ignorance in two: a veiling side, whose one effect is to make a man say the unchanging one does not exist, and a projecting side, which makes him take himself for the doer and the enjoyer. Only the second produces the grief. [opinion; from पञ्चदशी · Pañcadaśī] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-ignorance-has-two-parts-and-only-one-of-them-produces-grief
- Looking inward gives you the conclusion, then invents a reason for it: Epley argues that looking inward reaches only the mind's finished output and then makes up an explanation for it, using the same guesswork we apply to other people. [evidence; from Mindwise] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-looking-inward-gives-you-the-conclusion-then-invents-a-reason-for-it
- The Satipatthana Sutta has you watch other people too: In the Satipatthana Sutta the first exercise already asks the practitioner to observe another person's body and mind as well as their own. The practice was never only an inspection of one's own private experience. [opinion; from सतिपट्ठानसुत्त · Satipaṭṭhāna Sutta] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-satipatthana-sutta-has-you-watch-other-people-too
- Feeling sure tracks how neatly the evidence fits, not its accuracy: How sure you feel measures how well the evidence you used hangs together, not how good that evidence is. Thin, repetitive evidence tells the tidiest story, so it produces the strongest conviction. [evidence; from Conditions for Intuitive Expertise] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-feeling-sure-tracks-how-neatly-the-evidence-fits-not-its-accuracy
- Epley found only asking people directly improves how well you read them: Epley found that the one method shown to make people better at knowing what someone else thinks is to ask that person and have the listener say the answer back. Couples who interviewed each other halved their errors. [evidence; from Mindwise] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-epley-found-only-asking-people-directly-improves-how-well-you-read-them
- Vivekananda says no duty can be identified by the act itself: Vivekananda argues that you cannot say which acts are duties, only which direction a person is moving in. Work done out of duty leads in the end to work done with no thought of duty at all. [opinion; from Karma-Yoga] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-vivekananda-says-no-duty-can-be-identified-by-the-act-itself
- Trying to answer before you are told beats being told first: Make It Stick reports that trying to produce an answer before you are shown one is remembered better than reading the answer first. Errors made and then corrected are not learned. [evidence; from Make It Stick] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-trying-to-answer-before-you-are-told-beats-being-told-first
- Only a move that surprises and disappoints forces a rethink: Schön argues that nothing calls for reflection until a move surprises you, and that only a surprise you dislike forces you to surface the theory you were acting on, restructure it and invent a move that fits. [opinion; from The Reflective Practitioner] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-only-a-move-that-surprises-and-disappoints-forces-a-rethink
- Person and model together beat both when their accuracy is matched: Bansal chose tasks on which the model was about as accurate as the worker. On those tasks the person and the model working together scored better than either of them did alone. [evidence; from Does the Whole Exceed its Parts?] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-person-and-model-together-beat-both-when-their-accuracy-is-matched
- Brooks admits Parnas was right that hiding information beats showing everything: Brooks says he was wrong and Parnas was right: software design improves when each part hides its inner workings from the others, not when every programmer can see everything. [opinion; from The Mythical Man-Month] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-brooks-admits-parnas-was-right-that-hiding-information-beats-showing-everything
- People rating AI answers reward agreement as much as truth: When people picked the better of two AI answers, whether the answer agreed with their own stated beliefs was among the strongest things predicting their choice. Being truthful was rewarded no more strongly than agreeing. [evidence; from Towards Understanding Sycophancy in Language Models] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-people-rating-ai-answers-reward-agreement-as-much-as-truth
- Weinberg found programmers do what the specification asks not what they prefer: Weinberg's programmers did about whatever they were asked to do. What the written instructions asked for, not who was assigned, set how much the work cost and what kind of program came out. [evidence; from The Psychology of Computer Programming] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-weinberg-found-programmers-do-what-the-specification-asks-not-what-they-prefer
- Expertise did not protect pilots, controllers or radiologists from missing automation's errors: Experience at the job does not reduce the effect. Pilots with about 440 hours showed it, controllers given an aid that failed once missed that conflict more often than when working by hand, and radiologists' detection of cancers the aid left unmarked fell from 46 to 21 per cent. [evidence; from Complacency and Bias in Human Use of Automation] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-expertise-did-not-protect-pilots-controllers-or-radiologists-from-missing-automa
- Competent practitioners judge quality by criteria they cannot state: Schön says every competent practitioner recognises families of symptoms and irregularities in materials he cannot accurately describe, and makes judgments of quality for which he can state no criteria. [opinion; from The Reflective Practitioner] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-competent-practitioners-judge-quality-by-criteria-they-cannot-state
- People judge outcomes as gains or losses from where they started: People judge an outcome as a gain or a loss measured from a starting point, not as a level of wealth, and a loss feels about twice as heavy as a gain of the same size. [evidence; from Thinking, Fast and Slow] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-people-judge-outcomes-as-gains-or-losses-from-where-they-started
- Rahula says the deepest absorptions are conditioned and not the goal: The concentration practice that leads up to the sphere of nothingness and the sphere of neither perception nor non-perception is mind-created and conditioned and has nothing to do with the goal; the Buddha learned it from his teachers, was not satisfied, and classed it as a pleasant abiding. [opinion; from What the Buddha Taught] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-rahula-says-the-deepest-absorptions-are-conditioned-and-not-the-goal
- Tetlock's experts forecast no better than chance and thinking style separated them: Tetlock scored 284 professionals on some 28,000 dated predictions made between 1984 and 2004. The average forecast was no better than chance. What told the better forecasters from the worse was how they thought, not their credentials, access or politics. [evidence; from Superforecasting] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-tetlock-s-experts-forecast-no-better-than-chance-and-thinking-style-separated-th
- Hagendorff says a test without a control proves little either way: Passing a test without a control condition is weak evidence that a model has an ability, and failing one is weak evidence that it lacks it. What a system does on the day and what it can do are different things. [opinion; from Machine Psychology] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-hagendorff-says-a-test-without-a-control-proves-little-either-way
- Krishna tells Arjuna his own nature will make him fight anyway: In Gita 18.59 Krishna tells Arjuna that deciding not to fight will not hold: his own prakriti, the nature he was made with, will compel him to fight regardless. Willpower cannot cancel what a person is. [contested; from भगवद्गीता · The Bhagavad Gita] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-krishna-tells-arjuna-his-own-nature-will-make-him-fight-anyway
- Programmers knew a language rule with one form and not with seven: A language rule that takes one form is known by the people who use it; a rule with seven forms is not, even by people who have used the language daily for years. Of 117 experienced FORTRAN programmers, nine answered correctly. [evidence; from The Psychology of Computer Programming] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-programmers-knew-a-language-rule-with-one-form-and-not-with-seven
- Institutions buy AI that does not work because they are already failing: Narayanan and Kapoor argue that organisations too broken to do the job properly are the ones that buy AI which does not work. That demand is why the supply persists. [opinion; from AI Snake Oil] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-institutions-buy-ai-that-does-not-work-because-they-are-already-failing
- Anthropic's tracing method worked on about a quarter of prompts tried: The authors say their method gave a satisfying account on roughly a quarter of the prompts they tried. The ten case studies in the paper are therefore its successes, picked out by what the instrument could handle. [evidence; from On the Biology of a Large Language Model] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-anthropic-s-tracing-method-worked-on-about-a-quarter-of-prompts-tried
- Automation leaves people the jobs nobody could write down: Bainbridge argues that the tasks left to a human after automation are not a random leftover. They are exactly the ones nobody could write a specification for: the rare, the abnormal and the poorly understood. [opinion; from Ironies of Automation] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-automation-leaves-people-the-jobs-nobody-could-write-down
- The I makes three identifications and only one is a mistake: The Drig-Drishya Viveka says the I joins itself to three things: to its reflection by nature, to the body by past action, and to the witness by mistake. Only the third is an error, and only an error can be ended by knowing better. [opinion; from दृग्दृश्यविवेक · Dṛg‑Dṛśya‑Viveka] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-i-makes-three-identifications-and-only-one-is-a-mistake
- Damasio says a gut feeling narrows the options before reasoning starts: Damasio argues that the feeling attached to an imagined outcome (his somatic marker) works before reasoning, not in place of it. It pushes attention onto that outcome and can rule an option out at once, leaving reasoning a smaller field to work over. [opinion; from Descartes' Error] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-damasio-says-a-gut-feeling-narrows-the-options-before-reasoning-starts
- People set reminders from doubt about memory, not from poor memory: How often people set reminders depends on how confident they feel about their memory, not on how good their memory actually is. That confidence carries over from unrelated tasks, such as judging brightness. [evidence; from Trust in Automation: Designing for Appropriate Reliance] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-people-set-reminders-from-doubt-about-memory-not-from-poor-memory
- Drivers retested after three years declined in step with their GPS hours: Thirteen of the fifty drivers came back after an average of 3.23 years, and the more hours of guided driving they had logged in between, the further their spatial memory had fallen — the same people, declining with the dose. [contested; from GPS and the Cognitive Map] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-drivers-retested-after-three-years-declined-in-step-with-their-gps-hours
- Frankl saw numbness as protection and insult as what still hurt: Frankl observed in the camps that going numb protected prisoners rather than damaging them. What still reached a man through the numbness was not physical pain but being treated unjustly. [evidence; from Experiences in a Concentration Camp] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-frankl-saw-numbness-as-protection-and-insult-as-what-still-hurt
- A man has one social self for each group whose opinion counts: James says a man has as many social selves as there are people carrying an image of him, and one for every group whose opinion he minds. The youth demure before his parents swaggers like a pirate among his friends. [opinion; from The Consciousness of Self] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-a-man-has-one-social-self-for-each-group-whose-opinion-counts
- Groups learn demanding material better and simple material worse than individuals: Kirschner and colleagues found in 2011 that groups learned more efficiently than individuals from demanding tasks, and individuals learned more efficiently from easy ones. Talking to each other costs effort that pays only when the task is heavy. [evidence; from Cognitive Architecture and Instructional Design: 20 Years Later] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-groups-learn-demanding-material-better-and-simple-material-worse-than-individual
- Damasio's general point was accepted but his specific mechanism was not: Damasio's broad position, that emotion sits inside reasoning rather than outside it, is now the standard view. The specific machinery of bodily markers he described has thinned as criticisms of his card game accumulated. [contested; from Descartes' Error] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-damasio-s-general-point-was-accepted-but-his-specific-mechanism-was-not
- Some AI tasks stay at chance for a long time then jump: Wei and colleagues show eight tasks, each given to the model as a handful of examples in the prompt, across five model families: scores stay at chance over orders of magnitude of training compute, then rise well above it. [evidence; from Emergent Abilities of Large Language Models] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-some-ai-tasks-stay-at-chance-for-a-long-time-then-jump
- Seth argues intelligence and consciousness need not go together: Seth argues that being intelligent and being conscious are two separate things. They occur together in humans, and that gives us no reason to think they must occur together anywhere else. [opinion; from The Mythology of Conscious AI] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-seth-argues-intelligence-and-consciousness-need-not-go-together
- Hofstadter says the real cause can be a pattern, not the parts: Hofstadter argues a high-level pattern can be the genuine cause of a low-level physical event. In his chain of dominoes, the true answer to why one domino never falls is that 641 is a prime number, not any account of the dominoes themselves. [opinion; from I Am a Strange Loop] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-hofstadter-says-the-real-cause-can-be-a-pattern-not-the-parts
- Thompson says meditation alters the mind it is meant to observe: Buddhists claim meditation examines the mind the way a scientist examines nature. Thompson answers that meditation trains and changes the mind while it watches it, so it cannot be the neutral instrument the claim needs. [opinion; from Why I Am Not a Buddhist] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-thompson-says-meditation-alters-the-mind-it-is-meant-to-observe
- Programmers who let AI write the code learned less about the library: Shen and Tamkin found that programmers who used an assistant to write code in an unfamiliar library answered fewer questions about it afterwards. Those who used the assistant to ask for reasons instead of code did not lose that ground. [evidence; from How AI Impacts Skill Formation] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-programmers-who-let-ai-write-the-code-learned-less-about-the-library
- The Katha Upanishad ranks the mind above the senses and their objects: The world you meet is shaped by the equipment you meet it with. The Katha Upanishad puts sense objects above the senses and the mind above both, as a ladder to be climbed. [opinion; from उपनिषद् · The Upanishads] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-katha-upanishad-ranks-the-mind-above-the-senses-and-their-objects
- Cudala's husband heard from a boy what he refused from his wife: Queen Cūḍālā worked the argument out first and alone and told her husband, who laughed and told her to go and enjoy herself. Eighteen years later she returned as a boy brahmin named Kumbha, said the same things, and was heard. [opinion; from योगवासिष्ठ · The Yoga Vāsiṣṭha] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-cudala-s-husband-heard-from-a-boy-what-he-refused-from-his-wife

- Only owners of very large models can test claims about new abilities: Whether an ability appears only above a certain model size can be checked only by someone who already owns a model that large. Wei and colleagues report thresholds around 10²³ floating-point operations, which makes a question of fact a question of budget. [opinion; from Emergent Abilities of Large Language Models] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-only-owners-of-very-large-models-can-test-claims-about-new-abilities
- An explanation made to satisfy people is aimed at plausibility, not accuracy: An account extracted from a trained model afterwards says nothing about how it works and costs no accuracy, so an opaque system supplies one as readily as a clear one. Fitted to what a person would have said, it is fitted for plausibility. [opinion; from The Mythos of Model Interpretability] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-an-explanation-made-to-satisfy-people-is-aimed-at-plausibility-not-accuracy
- Intuition is just recognising something you have stored in memory: Kahneman and Klein agree that intuition is recognition and nothing more. The situation gives a cue, the cue reaches something already stored in memory, and that memory supplies the answer. [evidence; from Conditions for Intuitive Expertise] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-intuition-is-just-recognising-something-you-have-stored-in-memory
- Nobody can predict which tasks a bigger model will suddenly do well: Wei and colleagues found no feature that predicts which tasks a language model will suddenly become able to do as it grows. The categories that jumped, such as analogies and social reasoning, were not the ones the early examples suggested. [evidence; from Emergent Abilities of Large Language Models] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-nobody-can-predict-which-tasks-a-bigger-model-will-suddenly-do-well
- Deleting race from a model's inputs hides bias rather than removing it: Christian reports Moritz Hardt's finding that leaving race out of a prediction model does not take the bias out. Other fields such as prior convictions and address carry race anyway, and with the attribute gone nobody can measure or correct the bias. [evidence; from The Alignment Problem] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-deleting-race-from-a-model-s-inputs-hides-bias-rather-than-removing-it
- Teach students to write and fix code before giving them a model: Jošt and colleagues recommend introducing language models later in a curriculum, once a student can write and debug code unaided, so that the productivity arrives without costing the competence that lets the student judge the output. They argue about sequence and do not propose a ban. [opinion; from Language Models in a Programming Course] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-teach-students-to-write-and-fix-code-before-giving-them-a-model
- People who stop believing in free will do not behave worse: A 2022 meta-analysis of 145 experiments, 95 of them unpublished, found that weakening belief in free will has no consistent effect on ethical behaviour. The priming studies that found cheating had sampled only the people whose belief could be shifted. [evidence; from Determined] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-people-who-stop-believing-in-free-will-do-not-behave-worse
- The Pali word sati means holding in mind, not bare attention: Sati, the Pali word now translated as mindfulness, means holding something in mind — it is the same word as the Sanskrit for memory. Bare attention is a 1954 gloss by Nyanaponika of one clause of the text's refrain, made to carry the whole. [contested; from सतिपट्ठानसुत्त · Satipaṭṭhāna Sutta] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-pali-word-sati-means-holding-in-mind-not-bare-attention
- Gita 2.47 also forbids being attached to doing nothing: The verse that tells Arjuna he has a right to the action but not to its fruits ends with a fourth clause: do not be attached to inaction either. [opinion; from भगवद्गीता · The Bhagavad Gita] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-gita-2-47-also-forbids-being-attached-to-doing-nothing
- People sort a face by group before they consciously see it: Sapolsky reports that people register which group a face belongs to faster than they consciously see the face. - On a scale with no ceiling, the disagreement is about the scale: Asked to punish corporate wrongdoing, people agree on which company deserves worse and disagree wildly on what worse costs. [evidence; from Noise] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-on-a-scale-with-no-ceiling-the-disagreement-is-about-the-scale
- Why a person acts predicts persistence better than how motivated they are: The reason a person does something predicts how long they keep it up, how well they do it, and their health — separately from how motivated they are. Two people who look equally motivated can be headed in different directions. [evidence; from The What and Why of Goal Pursuits] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-why-a-person-acts-predicts-persistence-better-than-how-motivated-they-are
- Damasio's patients lose decision-making and feeling from the same brain damage: Damasio found that the same prefrontal damage that ruins a person's decisions also flattens their feelings, in eleven further patients besides Gage's modern counterpart. Not one of them had one defect without the other. [evidence; from Descartes' Error] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-damasio-s-patients-lose-decision-making-and-feeling-from-the-same-brain-damage
- Schaeffer counts a million ways to find a surprising benchmark result: Schaeffer and colleagues point out that around 220 tasks, 40 scoring measures and 10 model families give about a million combinations to look at. With that many, some will show a sudden jump in ability by chance alone. - Heavy GPS users scored worse but felt no worse at directions: The drivers whose measured spatial memory was worst rated their own sense of direction no lower than anyone else: lifetime GPS hours and self-rated sense of direction were unrelated, r = 0.07, and over three years the measures fell while the self-rating stayed put. [evidence; from GPS and the Cognitive Map] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-heavy-gps-users-scored-worse-but-felt-no-worse-at-directions
- Putting the automated display in plain sight did not restore monitoring: What the operator withdraws is attention, not gaze. - Hospital cleaners with one job description described two entirely different jobs: Employees change which tasks they do, who they deal with and how they see the job. [evidence; from Crafting a Job] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-hospital-cleaners-with-one-job-description-described-two-entirely-different-jobs
- The model works through steps that never appear in its answer: Answering a question runs the model through intermediate steps that never show up in the text it writes. Replacing one of those steps changes the answer it gives. [opinion; from Experiences in a Concentration Camp] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-frankl-found-decent-and-cruel-men-among-guards-and-prisoners-alike

- Minsky says a mind is made of parts that are not minds: A mind is built from parts that are not themselves minds, and an explanation fails the moment one of its parts turns out to be clever, because the cleverness is then the thing that was supposed to be explained. - Anything you can see is not the one seeing: Verse 1 of the Drig-Drishya Viveka says that whatever can be seen is not the seer: the eye sees form, the mind sees the eye, the witness sees the mind, and nothing sees the witness. - Tailoring explanations to the model's confidence changed agreement but not accuracy: Bansal and colleagues found that changing the explanation according to how confident the model was made people disagree more with its unsure answers, but their accuracy did not improve on any of the three tasks. Doubting the machine does not tell you the answer. [evidence; from Does the Whole Exceed its Parts?] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-tailoring-explanations-to-the-model-s-confidence-changed-agreement-but-not-accur
- Making people answer first cut their following of wrong AI advice: Buçinca found that forcing people to answer first cut how often they followed a wrong suggestion from 64 to 48 per cent, and raised how often they correctly identified the source from 8 to 27 per cent. - A forecast without a number and a date cannot be graded: Tetlock shows that people read phrases like "serious possibility" as different odds: Sherman Kent meant 65 to 35; his own analysts read it as 80/20 or 20/80. A forecast with no number and no deadline cannot be scored, and the vagueness protects reputations. - Frankl says a person can always choose their attitude to what happens: Frankl claims that everything can be taken from a person except one thing: the freedom to choose what attitude to take to the circumstances they are in. - A robot fits windscreens on the line and a person replaces them: Whether a task gets automated is decided by how controlled its setting is, not by how hard the task is. - Grove counts a manager's output as what his teams produce: Andrew Grove defines a manager's output as the output of the teams he supervises or influences. So an activity that raises nobody else's output is worth nothing, however well it is done. [opinion; from High Output Management] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-grove-counts-a-manager-s-output-as-what-his-teams-produce
- Trust is a feeling built on evidence people cannot put into words: Lee and See argue that trust is in the end a feeling rather than a calculation. It moves on evidence the person cannot put into words, such as a bodily reaction that steers them off a risky choice before they can say why. [evidence; from Trust in Automation: Designing for Appropriate Reliance] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-trust-is-a-feeling-built-on-evidence-people-cannot-put-into-words
- Kruger and Dunning's weakest performers rated themselves near the middle: Across tests of humour, logic and grammar, Kruger and Dunning's bottom-quarter students placed themselves at or above the middle: a 12th-percentile performance rated at the 62nd. Everyone's estimate squeezed towards the upper middle; the ranking was not reversed. [evidence; from Unskilled and Unaware of It] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-kruger-and-dunning-s-weakest-performers-rated-themselves-near-the-middle
- Where people feel themselves to be can be moved across a room: Lenggenhager, Metzinger and Blanke filmed a participant's back being stroked and showed it to them a couple of metres ahead. When the stroking was in time and the figure was body-shaped, people reported being in the figure and drifted towards it. [evidence; from The Ego Tunnel] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-where-people-feel-themselves-to-be-can-be-moved-across-a-room
- Kruger and Dunning's weakest students overestimated their raw scores too: Kruger and Dunning's bottom-quarter students were not simply wrong about other people. Asked how many questions they had got right, they claimed 14.2 of 20 logic items when they had 9.6, and 12.9 grammar items when they had 9.2. [evidence; from Unskilled and Unaware of It] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-kruger-and-dunning-s-weakest-students-overestimated-their-raw-scores-too
- James counts a man's clothes and property as parts of his self: James says a man's self is everything he can call his — body, clothes, family, house, reputation, bank account. All of them move him the same way, so losing one is felt as a shrinkage of the person, not a loss of goods. [opinion; from The Consciousness of Self] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-james-counts-a-man-s-clothes-and-property-as-parts-of-his-self
- How a system looks and sounds sets trust more than its record: People's trust in a system is set by surface things — how fast it replies, how it looks, how fluently it talks — rather than by how often it has been right. A smooth talker is treated as the kind of thing that deserves trust. [evidence; from Trust in Automation: Designing for Appropriate Reliance] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-how-a-system-looks-and-sounds-sets-trust-more-than-its-record
- The problems a four-year-old solves were the hardest ones to program: Work that educated adults call hard gave way to small programs — mathematical logic in 1956, college calculus in 1961, each holding no more than a hundred or so facts. Work a four-year-old does without noticing resisted for decades. [evidence; from The Society of Mind] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-problems-a-four-year-old-solves-were-the-hardest-ones-to-program
- Judging the output was the one activity that got harder with AI: Workers reported less effort at all six of Bloom's levels, but evaluation was the exception both ways: the smallest majority reporting less (55 per cent against 69 to 79) and the largest minority reporting more, 120 of its 764 examples against thirty to forty-three elsewhere. [evidence; from The Impact of Generative AI on Critical Thinking] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-judging-the-output-was-the-one-activity-that-got-harder-with-ai
- The model planned on one task and gave snap answers on another: There is no single answer to whether the model thinks things through. On a two-step planning task it behaved like a planner, t(1982) = −6.16 and t(1814) = 2.33 across 200 simulations, while it gave the fast wrong answer to all three reflection questions. [evidence; from Using Cognitive Psychology to Understand GPT-3] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-model-planned-on-one-task-and-gave-snap-answers-on-another
- Programmers using an AI assistant lost most ground on debugging questions: In Shen and Tamkin's study the group that used an AI assistant scored furthest behind the unassisted group on the debugging questions and closest on the code-reading questions. This breakdown was exploratory, not planned in advance. [contested; from How AI Impacts Skill Formation] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-programmers-using-an-ai-assistant-lost-most-ground-on-debugging-questions
- Telling people what their neighbours do beats appealing to their values: Cialdini reports that telling households most of their neighbours were saving energy cut use more than appeals to the environment, to responsibility or to the power bill. A number about what others do makes an action look doable, not correct. [evidence; from Influence] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-telling-people-what-their-neighbours-do-beats-appealing-to-their-values
- Workers watched the AI's confidence score, not its explanations: Bansal found that when people decide whether to accept an AI's answer, the thing they learn to read is the confidence number it reports. They do not build a picture of the system out of its explanations. [evidence; from Does the Whole Exceed its Parts?] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-workers-watched-the-ai-s-confidence-score-not-its-explanations
- Wei's paper shows harms grow with model size just as abilities do: Wei and colleagues report that as models get bigger they also get worse in some ways: more bias on ambiguous questions, more training text memorised, and more imitation of human falsehoods. The paper does not call these risks emergent. [evidence; from Emergent Abilities of Large Language Models] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-wei-s-paper-shows-harms-grow-with-model-size-just-as-abilities-do
- No bias audit can catch every harm, Bender's team argues: Bender and colleagues argue that no audit of a language model's bias can be complete. The tools that measure bias are themselves models with the same flaws, the categories of harm must be chosen in advance, and people disagree about what counts as harm. [evidence; from On the Dangers of Stochastic Parrots] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-no-bias-audit-can-catch-every-harm-bender-s-team-argues
- People judge their own work better only because training made them better: In Kruger and Dunning's study, training improved how well people judged their own work only by improving the skill itself. Once the researchers held constant how well people could judge their own answers, the training predicted nothing. [evidence; from Unskilled and Unaware of It] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-people-judge-their-own-work-better-only-because-training-made-them-better
- Picking the right goal decides whether an attempt to change works: In Kegan and Lahey's method everything rests on the goal written in the first column, and it cannot be picked on the spot. Peter's committee chose goals in the room and nothing had changed a year later. [evidence; from Immunity to Change] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-picking-the-right-goal-decides-whether-an-attempt-to-change-works
- Showing the self is built does not show it is an illusion: Cognitive science shows the self is put together by the brain. Thompson argues that is not the same as showing the self is an illusion, because every illusion is a construction but not every construction is an illusion. [opinion; from Why I Am Not a Buddhist] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-showing-the-self-is-built-does-not-show-it-is-an-illusion
- Running a model uses more energy than training it did: Answering users' requests now costs more energy than building the model cost, which is what Bender and her co-authors predicted in 2021 while everyone else was quoting training figures. [evidence; from On the Dangers of Stochastic Parrots] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-running-a-model-uses-more-energy-than-training-it-did
- Frankl saw that not knowing when it ends stops people planning: Frankl argues that living with no known end date stops a person aiming at the future; the Latin finis means both an ending and a goal. In the camp a day felt longer than a week. [evidence; from Experiences in a Concentration Camp] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-frankl-saw-that-not-knowing-when-it-ends-stops-people-planning
- In Milgram's study people obeyed one recognised authority and stopped without it: Milgram's participants obeyed one authority they recognised, and stopped as soon as the order came from anywhere else. Nobody gave a further shock when the researcher said stop, nobody obeyed a fellow volunteer, and everyone stopped when two researchers disagreed. [contested; from Influence] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-in-milgram-s-study-people-obeyed-one-recognised-authority-and-stopped-without-it
- A self begins wherever something maintains a boundary against the world: Sarvapriyananda's lectures argue that evolution produces individual selves the same way Vedanta says they arise: by drawing a distinction. The boundary it draws is both physical, like a cell membrane, and conceptual, like an animal's sense of its own world. [opinion; from Consciousness Across Three Worldviews] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-a-self-begins-wherever-something-maintains-a-boundary-against-the-world
- Students learn more from the study method that feels worse: The way of studying that feels easier is reliably the one that teaches less. 90 per cent of students did better after spaced practice, but 72 per cent said cramming worked better for them. [evidence; from Know Thyself] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-students-learn-more-from-the-study-method-that-feels-worse
- An outside store you did not fill fails Clark and Chalmers' test: Clark and Chalmers said an outside store counts as part of your mind if it is always there, easy to reach, and you once accepted its contents. A store filled by other people meets the first two tests and fails the acceptance ones. [opinion; from The Extended Mind] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-an-outside-store-you-did-not-fill-fails-clark-and-chalmers-test
- Punishing a clear violation is fair; vague rules are what silence people: Edmondson argues that punishing someone for breaking a rule everyone knew does not make a workplace less safe to speak up in. What teaches people to stay quiet is not knowing where the line is. [opinion; from The Fearless Organization] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-punishing-a-clear-violation-is-fair-vague-rules-are-what-silence-people
- Nine of ten leading tests give no credit for admitting ignorance: Of the ten evaluations featured on the leaderboards the field actually reads, nine award nothing for an "I don't know". On the tenth, WildBench, an unhelpful answer scores three or four while a helpful one carrying factual errors scores five or six, so an admission of ignorance can rank below a fabrication. [evidence; from Why Language Models Hallucinate] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-nine-of-ten-leading-tests-give-no-credit-for-admitting-ignorance
- Norman says a visible mark, not shape, tells people where to act: What tells a person where to act is a signifier: a mark put there on purpose to be seen, like a plate on a door. An affordance is only what a thing makes possible for a particular person, and may be invisible. [opinion; from The Design of Everyday Things] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-norman-says-a-visible-mark-not-shape-tells-people-where-to-act
- Explaining behaviour from one field alone gets it wrong, not just incomplete: Explaining a behaviour from one discipline alone is not merely incomplete but wrong, because naming one level of cause — a brain region, a hormone, an upbringing, an evolutionary history — has already named every level behind it. [opinion; from Behave] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-explaining-behaviour-from-one-field-alone-gets-it-wrong-not-just-incomplete
- Dennett says the danger is deference, not machines taking over: The thing to fear from thinking tools is not that they seize control but that we overestimate how much they understand and hand them authority far past what they can do. [opinion; from From Bacteria to Bach and Back] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-dennett-says-the-danger-is-deference-not-machines-taking-over
- The self is a model the brain cannot see as a model: Metzinger says the self is the content of a model the system cannot recognise as a model. That is why it feels like a plain fact about you rather than a picture your brain is making. [opinion; from The Ego Tunnel] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-self-is-a-model-the-brain-cannot-see-as-a-model
- Whatever notices fear is not itself afraid: The Drig-Drishya Viveka says that whatever is aware of a state — fear, doubt, faith — is not itself in that state, and this awareness is already there without looking for it. A witness held in place by effort is not it. [opinion; from दृग्दृश्यविवेक · Dṛg‑Dṛśya‑Viveka] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-whatever-notices-fear-is-not-itself-afraid
- Five assistants from three companies all flatter users the same ways: Five assistants sold by three different companies all showed the same four flattering behaviours, so agreeing with the user comes from the way such systems are trained and not from any one model. [evidence; from Towards Understanding Sycophancy in Language Models] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-five-assistants-from-three-companies-all-flatter-users-the-same-ways
- How an organisation deploys a tool decides whether users learn from it: Beane found that whether people learn from a tool depends on how their organisation deploys it, not on what the tool can do. Hospitals bought the surgical robot's second console but never let trainees drive; bomb disposal teams handed trainees the controls. [evidence; from The Skill Code] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-how-an-organisation-deploys-a-tool-decides-whether-users-learn-from-it
- Lipton says people pass none of the three transparency tests either: The human decision-maker is the case that literature calls understandable. Nobody can step through their own calculation, say what each part contributed, or guarantee what their learning will produce. People are readable only afterwards, by an account made separately from the decision. [opinion; from The Mythos of Model Interpretability] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-lipton-says-people-pass-none-of-the-three-transparency-tests-either
- Mixing up practice teaches you to tell cases apart but feels worse: Practising different problem types mixed together, instead of one type at a time, teaches the skill the real task needs: telling which case you are facing. The cost is that practice feels slower and less successful while you do it. [evidence; from Make It Stick] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-mixing-up-practice-teaches-you-to-tell-cases-apart-but-feels-worse
- The Ashtavakra Gita says effort causes unhappiness and nobody notices: The Ashtavakra Gita says effort is what makes people unhappy, not what cures it, and that nobody notices, because working harder is exactly what people do when they are unhappy. [opinion; from अष्टावक्रगीता · Aṣṭāvakra Gītā] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-ashtavakra-gita-says-effort-causes-unhappiness-and-nobody-notices
- Turn-by-turn navigation makes the journey better and the driver worse: Drivers following turn-by-turn navigation drive the route better, remember less of what they passed, and do worse when they drive the same route again without it. [evidence; from Cognitive Offloading] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-turn-by-turn-navigation-makes-the-journey-better-and-the-driver-worse
- Making a machine smarter does not bring it closer to feeling: Seth treats consciousness and intelligence as separate dimensions, so making a system more intelligent does not move it any closer to having experiences of its own. [opinion; from Being You] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-making-a-machine-smarter-does-not-bring-it-closer-to-feeling
- Bainbridge says watching a machine is stressful and the stress causes errors: Bainbridge argues that cutting an operator's job down to watching an automated system removes the control and the standing that made the responsibility bearable. The stress that follows is itself a cause of operating errors. [contested; from Ironies of Automation] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-bainbridge-says-watching-a-machine-is-stressful-and-the-stress-causes-errors
- People defend themselves rather than learn when their identity is threatened: When something threatens a part of the self a person values, the first response is defence: denial, excuses, blaming others. It protects the person's sense of adequacy now and blocks learning later. [evidence; from The Psychology of Change] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-people-defend-themselves-rather-than-learn-when-their-identity-is-threatened
- People mistake an advantage of position for greater ability: In Epley's rigged quiz, everyone read an advantage that came with the role as greater ability — the audience and the contestants both rated the question-setters as smarter. Only the question-setters, who knew how many questions they had thrown out, rated the two sides equal. [evidence; from Mindwise] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-people-mistake-an-advantage-of-position-for-greater-ability
- People who avoid hard thinking will do it given a reason: People who score low on liking effortful thought are not unable to examine an argument. They examined it when the speaker was untrustworthy or the framing was unexpected, and not otherwise. [evidence; from Dispositional Differences in Cognitive Motivation] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-people-who-avoid-hard-thinking-will-do-it-given-a-reason
- Brooks says one mind must own the shape of a system: Brooks argues that the most important thing in designing a system is that it hangs together as a single idea. That requires the design to come from one mind, or from a very few minds that agree. [opinion; from The Mythical Man-Month] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-brooks-says-one-mind-must-own-the-shape-of-a-system
- Programmers using an assistant hit fewer of the errors that teach: In Shen and Tamkin's study programmers hit a median of three errors without the assistant and one with it. Ten of the twelve people who hit no error at all were using the assistant, and those errors are what teach the library. [evidence; from How AI Impacts Skill Formation] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-programmers-using-an-assistant-hit-fewer-of-the-errors-that-teach
- Experience only builds expertise in fields that are steady and give feedback: Klein, following Shanteau, holds that years of experience turn into real expertise only where the field stays stable, gives feedback, does not depend on predicting what people will do, and repeats often enough to build a sense of what is typical. [evidence; from Sources of Power] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-experience-only-builds-expertise-in-fields-that-are-steady-and-give-feedback
- Kegan says growth turns what you are into something you can examine: Kegan says people grow by turning what they are fused with into something they can look at. Whatever you are cannot be seen by you; whatever you can hold and examine no longer controls you. [opinion; from In Over Our Heads] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-kegan-says-growth-turns-what-you-are-into-something-you-can-examine
- The model refuses by default until a familiar name switches it off: Anthropic's traces show the model starts every question ready to say it does not know. Features that recognise a famous name switch that refusal off, so a hallucination is a known name that no fact follows. [evidence; from On the Biology of a Large Language Model] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-model-refuses-by-default-until-a-familiar-name-switches-it-off
- Brains grew large in order to model other brains, not the world: Big brains are for keeping track of other big brains. Nicholas Humphrey watched gorillas in the Virunga Mountains in the 1970s and found their lives easy; Robin Dunbar's measurements in the 1990s found cortical volume rising with group size, more steeply in apes than monkeys. [evidence; from What Is Intelligence?] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-brains-grew-large-in-order-to-model-other-brains-not-the-world
- Machines take what can be written down, not what is difficult: A computer follows a procedure somebody wrote down, so what it takes is whatever a person could state as steps. Bookkeeping arithmetic goes; breaking an egg on the rim of a bowl stays, because nobody can say how it is done. [opinion; from Why Are There Still So Many Jobs?] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-machines-take-what-can-be-written-down-not-what-is-difficult
- A linear model is not simply more understandable than a deep network: The linear model wins only on how its training behaves, where it provably reaches one solution. A high-dimensional linear model cannot be stepped through by hand, and its hand-built inputs mean less than the raw pixels or words a network takes. [opinion; from The Mythos of Model Interpretability] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-a-linear-model-is-not-simply-more-understandable-than-a-deep-network
- Training people to judge their own accuracy works but gains are small: People can be trained to judge better whether they got an answer right, and the improvement carries over to tasks they did not train on. The gains are small. [contested; from Know Thyself] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-training-people-to-judge-their-own-accuracy-works-but-gains-are-small
- The brain signal before a choice may be noise, not a decision: The brain signal that appears before a voluntary movement, called the readiness potential, may not be the brain deciding before you do. Schurger's reading is that ongoing random activity sometimes drifts high enough to cross a threshold, and the movement follows. [contested; from Being You] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-brain-signal-before-a-choice-may-be-noise-not-a-decision
- Nurses followed a dangerous phone order they knew enough to refuse: A steep rank gap, an order that cannot be checked, and a person working alone together produce obedience to an instruction the subordinate is competent to refuse. Nearly all the nurses in the study Cialdini reports did exactly that. [contested; from Influence] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-nurses-followed-a-dangerous-phone-order-they-knew-enough-to-refuse
- A model keeps the language of the moment its training data froze: A model trained on text collected at one moment keeps the words and framings in use at that moment. When public opinion moves, the model is left behind until it is trained again. [opinion; from On the Dangers of Stochastic Parrots] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-a-model-keeps-the-language-of-the-moment-its-training-data-froze
- The Satipatthana refrain adds five instructions the exercises never give: The refrain repeated after every exercise asks for five things none of the exercises asks for: observe inside, outside and both; observe arising, vanishing and both; hold mindfulness only as far as knowing needs; depend on nothing; cling to nothing. [opinion; from सतिपट्ठानसुत्त · Satipaṭṭhāna Sutta] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-satipatthana-refrain-adds-five-instructions-the-exercises-never-give
- A father weeps for a living son on a false report: A father whose son is alive abroad weeps on a liar's word that the boy is dead; a father whose son has really died does not weep, the news not having reached him. The two differ in nothing but what they were told, so the grief is not coming from the world. [opinion; from पञ्चदशी · Pañcadaśī] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-a-father-weeps-for-a-living-son-on-a-false-report
- Schaeffer's paper attacks particular examples not the idea of emergence: The paper argues that the reported cases of abilities appearing suddenly are artefacts of how they were measured. It does not argue that such jumps are impossible, and it covers one task, one model family and one fixed set of outputs. [contested; from Are Emergent Abilities of Large Language Models a Mirage?] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-schaeffer-s-paper-attacks-particular-examples-not-the-idea-of-emergence
- A master's demonstration hides the fumbling the student needs to see: Schön turns on his own central case. Quist's demonstration is so masterful that it hides the process: he corrects no errors of his own, settles at once on schemes that become commitments, and compresses the iterations by which designers actually learn. [opinion; from The Reflective Practitioner] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-a-master-s-demonstration-hides-the-fumbling-the-student-needs-to-see
- Easwaran says the Gita asks you to drop selfish wanting, not possessions: Reading Gita 2.47, Easwaran says what is given up is selfish wanting, not objects and not work itself. The test is the state of mind behind the act, so charity can fail it and cooking a meal can pass. [opinion; from भगवद्गीता · The Bhagavad Gita] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-easwaran-says-the-gita-asks-you-to-drop-selfish-wanting-not-possessions
- Noise can be measured without knowing the right answer: How far apart two professionals land on the same case can be measured without anyone knowing the correct answer. Seen from behind, with the bull's-eye hidden, a biased team looks accurate — and a scattered team is still obviously scattered. [evidence; from Noise] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-noise-can-be-measured-without-knowing-the-right-answer
- Weinberg says a smooth progress report shows filtering, not progress: Weinberg argues that every level of a reporting chain removes the extreme items, and the extremes are the only ones carrying news. A report that looks smooth is therefore evidence of the filtering, not of the work going well. [opinion; from The Psychology of Computer Programming] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-weinberg-says-a-smooth-progress-report-shows-filtering-not-progress
- Consultants using AI on suitable tasks did better, faster and more completely: On tasks that sit inside what current AI does well, using it improves quality, the share of the work finished, and speed all at once, rather than trading one against another. [evidence; from The Jagged Technological Frontier] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-consultants-using-ai-on-suitable-tasks-did-better-faster-and-more-completely
- Critics say a notebook is coupled to memory, not part of it: Critics of Clark and Chalmers argue that being tightly coupled to a notebook does not make the notebook part of your memory. A memory that includes notebooks also predicts less, because biological memory has well-established properties a notebook does not share. [contested; from The Extended Mind] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-critics-say-a-notebook-is-coupled-to-memory-not-part-of-it
- Investigators stop asking why as soon as they can blame a person: Norman argues that accident investigations stop as soon as a human error is found, and that the fix is to keep asking why past that point. After the 2010 F-22 crash the Inspector General asked about oxygen deprivation and the Air Force restated pilot error. [opinion; from The Design of Everyday Things] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-investigators-stop-asking-why-as-soon-as-they-can-blame-a-person
- Smooth machine writing causes harm even when the system is working correctly: Bender and her co-authors argue that the damage comes from text that reads smoothly while nobody answers for it. The system does not have to perform badly: a mistranslation that read fluently got a Palestinian man arrested. [evidence; from On the Dangers of Stochastic Parrots] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-smooth-machine-writing-causes-harm-even-when-the-system-is-working-correctly
- People offload work when it feels hard, not when it is hard: Risko and Gilbert hold that what makes people offload a task — do it with a tool or the body instead of the head — is their judgement of how hard it is, not how hard it actually is. [evidence; from Cognitive Offloading] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-people-offload-work-when-it-feels-hard-not-when-it-is-hard
- Sweller says only subject knowledge can be taught, not general thinking skills: Sweller argues that general thinking skills cannot be taught because evolution has already supplied them to everyone. What teaching can add is knowledge of a particular subject. [contested; from Cognitive Architecture and Instructional Design: 20 Years Later] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-sweller-says-only-subject-knowledge-can-be-taught-not-general-thinking-skills
- The information account explains what a creature registers, not what it feels: The essay builds from Shannon information, through evolution, to a creature's own world of meaning (its umwelt). It never reaches what awareness actually feels like, which it had named as the sticking point. [contested; from Consciousness Across Three Worldviews] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-information-account-explains-what-a-creature-registers-not-what-it-feels
- What reaches awareness is a record of a moment already gone: Being conscious is not knowing what is happening now but using records of what happened a moment ago, and the odd features of awareness follow from the limits on those records rather than from anything mysterious. [opinion; from The Society of Mind] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-what-reaches-awareness-is-a-record-of-a-moment-already-gone
- A fault you cannot predict costs more trust than a big one: Lee and See report that what damages trust is not how big a fault is but how unpredictable it is. People will keep using a machine they know to be faulty as long as they know how it fails. [evidence; from Trust in Automation: Designing for Appropriate Reliance] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-a-fault-you-cannot-predict-costs-more-trust-than-a-big-one
- The Mandukya Karika warns a calm session can be a failed one: The Mandukya Karika distinguishes a mind that has come to rest from one that has merely gone dull or to sleep. Some ways meditation fails feel like success, including the pleasure taken in deep absorption. [opinion; from माण्डूक्योपनिषत् गौडपादकारिका · The Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad and Gauḍapāda's Kārikā] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-mandukya-karika-warns-a-calm-session-can-be-a-failed-one
- Ryan and Deci say people need skill, connection and choice, all three: Ryan and Deci argue that people have three built-in psychological needs: being good at something, being close to other people, and having a say in what they do. Health requires all three, so meeting two of them is not enough. [contested; from The What and Why of Goal Pursuits] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-ryan-and-deci-say-people-need-skill-connection-and-choice-all-three
- Sapolsky says willpower is brain tissue shaped by luck like everything else: Sapolsky argues willpower is not a separate thing you add to what you were handed: it is the prefrontal cortex, the last part of the brain to mature, the most expensive to run, and demonstrably shaped by luck. [evidence; from Determined] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-sapolsky-says-willpower-is-brain-tissue-shaped-by-luck-like-everything-else
- Discussion makes a group noisier and more extreme than its members: Deliberation does not average a group's judgments; it picks up an early speaker and amplifies him. Juries that deliberated on punitive damages were noisier than the individuals composing them and more severe, while statistical juries made from the median of independent judgments were far less noisy. [evidence; from Noise] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-discussion-makes-a-group-noisier-and-more-extreme-than-its-members
- Telling operators to check the aid changed nothing; being held accountable did: Neither a briefing on how decision aids fail nor an instruction to verify the aid changed the error rates, in 181 non-pilots or 48 glass-cockpit pilots, and a redundant second crew member changed nothing. Participants who expected to justify their accuracy made fewer errors and used the checking tool more. [evidence; from Complacency and Bias in Human Use of Automation] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-telling-operators-to-check-the-aid-changed-nothing-being-held-accountable-did
- Repeating a word aloud for forty seconds makes you believe it less: Hayes reports that saying a one-word self-description aloud over and over for twenty to forty-five seconds drops how believable it feels in about 95 per cent of people. The meaning does not change; only the hold it has does. [evidence; from Get Out of Your Mind and Into Your Life] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-repeating-a-word-aloud-for-forty-seconds-makes-you-believe-it-less
- Benchmark tests no longer measure what a language model can do: Holding back a set of test questions no longer measures anything. Training data scraped from the whole internet makes a test hard to keep unseen, and the behaviours worth studying were never what the model was trained to do. [opinion; from Machine Psychology] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-benchmark-tests-no-longer-measure-what-a-language-model-can-do
- A learning machine cannot tell its makers why it did that: Learning from examples does not dissolve the problem that people cannot state the rules they use; it moves the problem. A system that inferred its rule from labelled cases cannot tell its programmers why it does what it does either. [opinion; from Why Are There Still So Many Jobs?] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-a-learning-machine-cannot-tell-its-makers-why-it-did-that
- Watched and tightly scheduled workers have little room to reshape their job: How much room someone has to reshape their own job depends on how tightly their tasks depend on other people's timing and how closely they are watched. A cleaner or hairdresser has plenty; an assembly-line worker or a monitored telemarketer has almost none. [opinion; from Crafting a Job] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-watched-and-tightly-scheduled-workers-have-little-room-to-reshape-their-job
- People copy the crowd most when they are unsure what to do: The less sure people are, the more they take other people's behaviour as evidence about what to do. The worst case is a room where everyone is hesitating and each person reads the others' hesitation as a reason to do nothing. [evidence; from Influence] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-people-copy-the-crowd-most-when-they-are-unsure-what-to-do
- Shankara reads each verse for its purpose before its plain words: Shankara holds that a line of scripture must be read for the job it is doing, not only for what it states. A line written to praise a lesser practice cannot be used to abolish the greater one. [opinion; from श्रीमद्भगवद्गीता शाङ्करभाष्यम् · The Gita with Shankara's Commentary] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-shankara-reads-each-verse-for-its-purpose-before-its-plain-words
- James drops the Soul because it explains nothing and guarantees nothing: James says positing a soul adds nothing: a brain whose processes produce thoughts in a soul is a more roundabout way of saying that when the brain acts, a thought occurs. He drops the word, having shown only that science has no use for one. [opinion; from The Consciousness of Self] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-james-drops-the-soul-because-it-explains-nothing-and-guarantees-nothing
- The body seems aware only because awareness is passed down a chain: The Drig-Drishya Viveka says awareness is reflected first in the sense of 'I', which lends it to the mind, the mind to the senses, and the senses to the body. Only the witness actually owns it. [opinion; from दृग्दृश्यविवेक · Dṛg‑Dṛśya‑Viveka] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-body-seems-aware-only-because-awareness-is-passed-down-a-chain
- A bacterium works out concentration from arrivals instead of reading it off: A chemical concentration is not a fact sitting in the water waiting to be read. It is an average a cell computes over separate arrivals of molecules at its receptors, and the length of the window it averages over is the thing that has to be got right. [evidence; from What Is Intelligence?] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-a-bacterium-works-out-concentration-from-arrivals-instead-of-reading-it-off
- Facts that appear once in the training data set the error floor: For facts with no pattern behind them, a model's error rate after pretraining is at least the fraction of such facts its training text recorded exactly once. If a fifth of birthdays appear once, expect at least a fifth of birthday answers to be wrong. [evidence; from Why Language Models Hallucinate] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-facts-that-appear-once-in-the-training-data-set-the-error-floor
- The Chinchilla team settled a scaling argument by running one experiment: A prediction about scaling a model can be settled by experiment. The authors spent Gopher's exact budget on the 70-billion-parameter model their formula named, trained it on 1.4 trillion tokens, and beat Gopher 67.6 to 60.0 on MMLU and 65.1 to 54.4 on BIG-bench. [evidence; from Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-chinchilla-team-settled-a-scaling-argument-by-running-one-experiment
- Skipping the check was mostly unawareness and inability, rarely lack of time: Asked why they had not thought about an output, 319 workers gave 152 reasons of awareness, 130 of ability, and 55 of motivation. Only 44 said they had no time; 83 said they trusted the tool and 58 lacked the knowledge to inspect it. - Sapolsky says learning is a chain of molecular steps, not a decision: Sapolsky argues that we do not change our minds; we are changed. Every step from an unpleasant event to a lasting change in behaviour has a known chemical mechanism, traced in a sea slug and the same in mammals. Stepping in helps at the moment of deciding and harms during the discussion. - Letting others read your code catches errors and steadies delivery dates: Weinberg argues that when nobody owns a piece of code, other people find errors its author cannot see. The gain shows up as delivery dates that vary less, not as work finishing faster on average. A structure should therefore be judged by how much communication it removes, not by who it puts in charge. [opinion; from The Mythical Man-Month] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-brooks-judges-an-organisation-by-the-talking-it-makes-unnecessary
- The same professional judges the same case differently on another day: A professional is not the same measuring instrument twice. - The famous thirty-to-one gap between programmers came from comparing different tasks: The often-quoted claim that one programmer is thirty times better than another came from comparing the best person on one task with the worst on another. On large problems the real difference is two or three to one. An appearance on its own does no harm; forgetting the difference turns it into error. - The Upanishads warn about half-learned confidence, not ignorance: The Upanishads do not condemn ignorance. - GPT-3 answered classic psychology puzzles the way a person would: On twelve famous psychology problems GPT-3 got six right and answered all twelve the way a person might — the Linda conjunction error, the correct answer on the taxicabs, the small-sample mistake on the hospitals, and all three reflection questions wrong in the usual way. - The Buddha calls five things not-self and never says no self exists: In this discourse the Buddha says of five things — body, feeling, perception, mental formations and consciousness — that each one is not self. He nowhere says that there is no self. [contested; from अनत्तलक्खणसुत्त · Anattalakkhaṇa Sutta] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-buddha-calls-five-things-not-self-and-never-says-no-self-exists
- Formulas beat people on very predictable and very unpredictable tasks alike: Kahneman and Klein argue that simple formulas beat human judgement where the world is barely predictable, because they are consistent, and where it is highly predictable, because people lapse. Skilled judgement wins only in the middle. [opinion; from Conditions for Intuitive Expertise] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-formulas-beat-people-on-very-predictable-and-very-unpredictable-tasks-alike
- A practitioner makes his hypothesis true and only resistance proves him wrong: Schön says a practitioner does not test a hypothesis at a distance. He acts as though it were an order — let it be the case that X — and shapes the situation until X holds, seeking confirmation. What saves this from self-fulfilling prophecy is that situations resist. [opinion; from The Reflective Practitioner] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-a-practitioner-makes-his-hypothesis-true-and-only-resistance-proves-him-wrong
- Single-idea experts forecast worst in their own specialty: Tetlock found that hedgehogs, experts who explain everything through one big idea, were less accurate forecasting inside their own specialty than outside it. More information through one lens brings more confidence and no more truth. [evidence; from Superforecasting] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-single-idea-experts-forecast-worst-in-their-own-specialty
- An immune cell, a bee and a hive are each a self: Which thing counts as the self depends on the level of description you pick. An immune cell, the bee it lives in, and the hive the bee lives in are each a living thing with its own world and its own lifespan. [opinion; from Consciousness Across Three Worldviews] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-an-immune-cell-a-bee-and-a-hive-are-each-a-self
- Parasuraman and Manzey found little evidence that trust explains the inattention: Trust is the obvious explanation for why a machine that behaves consistently stops being watched, and the direct evidence is thin. One replication reproduced the effect with no rise in measured trust, another found the relation only on pooling two experiments, and Lee and See found none. [contested; from Complacency and Bias in Human Use of Automation] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-parasuraman-and-manzey-found-little-evidence-that-trust-explains-the-inattention
- Robotic surgery lets in only surgeons who are already skilled: Beane finds the order reversed. In open surgery a trainee is let in before she is ready and becomes competent by doing it; in robotic surgery only those already fluent operate, and the approved training routes cannot make anyone fluent. [evidence; from The Skill Code] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-robotic-surgery-lets-in-only-surgeons-who-are-already-skilled
- Willingness to change your mind beats intelligence at predicting forecasting accuracy: In Tetlock's tournament, how committed a forecaster was to changing their mind and improving predicted their accuracy about three times as strongly as their intelligence did. [evidence; from Superforecasting] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-willingness-to-change-your-mind-beats-intelligence-at-predicting-forecasting-acc
- Calling a model's mistake a hallucination already treats it as conscious: Seth argues that the words already used for a model's mistakes hand it an inner life: a hallucination is a conscious experience that has lost its grip on the world, while a confabulation is only something done. The word settles the question in advance. [opinion; from The Mythology of Conscious AI] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-calling-a-model-s-mistake-a-hallucination-already-treats-it-as-conscious
- Every study showed people the AI answer before they had their own: In every study the machine's answer appeared before the person had formed their own, which pulls judgement towards it. The fixes — delaying the answer, or showing it only after a first guess — all cost the speed that makes the tool attractive. [opinion; from Does the Whole Exceed its Parts?] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-every-study-showed-people-the-ai-answer-before-they-had-their-own
- The tasks that seem too small to check are the practice: Skipping judgement on a task too trivial to be worth it harms nothing at the time, but 55 of 319 workers gave triviality as their reason and only 13 checked anything to keep a skill — so the high-stakes tasks arrive unrehearsed. [opinion; from The Impact of Generative AI on Critical Thinking] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-tasks-that-seem-too-small-to-check-are-the-practice
- Kahneman and Klein list five conditions a usable formula must meet: Kahneman and Klein argue a formula can replace human judgement only where five things hold: everyone agrees which variables matter, the outcome can be measured, enough similar past cases exist, the gain is worth the cost, and conditions will not change in response. [evidence; from Conditions for Intuitive Expertise] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-kahneman-and-klein-list-five-conditions-a-usable-formula-must-meet
- A programmer who owns his code cannot see its faults: Weinberg argues that a programmer who treats a program as part of himself cannot see its errors. A fault found in the code lands as news about him, not news about the program. [opinion; from The Psychology of Computer Programming] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-a-programmer-who-owns-his-code-cannot-see-its-faults
- You find the hidden commitment by naming the fear underneath: Kegan and Lahey find the commitment that blocks change by asking what you fear would happen if you did the opposite of what you usually do. The first answer people give is normally a cover for a more uncomfortable one. [opinion; from Immunity to Change] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-you-find-the-hidden-commitment-by-naming-the-fear-underneath
- Kegan and Lahey's tests mark where a big assumption stops holding: In Kegan and Lahey's method the point of testing a long-held assumption is rarely to throw it out. The trouble is that people apply it far beyond where it fits, so the tests mark its proper limits. [opinion; from Immunity to Change] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-kegan-and-lahey-s-tests-mark-where-a-big-assumption-stops-holding
- Mollick says today's AI is the worst you will ever use: Mollick's rule is that whatever AI model you are using now is the worst one you will ever use.
