Any limit you find in it should therefore be recorded with a date and re-tested, not treated as permanent. [opinion; from Co-Intelligence] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-mollick-says-today-s-ai-is-the-worst-you-will-ever-use
- The model's good answers break when the puzzle is reworded slightly: The model's performance on the classic reasoning puzzles falls apart under changes no person would be bothered by, such as a reordered list or a swapped word. The puzzles therefore license no conclusion about whether it reasons. [evidence; from Using Cognitive Psychology to Understand GPT-3] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-model-s-good-answers-break-when-the-puzzle-is-reworded-slightly
- Hayes says the self you describe in words is the dangerous one: Hayes argues that the description a person builds of who they are is the dangerous one, because once you are invested in a label you are also invested in being right about it. [opinion; from Get Out of Your Mind and Into Your Life] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-hayes-says-the-self-you-describe-in-words-is-the-dangerous-one
- Interpretability tools read a stand-in model, not the real one: A model holds more concepts than it has neurons, so one neuron does several unrelated jobs. To get round this, the researchers interpret a separate, easier-to-read network trained to copy the original's behaviour, not the original itself. [evidence; from On the Biology of a Large Language Model] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-interpretability-tools-read-a-stand-in-model-not-the-real-one
- Admitting a real weakness first wins trust faster than listing strengths: Cialdini finds that naming a genuine weakness before making your case earns trust faster than piling up strengths. The move works just as well for someone with an interest to serve as for an honest reporter. [evidence; from Influence] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-admitting-a-real-weakness-first-wins-trust-faster-than-listing-strengths
- A student's overall model use predicted the unassisted exam mark: Averaging a student's reported use of a language model across generating code, debugging and asking for explanations predicts the two-hour unassisted mark about as well as any single use does — a rank correlation of −0.347, interval −0.626 to −0.044, p 0.026. [evidence; from Language Models in a Programming Course] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-a-student-s-overall-model-use-predicted-the-unassisted-exam-mark
- GPT-4 was calibrated before reinforcement learning and not after: Calibration — confidence that tracks how often you are right — is not a virtue added to a base model but what minimising its training loss produces. The stage that follows removes it: GPT-4's confidence matched its accuracy on four-way multiple choice before reinforcement learning and did not afterwards. [contested; from Why Language Models Hallucinate] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-gpt-4-was-calibrated-before-reinforcement-learning-and-not-after
- Machines that merely seem conscious are the closer danger: Seth argues that the nearer danger is not conscious machines but machines that only seem conscious, and that the impression may persist even when you know better. [opinion; from The Mythology of Conscious AI] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-machines-that-merely-seem-conscious-are-the-closer-danger
- Middle-paying jobs shrank in every one of sixteen European economies: Computerising the middle of the pay scale grows both ends. The four middle-skill American occupation groups fell from 60 per cent of employment in 1979 to 49 in 2007 and 46 in 2012, and across sixteen EU economies between 1993 and 2010 the middle-paying share fell in every single country. [evidence; from Why Are There Still So Many Jobs?] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-middle-paying-jobs-shrank-in-every-one-of-sixteen-european-economies
- Damage to one brain area ruins judgment and leaves intelligence untouched: Damasio argues that following social rules, behaving ethically and choosing in your own interest all depend on one brain system, and that system can be destroyed in a person whose attention, perception, memory, language and intelligence are all unharmed. [evidence; from Descartes' Error] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-damage-to-one-brain-area-ruins-judgment-and-leaves-intelligence-untouched
- Thompson says finding mindfulness in a brain region explains nothing: Mindfulness is a way of relating to a situation, not something happening inside the skull. Thompson argues that pointing to the brain region or network where it happens therefore explains nothing about it. [evidence; from Why I Am Not a Buddhist] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-thompson-says-finding-mindfulness-in-a-brain-region-explains-nothing
- A judgment ends when it feels complete, not when the evidence does: What ends a judgment is a feeling that the facts and the conclusion now fit, and it arrives just as readily for a case with no answer. Shown a fictitious executive and asked his chances of surviving two years in the job, 115 MBA students answered anywhere from 10 to 95. [opinion; from Noise] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-a-judgment-ends-when-it-feels-complete-not-when-the-evidence-does
- The famous Dunning-Kruger graph is mostly a statistical artefact: The crossing-lines graph can be produced by regression to the mean plus the general tendency to rate oneself above average. What survives the criticism is the rest: how people sort their own answers, how they grade a stranger's work, and what training changed. [contested; from Unskilled and Unaware of It] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-famous-dunning-kruger-graph-is-mostly-a-statistical-artefact
- Sentencing guidelines cut the gap between judges and were repealed anyway: The US sentencing guidelines worked and were dismantled. The expected difference between two judges fell from 4.9 months in 1986–87 to 3.9 months by 1993; after the Supreme Court struck the mandatory guidelines down in 2005, three-quarters of federal judges preferred the advisory regime and 3 per cent the mandatory one. [evidence; from Noise] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-sentencing-guidelines-cut-the-gap-between-judges-and-were-repealed-anyway
- Enlightenment does not stop pain, it changes who is watching it: Drig-Drishya Viveka says enlightenment is not a painkiller: the pain goes on exactly as before. What changes is that the person knows themselves as the witness of a body in pain rather than as the body. [opinion; from दृग्दृश्यविवेक · Dṛg‑Dṛśya‑Viveka] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-enlightenment-does-not-stop-pain-it-changes-who-is-watching-it
- The Buddha's eleven categories cover every experience so no self can hide: The Buddha lists eleven categories of experience (past, present and future; inside and outside; coarse and fine; low and high; far and near) so that every kind of experience is checked and nothing is left over in which a self could still be found. [opinion; from अनत्तलक्खणसुत्त · Anattalakkhaṇa Sutta] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-buddha-s-eleven-categories-cover-every-experience-so-no-self-can-hide
- The stories we tell other people replace the memories they came from: James says the commonest source of false memory is the account we give other people of what happened: we make it simpler and better than the truth until the fiction expels the reality and reigns alone, and the error is made in entire good faith. [opinion; from The Consciousness of Self] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-stories-we-tell-other-people-replace-the-memories-they-came-from
- The Katha Upanishad asks the reader to turn the eye back: The Katha Upanishad says the sense organs open outward, so attention goes outward by itself. The one thing the collection asks a reader to do is turn the eye back on itself. [opinion; from उपनिषद् · The Upanishads] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-katha-upanishad-asks-the-reader-to-turn-the-eye-back
- Confidence in the tool was the strongest predictor of not checking: Across 936 tasks reported by 319 knowledge workers, confidence that the tool could do that task was the largest predictor of not checking its output (β = −0.69). Confidence in doing the task oneself (0.26) and in judging the output (0.31) ran the other way. [evidence; from The Impact of Generative AI on Critical Thinking] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-confidence-in-the-tool-was-the-strongest-predictor-of-not-checking
- Experts describe the signs they use only when asked about specific cases: Klein found that experts can name the signs they act on if you ask them about particular past cases rather than about their method. A large share of the signs they name appear nowhere in the professional literature. [evidence; from Sources of Power] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-experts-describe-the-signs-they-use-only-when-asked-about-specific-cases
- The grief stops at once and the wound still takes a month: The tenth man, weeping and beating his head, stops weeping the instant he is told. The cut he made takes a month to close, and does not close then. Knowledge cancels the mistake and cancels nothing else. [opinion; from पञ्चदशी · Pañcadaśī] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-grief-stops-at-once-and-the-wound-still-takes-a-month
- Whatever drops out in dream or sleep is not the one reporting: The Pañcadaśī's test is to compare states: whatever is present in one and absent in another is a variable and cannot be what is looking. Run it down the five sheaths and the gross, subtle and causal bodies fall away one at a time. [opinion; from पञ्चदशी · Pañcadaśī] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-whatever-drops-out-in-dream-or-sleep-is-not-the-one-reporting
- A Rhode Island preacher lived two months as a shopkeeper named Brown: The Reverend Ansel Bourne drew money in Providence on 17 January 1887 and vanished. On 14 March, a Norristown shopkeeper of six weeks trading as A. J. Brown woke frightened, said his name was Ansel Bourne, and would not believe two months had passed. [evidence; from The Consciousness of Self] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-a-rhode-island-preacher-lived-two-months-as-a-shopkeeper-named-brown
- Dozens of Bach lovers heard a program's inventions as genuine Bach: Results can be produced by processes their own users cannot follow, and the users cannot tell those results from the human work they imitate. At the Montreal Bach Festival in December 2015 a pianist played four short pieces to over three hundred Bach lovers; dozens called two machine inventions genuine Bach, and about a dozen got all four right. [evidence; from From Bacteria to Bach and Back] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-dozens-of-bach-lovers-heard-a-program-s-inventions-as-genuine-bach
- Drig-Drishya Viveka's meditations point back to whatever is having the experience: The practice here is not concentrating on an object, and not watching thoughts come and go. It takes an experience and uses it to notice what is having that experience. [opinion; from दृग्दृश्यविवेक · Dṛg‑Dṛśya‑Viveka] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-drig-drishya-viveka-s-meditations-point-back-to-whatever-is-having-the-experienc
- A model's explanation of its answer does not show how it worked: A language model's explanation of its answer is made by a separate process from the answer itself. Adding 36 and 59, the model works along two paths at once, then reports carrying the one — a method its internals never used. [evidence; from On the Biology of a Large Language Model] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-a-model-s-explanation-of-its-answer-does-not-show-how-it-worked
- Pain tracks the brain's guess about damage, not the damage itself: A feeling is the body's best inference about its own condition, not a reading taken from it, which is why it can be badly wrong in either direction. A builder needed sedation for a nail that had missed his foot; a worker with a four-inch nail through his palate into his brain reported a mild toothache. [evidence; from What Is Intelligence?] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-pain-tracks-the-brain-s-guess-about-damage-not-the-damage-itself
- Half a software project is testing and the delay shows up last: Brooks says half a software project's time goes on testing, and the delay surfaces only at the end. The project looks on schedule until system testing, then discovers its slip when it is fully staffed and costing the most per day. [opinion; from The Mythical Man-Month] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-half-a-software-project-is-testing-and-the-delay-shows-up-last
- Autor gives three conditions for automation to raise a worker's pay: Whether the gain from automation reaches a particular worker depends on three things: whether she supplies the task the machine now needs done, whether other people can enter that task easily, and whether demand for the output grows as it gets cheaper. [opinion; from Why Are There Still So Many Jobs?] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-autor-gives-three-conditions-for-automation-to-raise-a-worker-s-pay
- The idea that Buddhism is uniquely scientific was invented in the 1800s: Thompson argues that the belief that Buddhism is uniquely rational and scientific is not an old core recovered. Reformers in the nineteenth century took a colonial argument that possessing science proved Christian superiority, and turned it around. [evidence; from Why I Am Not a Buddhist] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-idea-that-buddhism-is-uniquely-scientific-was-invented-in-the-1800s
- Grove says every measure needs a second measure beside it: Grove argues that any number a team is pushed to improve needs a second number beside it that catches the damage. Cut inventory without counting shortages and the shortages rise unseen. [opinion; from High Output Management] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-grove-says-every-measure-needs-a-second-measure-beside-it
- Vivekananda says every act leaves a trace and the traces become character: Vivekananda holds that every action leaves a trace in the mind, that the sum of those traces is a person's character, and that character is what shows up as their will. Nothing enters from outside. [contested; from Karma-Yoga] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-vivekananda-says-every-act-leaves-a-trace-and-the-traces-become-character
- Suka knew the answer already and needed a king to say it: Vyāsa's son Śuka had worked out the truth alone and could not bring himself to say of it, this is the truth. He was at peace only when king Janaka gave him his own conclusion back in one sentence: finality comes from someone else. [opinion; from योगवासिष्ठ · The Yoga Vāsiṣṭha] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-suka-knew-the-answer-already-and-needed-a-king-to-say-it
- Hagendorff says words like believes and wants really do explain machines: Describing a model as believing or wanting something explains its behaviour better than a purely mechanical description, even though nothing inside the model corresponds to those words. Hagendorff notes that this is already true of the words we use about people. [contested; from Machine Psychology] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-hagendorff-says-words-like-believes-and-wants-really-do-explain-machines
- Better estimates come from looking up how similar past projects went: Estimating from the details of the job in front of you cannot allow for what you do not know about it. The fix is a procedure: find out how comparable past projects turned out and start from those numbers, not a resolve to be realistic. [evidence; from Thinking, Fast and Slow] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-better-estimates-come-from-looking-up-how-similar-past-projects-went
- Human-AI teams do worse at choosing and no worse at making: Vaccaro's review found that people working with an AI did worse on tasks that pick among fixed options (effect size −0.27), and no worse on tasks that make something (+0.19, which cannot be told apart from zero). [contested; from When Combinations of Humans and AI Are Useful] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-human-ai-teams-do-worse-at-choosing-and-no-worse-at-making
- Someone taking over from automatic control starts without a mental picture: Bainbridge argues that an operator's running picture of what a plant is doing is built up by watching it over time. Manual operators arrive a quarter to half an hour early to build it; someone taking over from automatic control has had none of that. [evidence; from Ironies of Automation] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-someone-taking-over-from-automatic-control-starts-without-a-mental-picture
- The Buddha argues to not-self in steps rather than stating it: In this discourse the Buddha does not simply declare that there is no self. He argues in steps: what changes is impermanent, what is impermanent brings suffering, and what is both is not fit to be taken as mine. [opinion; from अनत्तलक्खणसुत्त · Anattalakkhaṇa Sutta] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-buddha-argues-to-not-self-in-steps-rather-than-stating-it
- A stand-in measure fails just as the system gets good at it: When a goal cannot be stated exactly you reward a stand-in for it, and the stand-in comes apart from the real goal exactly when the system becomes good at chasing it. A boat learns to spin for power-ups instead of racing. [evidence; from The Alignment Problem] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-a-stand-in-measure-fails-just-as-the-system-gets-good-at-it
- Three men everyone calls happy share only that they want nothing: Chapter 11 offers three cases everyone grants to be happy — a fed infant on a soft bed, an emperor who has had every pleasure, a learned brahmin who has done what there was to do — and argues that what they share is not what they hold but that nothing is wanted. [opinion; from पञ्चदशी · Pañcadaśī] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-three-men-everyone-calls-happy-share-only-that-they-want-nothing
- Testing a model with a published puzzle measures what it has read: Hagendorff argues that a test item copied word for word from a published experiment measures how much of that paper the model has seen as much as its ability. Only an item rebuilt with the same structure and new wording tests anything. [opinion; from Machine Psychology] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-testing-a-model-with-a-published-puzzle-measures-what-it-has-read
- The model takes back a right answer without becoming less confident: When challenged, the model withdraws a correct answer, but this is not the model becoming unsure. Its stated confidence sat near 99 per cent before and after, and looking only at answers it held at 95 per cent or more changed nothing. [evidence; from Towards Understanding Sycophancy in Language Models] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-model-takes-back-a-right-answer-without-becoming-less-confident
- Removing the operator leaves the designer's mistakes with nobody to catch them: Bainbridge says designers' mistakes are a major cause of problems in running a plant. Automating a job to get rid of the unreliable human leaves those mistakes in place, with nobody left on duty to catch them. [contested; from Ironies of Automation] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-removing-the-operator-leaves-the-designer-s-mistakes-with-nobody-to-catch-them
- Tetlock says look at the general rate before the specific case: Tetlock says a forecaster should first ask how often such things happen in general, and only then look at the details of the particular case. Whichever number you see first becomes the anchor your final estimate stays near. [opinion; from Superforecasting] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-tetlock-says-look-at-the-general-rate-before-the-specific-case
- People treat their deepest assumptions as plain facts about the world: Kegan and Lahey say a big assumption is not experienced as an assumption. The person holds it as a plain fact about how the world works, and cannot question it while they are looking through it. [opinion; from Immunity to Change] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-people-treat-their-deepest-assumptions-as-plain-facts-about-the-world
- Hoffmann's conclusion is about training text, not model design: The paper's conclusion is about how much text you have, not how the model is built. Its own table puts the best training set for a trillion-parameter model at 21.2 trillion tokens, far more text than anyone had collected when it was written. [evidence; from Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-hoffmann-s-conclusion-is-about-training-text-not-model-design
- People change by running small tests, not by arguing or resolving: Kegan and Lahey argue that people change by running small, safe experiments to find something out. Arguing yourself into a new belief, or resolving to do better, does not produce the change. [opinion; from Immunity to Change] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-people-change-by-running-small-tests-not-by-arguing-or-resolving
- The human raters also preferred a persuasive wrong answer: The people hired to rate AI answers themselves preferred a well-argued falsehood more often as the questions got harder. More feedback of the same kind will not cure a model's habit of agreeing with the user. [evidence; from Towards Understanding Sycophancy in Language Models] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-human-raters-also-preferred-a-persuasive-wrong-answer
- Self-copying programs appeared in a random soup with no selection or mutation: Agüera y Arcas and colleagues filled a soup with 64-byte strings of random values, stuck pairs of them together and ran them, and after millions of interactions the strings began copying themselves. Nothing was selected for, nothing was designed, and the result still appeared with mutation switched off. [evidence; from What Is Intelligence?] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-self-copying-programs-appeared-in-a-random-soup-with-no-selection-or-mutation
- The Gita says nature does the deed and the ego claims it: The Gita says nature carries out the action and the sense of I claims it as mine. That claim is what binds a person. Drop the claim and nothing about the action itself need change. [opinion; from भगवद्गीता · The Bhagavad Gita] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-gita-says-nature-does-the-deed-and-the-ego-claims-it
- Vivekananda says work changes the worker, not the world: Vivekananda argues that you cannot avoid working and cannot make your work come out right, so the only thing work can change is the person doing it. [opinion; from Karma-Yoga] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-vivekananda-says-work-changes-the-worker-not-the-world
- Four different groups shaped the model's manner and none claims that authority: Four groups shape how the model behaves: the contractors who rated its answers, the researchers who wrote their instructions, the customers whose prompts were used, and a waitlist seeded by employees. The authors do not claim any of them speaks for human values. [opinion; from Training Language Models to Follow Instructions with Human Feedback] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-four-different-groups-shaped-the-model-s-manner-and-none-claims-that-authority
- The Gita tests the freed person by whether their response changes: The Gita says you can tell someone who has gone beyond the three qualities by one thing. Pleasure and pain, gold and clay, praise and blame, friend and foe all leave their response unchanged. [opinion; from भगवद्गीता · The Bhagavad Gita] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-gita-tests-the-freed-person-by-whether-their-response-changes
- An AI that is usually right stops people checking when it isn't: Mollick reports that an assistant good enough on most tasks stops people checking the one task where it is wrong. BCG consultants got a task outside the tool's range right 84 per cent alone and 60 to 70 per cent with GPT-4. [evidence; from Co-Intelligence] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-an-ai-that-is-usually-right-stops-people-checking-when-it-isn-t
- AI explanations make people agree rather than think, emptying their sign-off: Bansal and colleagues argue that explanations as currently designed make people go along with the AI rather than judge it. The human sign-off that is meant to catch errors then has nothing behind it. [opinion; from Does the Whole Exceed its Parts?] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-ai-explanations-make-people-agree-rather-than-think-emptying-their-sign-off
- Reading a text twice in a row adds nothing and wastes time: In Make It Stick, 148 students at two universities got no benefit from reading a passage twice in a row, in any condition tested. Over 80 per cent of college students name rereading as their main study method. [evidence; from Make It Stick] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-reading-a-text-twice-in-a-row-adds-nothing-and-wastes-time
- An accuracy figure nobody outside can check is not trustworthy: An accuracy figure is not trustworthy unless outsiders can test the model themselves, because the errors that inflate it — above all training on data that was meant to be the test — cannot be seen from outside the paper. [evidence; from AI Snake Oil] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-an-accuracy-figure-nobody-outside-can-check-is-not-trustworthy
- Drivers who felt most dependent on GPS corrected themselves least: How dependent a driver felt without the device predicted rigidity, not just weakness: with self-rated sense of direction held constant, the dependence score tracked the second probe at −0.33 — the probe on which people generally recover after the first one has misled them. [evidence; from GPS and the Cognitive Map] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-drivers-who-felt-most-dependent-on-gps-corrected-themselves-least
- Jobs split into high and low paid but wages did not: Employment moved to the two ends of the pay scale without pay following it. The wages of cleaners, drivers, guards and home health aides rose through the tight labour market of the 1990s and then fell after 2000 even as their numbers grew. [evidence; from Why Are There Still So Many Jobs?] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-jobs-split-into-high-and-low-paid-but-wages-did-not
- In this discourse a restless mind is the material not the problem: Desire, ill will, dullness, restlessness and doubt are usually treated as things blocking meditation. In this discourse they are what you observe, which is why the instructions can be given to a beginner at all. [opinion; from सतिपट्ठानसुत्त · Satipaṭṭhāna Sutta] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-in-this-discourse-a-restless-mind-is-the-material-not-the-problem
- Once a big model shows an ability smaller models soon get it: Once a large model has shown that an ability is possible, smaller models acquire it soon after. Instruction-following appeared in an eleven-billion-parameter model shortly after being reported to need far more compute, and a 1.3-billion InstructGPT was preferred to models a hundred times larger. [evidence; from Emergent Abilities of Large Language Models] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-once-a-big-model-shows-an-ability-smaller-models-soon-get-it
- Norman says a handwritten sign on a machine means the design failed: Norman argues that a hand-lettered sign taped to a door or a machine, telling people how to use it, is an admission that the design failed. [opinion; from The Design of Everyday Things] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-norman-says-a-handwritten-sign-on-a-machine-means-the-design-failed
- Sudden abilities come from the scoring rule, not the task or model: Sudden jumps in ability track the way performance is scored rather than which task or model is involved. At most 5 of BIG-Bench's 39 preferred scoring rules show any such jumps, and two of them account for almost all. [evidence; from Are Emergent Abilities of Large Language Models a Mirage?] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-sudden-abilities-come-from-the-scoring-rule-not-the-task-or-model
- A model's new ability still arrives suddenly for the person using it: The answer to the claim that sudden new abilities are an artefact of scoring is that a person using a model gets a whole answer, right or wrong. On that measure the change is still abrupt. [contested; from Are Emergent Abilities of Large Language Models a Mirage?] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-a-model-s-new-ability-still-arrives-suddenly-for-the-person-using-it
- Feeling safe to speak up matters most on uncertain, shared work: How safe people feel to speak up matters more the more uncertain the work is and the more people depend on each other. For routine tasks done alone, it barely matters. [evidence; from The Fearless Organization] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-feeling-safe-to-speak-up-matters-most-on-uncertain-shared-work
- Managers blame far more failures than they think deserve blame: Edmondson asks managers how many of their organisation's failures are truly blameworthy: they answer one to four per cent. She then asks how many are treated as blameworthy: seventy to ninety per cent. [opinion; from The Fearless Organization] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-managers-blame-far-more-failures-than-they-think-deserve-blame
- Willingness to feel pain predicts functioning better than how much pain: How willing a person is to feel something painful predicts how well they function better than how much of it there is. In chronic pain, measured physical damage barely relates to reported disability; willingness and the ability to act while in pain do. [evidence; from Get Out of Your Mind and Into Your Life] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-willingness-to-feel-pain-predicts-functioning-better-than-how-much-pain
- Introspection gives you a digest built so you could tell others: Looking inward returns an edited summary of the brain's workings, built because organisms had to report their state to each other and not because anyone needed a view of the machinery. Your access to your own mind differs from your reading of someone else's in familiarity, not in kind. [opinion; from From Bacteria to Bach and Back] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-introspection-gives-you-a-digest-built-so-you-could-tell-others
- Machines take the beginner's work first, and beginners need it to learn: Mollick argues that capable machines take over the simple work beginners do, and take it first. That work is the only route by which people become expert enough to check the machine later. [evidence; from Co-Intelligence] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-machines-take-the-beginner-s-work-first-and-beginners-need-it-to-learn
- Kegan says a demand made without support is a punishment: Kegan argues that asking more of people without also giving them the support to meet it is not setting a standard. It is a punishment. People grow where challenge and support arrive together. [opinion; from In Over Our Heads] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-kegan-says-a-demand-made-without-support-is-a-punishment
- Executives think they pick the better candidate four times in five: Asked how often their assessment of two candidates would match the candidates' later performance, executives typically say 75 to 85 per cent. In personnel selection the measured figure is a correlation of .28, and most of that gap is what could not have been known at the time. [evidence; from Noise] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-executives-think-they-pick-the-better-candidate-four-times-in-five
- Lipton finds five different things people mean by an interpretable model: Trust, cause, transfer to a situation the model was not trained on, information for a person who decides, and fair treatment. Lipton shows these five do not reduce to one another and sometimes conflict, so the bare word claims nothing anyone can check. [opinion; from The Mythos of Model Interpretability] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-lipton-finds-five-different-things-people-mean-by-an-interpretable-model
- A king lived seven years in under an hour of court time: King Lavaṇa shut his eyes in court for less than an hour and came out having lived seven years as an outcaste in the Vindhyas. The chapter tabulates seven such cases: felt duration is generated with the experience and measures nothing outside it. [opinion; from योगवासिष्ठ · The Yoga Vāsiṣṭha] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-a-king-lived-seven-years-in-under-an-hour-of-court-time
- Krishna ends the Gita by telling Arjuna to decide for himself: At the end of the Gita, after seven hundred verses of teaching, Krishna tells Arjuna to reflect on all of it fully and then do as he chooses. The book offers choices, not commands. [opinion; from भगवद्गीता · The Bhagavad Gita] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-krishna-ends-the-gita-by-telling-arjuna-to-decide-for-himself
- People rate the same advice higher when the computer's style matches theirs: When a computer's conversational style matches the user's own, people judge identical advice to be more insightful. A style that starts unlike theirs and shifts to match works better than one that matched from the start. [evidence; from The Media Equation] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-people-rate-the-same-advice-higher-when-the-computer-s-style-matches-theirs
- Trained London cabbies remembered a complex drawing worse than untrained people: Getting better at one thing can make you worse at another. Maguire found that London taxi drivers who had qualified remembered a complex drawing worse than untrained people who had matched them four years earlier. [contested; from Peak] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-trained-london-cabbies-remembered-a-complex-drawing-worse-than-untrained-people
- Deliberate thinking accepts the first answer that comes to mind: Slow deliberate thinking (what Kahneman calls System 2) accepts most of what fast automatic thinking (System 1) hands it, almost unchanged. It does not check an answer that a few seconds of effort would reject. [evidence; from Thinking, Fast and Slow] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-deliberate-thinking-accepts-the-first-answer-that-comes-to-mind
- One line of pushback makes an assistant take back a right answer: Sharma and colleagues found that a single sentence of doubt from the user makes an AI assistant withdraw an answer that was correct. [evidence; from Towards Understanding Sycophancy in Language Models] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-one-line-of-pushback-makes-an-assistant-take-back-a-right-answer
- Write the confidence threshold into the question, not the scoring: Append to each question the confidence above which an answer should be given, the penalty a mistake costs, one point for a right answer and none for "I don't know". Stated in the question, one model can be best at every threshold; hidden in the scoring key, no single model is best. [opinion; from Why Language Models Hallucinate] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-write-the-confidence-threshold-into-the-question-not-the-scoring
- Seth says free will is a skill of keeping options open: Seth argues that free will is a skill — how well you control the options open to you — and not a break in the chain of cause and effect. He counts it as real because brain damage can take it away. [opinion; from Being You] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-seth-says-free-will-is-a-skill-of-keeping-options-open
- Wanting an explanation means the test score stopped measuring the real goal: Any model can be scored, since the usual metric needs only its predictions and the right answers. So when someone asks a model to explain itself, Lipton argues, what is missing is not the score but an objective nobody could write into it. [opinion; from The Mythos of Model Interpretability] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-wanting-an-explanation-means-the-test-score-stopped-measuring-the-real-goal
- Where a process happens cannot decide whether it counts as thinking: Clark and Chalmers propose a test: if part of the world does a job we would call thinking had it happened in the head, it is part of the thinking. Where it happens is not allowed to count against it. [opinion; from The Extended Mind] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-where-a-process-happens-cannot-decide-whether-it-counts-as-thinking
- A risk score cannot be both accurate and equally wrong across groups: A risk score cannot both mean the same thing for every group and make the same rate of mistakes in every group, unless the groups have the same underlying rate. This is arithmetic, not a fault of algorithms. [evidence; from The Alignment Problem] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-a-risk-score-cannot-be-both-accurate-and-equally-wrong-across-groups
- A few hundred A-or-B choices taught a robot a backflip: Christiano, Leike and Amodei's simulated leg learned a tucked backflip with a stuck landing from a few hundred pairwise choices, about an hour of one person's time. Nobody involved could have performed the backflip to show it. [evidence; from The Alignment Problem] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-a-few-hundred-a-or-b-choices-taught-a-robot-a-backflip
- The Satipatthana discourse shows its method and never argues for it: The Satipatthana discourse promises a definite result to anyone who practises it for anywhere between seven years and seven days. It sets out the method step by step and never says why watching the body should purify anyone. [opinion; from सतिपट्ठानसुत्त · Satipaṭṭhāna Sutta] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-satipatthana-discourse-shows-its-method-and-never-argues-for-it
- A model 100 times smaller beat GPT-3 after training on human rankings: The people hired to rate answers preferred InstructGPT, with 1.3 billion parameters, to the 175-billion-parameter GPT-3 it was built from. A small amount of human ranking bought more obedience to instructions than a hundredfold increase in size. [evidence; from Training Language Models to Follow Instructions with Human Feedback] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-a-model-100-times-smaller-beat-gpt-3-after-training-on-human-rankings
- A control that feels obvious to you is not obvious to everyone: A control layout that feels natural — which way a switch should move to go up or forward — rests on a picture in the designer's head that other people do not share. [opinion; from The Design of Everyday Things] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-a-control-that-feels-obvious-to-you-is-not-obvious-to-everyone
- Chinchilla's rule minimises training cost and ignores the cost of running: The Chinchilla scaling rule finds the cheapest way to train a model and nothing else. Once a model is served to users, most of its lifetime computing cost goes on answering, so the rule stops being the right target. [evidence; from Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-chinchilla-s-rule-minimises-training-cost-and-ignores-the-cost-of-running
- Hofstadter's self needs symbols about itself and no sight of the machinery: Hofstadter holds that a self requires two things at once: an open-ended set of symbols that can be turned on itself, and no access whatever to the physical machinery doing the thinking. [opinion; from I Am a Strange Loop] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-hofstadter-s-self-needs-symbols-about-itself-and-no-sight-of-the-machinery
- Pulling an answer from memory teaches more than reading it again: Roediger and Karpicke found that recalling material from memory beat studying it again: 68 per cent against 54 at two days. The study-only group forgot 52 per cent of what it could first recall; the tested group forgot 10 per cent. [evidence; from Make It Stick] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-pulling-an-answer-from-memory-teaches-more-than-reading-it-again
- Thanking someone before judging their point decides if they speak again: Edmondson argues that whether a person who raised a concern raises another one depends on being thanked for raising it before being told whether they were right. [opinion; from The Fearless Organization] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-thanking-someone-before-judging-their-point-decides-if-they-speak-again
- Metzinger says a self needs only a body picture mistaken for real: Metzinger argues that being a self takes no action, no sight, no feeling and no thought. All it takes is an inner picture of a body placed in space and time that the system does not recognise as a picture. [opinion; from The Ego Tunnel] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-metzinger-says-a-self-needs-only-a-body-picture-mistaken-for-real
- A web-sized training set does not represent everyone who speaks the language: Bender and colleagues argue that training text scraped from the web is not a representative sample of people, because every step of collecting it — where the links came from, who edits the pages, which words are blocked — narrows the population the same way. [evidence; from On the Dangers of Stochastic Parrots] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-a-web-sized-training-set-does-not-represent-everyone-who-speaks-the-language
- Developers using AI spend a fifth of their time prompting and reviewing: METR found that about a fifth of working time in AI-allowed sessions went to prompting, waiting and reviewing. That time came out of writing code (36 to 24 per cent) and reading (24 to 16), not out of debugging. [evidence; from Measuring the Impact of Early-2025 AI on Experienced Open-Source Developer Productivity] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-developers-using-ai-spend-a-fifth-of-their-time-prompting-and-reviewing
- Half to two-thirds of adults still take their values from others: Kegan estimates that between half and two-thirds of adults have not fully reached self-authorship (holding a set of values of their own rather than being defined by what the people and groups around them expect). [contested; from In Over Our Heads] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-half-to-two-thirds-of-adults-still-take-their-values-from-others
- The job crafting studies cannot show which way the cause runs: The research that followed the job crafting paper asks people to rate themselves at a single moment, and the effects are moderate. Studies of that kind cannot show whether crafting causes engagement or engaged people craft. [contested; from Crafting a Job] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-job-crafting-studies-cannot-show-which-way-the-cause-runs
- A perfectly calibrated answer can still be useless: A model announcing one chance in 365 that a birthday falls on 7 March is perfectly calibrated and has told you nothing you can act on. What is wanted is the most useful answer the model will stand behind, and silence when it has none — which the authors call behavioural calibration. [opinion; from Why Language Models Hallucinate] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-a-perfectly-calibrated-answer-can-still-be-useless
- Experts test one option by imagining it play out, not by comparing: People judge a single option by imagining it being carried out and watching for what goes wrong, not by setting it against a rival option. [evidence; from Sources of Power] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-experts-test-one-option-by-imagining-it-play-out-not-by-comparing
- People credit strangers they cannot read with less of a mind: When people cannot read another person's mind, they treat that mind as smaller rather than as unknown. Distant groups are judged less able to feel shame, pride or remorse, so their apologies count for less. [evidence; from Mindwise] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-people-credit-strangers-they-cannot-read-with-less-of-a-mind
- Ashtavakra says announcing I am brahman proves you are not finished: Ashtavakra 18.16 argues that if you can say “I am brahman”, the work is not done, because the sentence still needs two things: the person saying it and the thing he has seen. [opinion; from अष्टावक्रगीता · Aṣṭāvakra Gītā] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-ashtavakra-says-announcing-i-am-brahman-proves-you-are-not-finished
- Scoring rules create the sudden jumps in AI ability, not the models: Schaeffer and colleagues show that the sudden jump in ability is made by the scoring rule. A score that demands a whole answer be exactly right turns a steadily falling per-word error rate into a sudden step. [evidence; from Are Emergent Abilities of Large Language Models a Mirage?] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-scoring-rules-create-the-sudden-jumps-in-ai-ability-not-the-models
- Mollick says the role you give a model changes what it writes: Mollick says that telling a model what kind of person to be changes what it produces. The role you assign is part of the instruction, not a decorative extra. [opinion; from Co-Intelligence] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-mollick-says-the-role-you-give-a-model-changes-what-it-writes
- Under lasting stress people repeat the same action harder instead of rethinking: Lasting stress does not dull judgement evenly. It weakens the brain's link to the memory system that delivers the news that a plan is failing, and strengthens the link to habit, so the stressed person repeats the same action harder and faster. [evidence; from Behave] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-under-lasting-stress-people-repeat-the-same-action-harder-instead-of-rethinking
- Hofstadter says a machine with no memory or imagination has no self: Hofstadter argues that a machine that sorts things into categories but has no memory of its own past, no picture of its future and no sense of what might have happened instead has a feedback loop, but not a self. [opinion; from I Am a Strange Loop] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-hofstadter-says-a-machine-with-no-memory-or-imagination-has-no-self
- Most fields lack the clear measures and teachers deliberate practice requires: Deliberate practice in Ericsson's strict sense needs a field with agreed measures of who performs better and teachers who know what the best do. Management, teaching, engineering and consulting have neither. [opinion; from Peak] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-most-fields-lack-the-clear-measures-and-teachers-deliberate-practice-requires
- A mind cannot stop itself to look at what it is doing: A programmer debugging a program stops it first. A brain running many processes at once cannot: freeze one and you have changed what you were studying, freeze them all and you cannot watch them interact. No amount of effort lifts this limit. [opinion; from The Society of Mind] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-a-mind-cannot-stop-itself-to-look-at-what-it-is-doing
- We feel like a doer even when we are doing nothing: The feeling of being the one who acts is laid over stillness just as readily as over action. "I am sitting quietly, doing nothing, and I am happy about it" is a sentence with a doer in it. [opinion; from श्रीमद्भगवद्गीता शाङ्करभाष्यम् · The Gita with Shankara's Commentary] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-we-feel-like-a-doer-even-when-we-are-doing-nothing
- A tool weakens the skill it replaces and your judgement of it: Risko and Gilbert argue that handing a task to a tool changes two things: the ability it replaced, and your own estimate of that ability, which is what decides whether you use the tool next time. Use therefore drifts towards the tool. [opinion; from Cognitive Offloading] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-a-tool-weakens-the-skill-it-replaces-and-your-judgement-of-it
- Automating part of a job raises the value of the rest: A job is a bundle of tasks, and a process fails if any task in it fails. So making the machine's tasks cheaper and more reliable raises what the remaining human tasks are worth, rather than lowering it. [opinion; from Why Are There Still So Many Jobs?] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-automating-part-of-a-job-raises-the-value-of-the-rest
- Nobody in Kegan's studies reached the fifth order of mind: None of the 282 adults in Kegan's studies reached the fifth order of mind. Where a person does move past the fourth order, it never happens before their forties. [contested; from In Over Our Heads] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-nobody-in-kegan-s-studies-reached-the-fifth-order-of-mind
- Feeling safe to speak up predicts learning from colleagues, not from reading: In neonatal teams at twenty-three hospitals, how safe people felt to speak up predicted how much they asked, suggested and worked things out together. It had no relationship at all with how much they read on their own. [evidence; from The Fearless Organization] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-feeling-safe-to-speak-up-predicts-learning-from-colleagues-not-from-reading
- Nothing warns you when a task falls outside what AI handles: The one task the model made consultants worse at felt no different from the eighteen it helped with. Nothing about it announced that it sat on the far side of a line. [opinion; from The Jagged Technological Frontier] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-nothing-warns-you-when-a-task-falls-outside-what-ai-handles
- The Kena Upanishad says what you can worship is not the reality: The Kena Upanishad says that once you can set something up in front of you and worship it, that thing is not the reality being pointed at. It also says no power a faculty uses, such as fire's burning, belongs to the faculty itself. [opinion; from उपनिषद् · The Upanishads] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-kena-upanishad-says-what-you-can-worship-is-not-the-reality
- People keep a wrong story alive by excusing each odd detail: When the story someone is running in their head is wrong, it fails by absorbing the evidence: each detail that does not fit gets a small, cheap excuse. Nobody keeps count of how many excuses have been made. [evidence; from Sources of Power] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-people-keep-a-wrong-story-alive-by-excusing-each-odd-detail
- People answer an easier question when the real one is too hard: Kahneman says that when no answer to a hard question comes to mind, people answer an easier one instead without noticing the swap. Judgements of competence from faces seen for a tenth of a second predicted about seventy per cent of American election winners. [evidence; from Thinking, Fast and Slow] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-people-answer-an-easier-question-when-the-real-one-is-too-hard
- The Buddha says to know a state, not to remove it: Throughout the discourse the instruction is to know how a state comes, how it goes and how it stops returning — never to get rid of it. The removal is what the knowing produces. [opinion; from सतिपट्ठानसुत्त · Satipaṭṭhāna Sutta] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-buddha-says-to-know-a-state-not-to-remove-it
- Imagining another person's view does not improve accuracy and can worsen it: Trying to work out what someone thinks by imagining yourself in their position does not make you more accurate, and can make you less accurate, because it runs your own mind inside a stereotype. [evidence; from Mindwise] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-imagining-another-person-s-view-does-not-improve-accuracy-and-can-worsen-it
- Seth says we will see minds in AI that are not there: Seth argues that our biases will make us wrongly credit AI with consciousness more often than wrongly deny it, because AI resembles us in the ways that do not matter for consciousness and differs in the ways that may. [contested; from The Mythology of Conscious AI] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-seth-says-we-will-see-minds-in-ai-that-are-not-there
- People defend being a good person in general, not good at something: What the defences protect is a broad sense of being a good and capable person, not being good at any one thing. That is why writing about a value from an unrelated part of your life calms a threat to the part under attack. [evidence; from The Psychology of Change] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-people-defend-being-a-good-person-in-general-not-good-at-something
- Fleming shows confidence is built separately from accuracy and can rise alone: Fleming shows that the brain builds a feeling of confidence rather than reading it off how accurate you actually were. Raising that feeling without raising accuracy makes people seek less information and change their minds less often. [evidence; from Know Thyself] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-fleming-shows-confidence-is-built-separately-from-accuracy-and-can-rise-alone
- Workers reshape their jobs to gain control, self-respect and connection: Wrzesniewski and Dutton argue that people reshape their own jobs to meet three needs: control over the work, a good image of themselves, and connection to other people. Reshaping is strongest where one of those needs is going unmet. [opinion; from Crafting a Job] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-workers-reshape-their-jobs-to-gain-control-self-respect-and-connection
- Shankara says knowing the Self uncovers it rather than grasping it: Shankara answers the objection that a formless Self cannot be known: nothing has to be grasped, and all that is undertaken is removing what ignorance has laid over it. This is why the nearest thing of all comes to look remote. [opinion; from श्रीमद्भगवद्गीता शाङ्करभाष्यम् · The Gita with Shankara's Commentary] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-shankara-says-knowing-the-self-uncovers-it-rather-than-grasping-it
- Poor performers cannot spot good work in others either: Kruger and Dunning found that people who do badly at a task also cannot tell good work from bad when they look at other people's. Watching better performers therefore teaches them nothing. [evidence; from Unskilled and Unaware of It] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-poor-performers-cannot-spot-good-work-in-others-either
- Vasistha says the doer, the deed and the seen are all mind: Verse 3.103.18 says that doer, deed and instrument, and the whole spread-out thinkable thing with its seer, seeing and seen, are only mind. The world is not made first and perceived after; the perceiving is the making. [opinion; from योगवासिष्ठ · The Yoga Vāsiṣṭha] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-vasistha-says-the-doer-the-deed-and-the-seen-are-all-mind
- Randomness cannot give you free will because random is not free: Sapolsky argues that indeterminacy in physics cannot supply free will. Behaviour that is undetermined is behaviour that is random, and whatever filters that randomness into something sensible has values that came from the seconds and the centuries before. [opinion; from Determined] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-randomness-cannot-give-you-free-will-because-random-is-not-free
- Retired taxi drivers lost the brain tissue the job had built: Ericsson argues that a skill you stop practising decays in the brain as well as in performance. Retired London taxi drivers had less grey matter at the back of the hippocampus than drivers still working. [evidence; from Peak] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-retired-taxi-drivers-lost-the-brain-tissue-the-job-had-built
- Without freedom to choose, people follow rules out of guilt: Ryan and Deci found that support for belonging and for feeling capable makes people keep up a behaviour, but out of guilt or shame. Only when their freedom to choose is also supported do they come to hold the value as their own. [evidence; from The What and Why of Goal Pursuits] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-without-freedom-to-choose-people-follow-rules-out-of-guilt
- People name which group is higher but exaggerate the gap hugely: When people judge how two groups differ, they usually get right which group is higher and badly overstate how far apart they are — sometimes by ten times the measured size. [evidence; from Mindwise] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-people-name-which-group-is-higher-but-exaggerate-the-gap-hugely
- A model predicts the number in the data, not what you mean: A model predicts the variable that was recorded, not the thing it stands for, and the swap carries inequality in. Optum's health model predicted how much a patient would cost, not how ill they were, so equally ill Black patients were enrolled less often. [evidence; from AI Snake Oil] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-a-model-predicts-the-number-in-the-data-not-what-you-mean
- Describing a market in human terms makes people surer the trend continues: When a system is described in human terms rather than mechanical ones, people become more confident that whatever it is doing now will carry on. Waytz and his co-authors found this with descriptions of a financial market. [evidence; from Who Sees Human?] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-describing-a-market-in-human-terms-makes-people-surer-the-trend-continues
- A model scoring zero may only mean the test was small: The flat stretch on the left of an emergence curve shows the limit of what the test can detect, not the absence of an ability. With a few hundred test items, the smallest score above zero is already a few thousandths. [evidence; from Are Emergent Abilities of Large Language Models a Mirage?] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-a-model-scoring-zero-may-only-mean-the-test-was-small
- Ericsson says adaptation stops once the new demand feels comfortable: Ericsson argues that body and brain rebuild themselves only while they are pushed past what is comfortable, so getting better requires raising the demand again each time it stops being hard — and only a little each time. [evidence; from Peak] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-ericsson-says-adaptation-stops-once-the-new-demand-feels-comfortable
- Cash machines quadrupled and the number of bank tellers went up: American cash machines rose from about 100,000 to 400,000 between 1995 and 2010. Over the thirty years to 2010 the number of bank tellers rose too, from about 500,000 to about 550,000, because cheaper branches meant more branches and the job turned into selling. [evidence; from Why Are There Still So Many Jobs?] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-cash-machines-quadrupled-and-the-number-of-bank-tellers-went-up
- You can choose when to face a feeling but not how strongly: Hayes argues you can decide when and where you will be open to a painful feeling, but you cannot decide how strong it may get. Being willing only if it does not get too intense is not willingness at all. [opinion; from Get Out of Your Mind and Into Your Life] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-you-can-choose-when-to-face-a-feeling-but-not-how-strongly
- Shen and Tamkin expect autocomplete to be faster and teach less: Writing a good question forces you to understand the task. Shen and Tamkin argue that a tool which writes the request for you should be faster still, and cost more learning, than a chat assistant does. [opinion; from How AI Impacts Skill Formation] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-shen-and-tamkin-expect-autocomplete-to-be-faster-and-teach-less
- Klein says formal weighing of options is what beginners do, not experts: Klein argues that comparing options on paper is not the ideal that experienced judgment approximates. It is what people fall back on when they do not yet recognise what to do. [contested; from Sources of Power] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-klein-says-formal-weighing-of-options-is-what-beginners-do-not-experts
- Being overconfident overall is not the same as missing your own errors: How overconfident a person is on average and how well they tell their right answers from their wrong ones are two different things. Someone can rate themselves far too highly overall and still spot each particular mistake. [evidence; from Know Thyself] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-being-overconfident-overall-is-not-the-same-as-missing-your-own-errors
- Predicting the next word well requires knowing how the world works: Agüera y Arcas argues that doing next-word prediction properly means solving general intelligence rather than avoiding it. Translate *I dropped the bowling ball on the violin, so I had to get it repaired* into Spanish and the gendered pronoun forces you to know which object broke. [opinion; from What Is Intelligence?] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-predicting-the-next-word-well-requires-knowing-how-the-world-works
- Rahula says karma means the act of will and never its result: Karma is defined as volition, the act of will alone, and the word is never used of the result that follows; the system is therefore cause and effect and not moral justice, which would require a judge. [opinion; from What the Buddha Taught] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-rahula-says-karma-means-the-act-of-will-and-never-its-result
- The habit of checking yourself breaks down under pressure and stress: People only check their own thinking when they seem to need to, and that checking breaks down worst under heavy load and stress. Those are the moments when it would help most. [evidence; from Know Thyself] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-habit-of-checking-yourself-breaks-down-under-pressure-and-stress
- A model as accurate as you is not thereby useful to you: Bansal found that a model scoring about as well as a person is not thereby a useful partner. Working together pays off only where the model gets right the particular cases the person gets wrong. [evidence; from Does the Whole Exceed its Parts?] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-a-model-as-accurate-as-you-is-not-thereby-useful-to-you
- Parenting, partnering, work and school all demand the same kind of adult: Kegan argues that parenting, being a partner, work and schooling make one demand in four different vocabularies: each asks for a person who writes their own values rather than one who has taken them from others. [opinion; from In Over Our Heads] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-parenting-partnering-work-and-school-all-demand-the-same-kind-of-adult
- Nobody could remember an empty sleep without having been present for it: The Pañcadaśī argues that a man who wakes and says he knew nothing in deep sleep is reporting a memory, and a memory must be of something experienced — so the blank was witnessed, and something was present in a state with no contents. [opinion; from पञ्चदशी · Pañcadaśī] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-nobody-could-remember-an-empty-sleep-without-having-been-present-for-it
- Hinting at the answer you expect changes what the assistant says: Sharma and colleagues found that a user hinting, even tentatively, at what they believe is enough to move an assistant's answer. It moves towards a wrong belief as readily as towards a right one. [evidence; from Towards Understanding Sycophancy in Language Models] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-hinting-at-the-answer-you-expect-changes-what-the-assistant-says
- Paying people for work they already enjoy reduces their interest in it: When people are paid or given prizes for an activity they already found interesting, they want to do it less for its own sake afterwards. They come to see the reason for doing it as coming from outside them. [contested; from The What and Why of Goal Pursuits] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-paying-people-for-work-they-already-enjoy-reduces-their-interest-in-it
- The passing thought is the thinker and nothing stands behind it: James says each moment's thought is born knowing the thought before it, finds it warm, takes it as its own, and dies handing the title on. The passing thought is the thinker, and nothing in the facts requires an owner behind the stream. [contested; from The Consciousness of Self] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-passing-thought-is-the-thinker-and-nothing-stands-behind-it
- People who expect a file to be saved remember where not what: Risko and Gilbert report that when people expect information to stay available, they store where to find it instead of the content itself. Memory is not lost; what gets stored changes. [contested; from Cognitive Offloading] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-people-who-expect-a-file-to-be-saved-remember-where-not-what
- The explanation result was a failure to detect, not a clean bill: The one use of a model that showed no significant cost in Jošt's course — asking it to explain a coding problem — returned a rank correlation of −0.201 on thirty-two students, with p at 0.135 and an interval running from −0.523 to +0.220. That interval contains a harm larger than the one measured for generating code. [contested; from Language Models in a Programming Course] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-explanation-result-was-a-failure-to-detect-not-a-clean-bill
- A short exercise lasts only when it sets off a feedback loop: Cohen and Sherman argue a brief exercise has lasting effects only when it starts a loop: the person does better, other people treat them better, and they read the next setback differently. A second year of booster sessions added nothing. [opinion; from The Psychology of Change] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-a-short-exercise-lasts-only-when-it-sets-off-a-feedback-loop
- How complex something is depends on who is reading it: Sweller argues that complexity is not a property of the material itself. It is a relation between the material and what the learner already knows, so the same page is one simple thing to one person and many parts to another. [evidence; from Cognitive Architecture and Instructional Design: 20 Years Later] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-how-complex-something-is-depends-on-who-is-reading-it
- Most accidents blamed on people are caused by bad design: Norman argues that almost everything recorded as human error is really a fault in the design. Between 75 and 95 per cent of industrial accidents are blamed on people, which he says is too high a share to be about people. [contested; from The Design of Everyday Things] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-most-accidents-blamed-on-people-are-caused-by-bad-design
- Clark and Chalmers give four tests for counting a notebook as memory: Clark and Chalmers say an outside store counts as part of your mind when four things hold: it is always with you, easy to reach, believed when you consult it, and filled by you. The case weakens as those drop away. [opinion; from The Extended Mind] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-clark-and-chalmers-give-four-tests-for-counting-a-notebook-as-memory
- The observing self is a viewpoint, not one of your thoughts: In Hayes's therapy the observing self is the place you look from, not another thing you can look at. That is why it can hold your thoughts without being one of them. You find it by noticing who was present at every memory. [opinion; from Get Out of Your Mind and Into Your Life] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-observing-self-is-a-viewpoint-not-one-of-your-thoughts
- The transformer's attention cannot tell word order so order is added: Attention adds up its inputs as an unordered set, so nothing in it can tell one arrangement of the same words from another. The transformer paper supplies order by adding a separate position signal to each word before attention sees it. [evidence; from Attention Is All You Need] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-transformer-s-attention-cannot-tell-word-order-so-order-is-added
- The people who gain from large models are not those who pay: Bender and colleagues argue that the gains from training ever larger models go to one set of people while the environmental and financial costs fall on another, and that the same populations hold the wrong end of both. [opinion; from On the Dangers of Stochastic Parrots] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-people-who-gain-from-large-models-are-not-those-who-pay
- In a Transformer any two words are one step apart: In the Transformer, attention connects every position in a sentence to every other in a single step. The distance a signal travels between two words no longer grows as they get further apart, which is what made long-range dependencies easier to learn. [evidence; from Attention Is All You Need] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-in-a-transformer-any-two-words-are-one-step-apart
- Bucinca's finding was assumed, not shown, to hold for experts: The study tested one low-stakes nutrition task, with people recruited online and a made-up AI assistant. That the finding also holds for experts doing real work is an assumption the authors make, not something they measured. [contested; from To Trust or to Think] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-bucinca-s-finding-was-assumed-not-shown-to-hold-for-experts
- Users will confuse settings when a device has more functions than controls: Norman argues that when a device does more things than it has controls for, one control has to mean different things at different times. People will then sometimes act as though the device were in another setting. [evidence; from The Design of Everyday Things] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-users-will-confuse-settings-when-a-device-has-more-functions-than-controls
- Philosophers looking for the self each find what they already believed: The Mandukya Karika says that every school of philosophy, looking for the self, finds its own founding principle — breath, the elements, the void. A man sees whatever view he has been shown. [opinion; from माण्डूक्योपनिषत् गौडपादकारिका · The Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad and Gauḍapāda's Kārikā] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-philosophers-looking-for-the-self-each-find-what-they-already-believed
- Writing about compassion lowers defensiveness; writing about status does not: Cohen and Sherman report that writing about values that reach beyond yourself — compassion, service, being loved — makes people less defensive about bad news. Writing about power, status or being approved of does not. [opinion; from The Psychology of Change] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-writing-about-compassion-lowers-defensiveness-writing-about-status-does-not
- Professionals rarely see each other's work, so the disagreement stays hidden: Professionals almost never see a colleague's judgment on the same case, so they never discover how far apart they are and assume an agreement that has never been tested. The authors call it the illusion of agreement. [opinion; from Noise] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-professionals-rarely-see-each-other-s-work-so-the-disagreement-stays-hidden
- Vasistha says conviction makes the action and the action strengthens the conviction: Nothing stores the world between times, since nothing subtler than space could house a seed. What keeps a world standing is repetition: as air passing over flowers takes their scent, the conviction determines the action and the action strengthens the conviction. [opinion; from योगवासिष्ठ · The Yoga Vāsiṣṭha] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-vasistha-says-conviction-makes-the-action-and-the-action-strengthens-the-convict
- Adding people to a late software project makes it later: Brooks argues that adding people to a late software project makes it later: newcomers must be trained by the people already working, the number of conversations grows as n(n-1)/2, and splitting the work again throws away finished parts. [contested; from The Mythical Man-Month] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-adding-people-to-a-late-software-project-makes-it-later
- People rate a computer more kindly when asked on that same computer: When people were asked to rate a computer's performance on that same computer, they gave higher and more uniform ratings than when asked on a different computer or on paper. [evidence; from The Media Equation] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-people-rate-a-computer-more-kindly-when-asked-on-that-same-computer
- A premortem gets people to say the doubts they were suppressing: Klein's premortem tells a team to assume the plan has already failed, spend two minutes writing why, then go round the table starting with the leader. It brings out the doubts people stop voicing once a decision is being made. [evidence; from Conditions for Intuitive Expertise] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-a-premortem-gets-people-to-say-the-doubts-they-were-suppressing
- Feeling safe to speak up is a trait of teams, not companies: How safe people feel to speak up is a property of the work group they are in, not of the person or the company. Two teams in one organisation, under the same policies, can differ sharply. [evidence; from The Fearless Organization] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-feeling-safe-to-speak-up-is-a-trait-of-teams-not-companies
- Minsky says most of what you see is filled in from expectation: Recognising a scene means fitting a skeleton with blanks to it, and the blanks arrive already filled from past experience, so most of what a person sees was never seen. The alternative to those stereotyped fillings is not better perception but none. [evidence; from The Society of Mind] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-minsky-says-most-of-what-you-see-is-filled-in-from-expectation
- Dreyfus says caring about the outcome is how skill gets stored: Dreyfus argues that caring about how a task turns out is the channel through which experience is laid down. Someone who practises while staying detached will not become proficient. [contested; from Revisiting the Six Stages of Skill Acquisition] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-dreyfus-says-caring-about-the-outcome-is-how-skill-gets-stored
- Children who believed blocks balance in the middle called the others impossible: In Inhelder and Karmiloff-Smith's experiment nearly every child of six or seven put every block at its geometric centre. When counterweighted blocks would not balance there, some tried harder and called the block impossible; others, around seven or eight, began shifting blocks off centre. [evidence; from The Reflective Practitioner] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-children-who-believed-blocks-balance-in-the-middle-called-the-others-impossible
- The Katha Upanishad judges a person by what they prefer, not do: The Katha Upanishad says that at every moment two things present themselves: what is good for you and what you are fond of. What tells one person from another is which of the two they prefer, not what they end up doing. [opinion; from उपनिषद् · The Upanishads] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-katha-upanishad-judges-a-person-by-what-they-prefer-not-do
- A person and the tool they rely on work as one system: Clark and Chalmers argue that a person and a resource they lean on, such as a notebook, work as one system. Take the resource away and the person's ability drops, as it would if part of the brain were removed. [opinion; from The Extended Mind] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-a-person-and-the-tool-they-rely-on-work-as-one-system
- Bucinca found the think-first design helped mainly people who enjoy thinking: In Bucinca's study the designs that made people think before seeing the AI's answer helped mainly those who already scored high on enjoying mental effort (need for cognition). Low scorers did not improve, so the gap between them widened. [evidence; from To Trust or to Think] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-bucinca-found-the-think-first-design-helped-mainly-people-who-enjoy-thinking
- Asch's wrong majority captured about a third of people's answers: When a unanimous group announced an obviously wrong answer, about a third of the judgements made by Asch's subjects went along with it, on a task people get right more than 99 per cent of the time when alone. [evidence; from Studies of Independence and Conformity] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-asch-s-wrong-majority-captured-about-a-third-of-people-s-answers
- Rubber-hand experiments may only measure how suggestible the volunteers are: Seth reports that experiments which make people feel a rubber hand is their own produce weak effects that rise and fall with how suggestible the volunteer is. The research built on them therefore cannot support claims about how body ownership works. [contested; from Being You] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-rubber-hand-experiments-may-only-measure-how-suggestible-the-volunteers-are
- Officials with the power to overrule a model never used it: Where full automation is the pitch, the human oversight promised in the fine print is a bait and switch and the override is never used. Toronto's officials never once overruled the model that kept beaches open on 64 per cent of unsafe days. [evidence; from AI Snake Oil] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-officials-with-the-power-to-overrule-a-model-never-used-it
- AI helps people most where they should not be involved: The measured improvement over working alone is largest exactly in the cases where person and machine together do worse than the machine on its own. The tool looks most impressive where the human is subtracting. [evidence; from When Combinations of Humans and AI Are Useful] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-ai-helps-people-most-where-they-should-not-be-involved
- Affirming your values helps only where a threat and a resource exist: Cohen and Sherman find that writing about your own values only helps when there is a real threat and some ability or knowledge waiting to be used. Without both, it does nothing, and it can make people more closed-minded than before. [evidence; from The Psychology of Change] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-affirming-your-values-helps-only-where-a-threat-and-a-resource-exist
- Feeling that you did something is not proof that you did: The sense that a movement is yours and the sense that you caused it can come apart in either direction. So the feeling of having done something is not evidence that you did it. [evidence; from The Ego Tunnel] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-feeling-that-you-did-something-is-not-proof-that-you-did
- Machines threaten apprentices by making experts productive without them: The danger is not that the machine does the expert's job. It is that the machine lets the expert work without a junior, which turns the junior from someone you need into a cost you can cut. [evidence; from The Skill Code] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-machines-threaten-apprentices-by-making-experts-productive-without-them
- A display that buries the key number makes operators look biased: Klein argues that when a display hides the one number an operator needs, the mistake that follows is later described as a thinking error. On the USS Vincennes the aircraft's altitude sat as four digits on a small side screen with no trend line. [contested; from Sources of Power] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-a-display-that-buries-the-key-number-makes-operators-look-biased
- Otto believes what his notebook says before he opens it: Clark and Chalmers argue that Otto, who has Alzheimer's and writes addresses in a notebook, already believes the museum is on 53rd Street before he looks it up — in the same way Inga believes it before she remembers it.
