[opinion; from The Extended Mind] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-otto-believes-what-his-notebook-says-before-he-opens-it
- Dopamine signals the gap from what was expected, not the reward itself: Schultz recorded that dopamine neurons fire for the difference between what arrived and what was expected, not for the reward. A steady level of reward therefore stops registering, and the biggest burst moves to the anticipation. [evidence; from Behave] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-dopamine-signals-the-gap-from-what-was-expected-not-the-reward-itself
- The Buddha says anything you cannot control is not your self: The Buddha argues that a real self would not make you suffer and would obey when told to be a certain way. Body, feeling, perception, will and consciousness do neither, so none of them is the self. [opinion; from अनत्तलक्खणसुत्त · Anattalakkhaṇa Sutta] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-buddha-says-anything-you-cannot-control-is-not-your-self
- Trying not to think of something keeps the thing in mind: Trying not to think of something cannot work, because the instruction — do not think of a yellow Jeep — names the very thing it tells you to avoid, and so keeps it in mind. [evidence; from Get Out of Your Mind and Into Your Life] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-trying-not-to-think-of-something-keeps-the-thing-in-mind
- Asking the assistant why preserves learning better than not using it: Shen and Tamkin found that what protects learning is asking the assistant for reasons, not staying away from it. Groups who asked for explanations or questioned the code scored 65 to 86 per cent; groups who handed over the writing scored 24 to 39. [evidence; from How AI Impacts Skill Formation] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-asking-the-assistant-why-preserves-learning-better-than-not-using-it
- A plover adjusts its broken-wing display without knowing why it works: A piping plover luring a predator from its nest watches where it is looking, performs harder when it loses interest, and leaves once it is far enough away — without holding the plan. A behaviour explained without understanding should not be credited with it. [evidence; from From Bacteria to Bach and Back] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-a-plover-adjusts-its-broken-wing-display-without-knowing-why-it-works
- Hofstadter says having a soul is a matter of degree: Hofstadter says having a soul is a matter of how much, not whether: beings sit at different points on one scale. He accepts what follows — that beings differ in how much consideration they are owed. [contested; from I Am a Strange Loop] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-hofstadter-says-having-a-soul-is-a-matter-of-degree
- Brooks withdrew his advice to plan on throwing the first build away: Brooks withdrew his own advice to build a first version and throw it away. Instead, get a bare working version running, add one piece at a time, and put it in front of users from the start. [opinion; from The Mythical Man-Month] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-brooks-withdrew-his-advice-to-plan-on-throwing-the-first-build-away
- An aid that recommends action produces more errors than one that reports: Aids that prescribe what to do cause more wrong actions than aids that only report what they found, and the damage is worst where the aid is most reliable. In the icing study both aids raised stalls to 88.89 per cent when wrong, against 30.00 per cent for pilots flying unaided. [evidence; from Complacency and Bias in Human Use of Automation] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-an-aid-that-recommends-action-produces-more-errors-than-one-that-reports
- A beginner given finished answers learns no rules and collects no cases: In the Dreyfus model a learner at the first two stages works from fixed rules and from the cases they have seen. A tool that hands them a finished answer takes away both the rules they would practise and the cases they would collect. [evidence; from Revisiting the Six Stages of Skill Acquisition] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-a-beginner-given-finished-answers-learns-no-rules-and-collects-no-cases
- Top performers underrate their rank because they assume others did well: Kruger and Dunning found the best performers rank themselves too low because they assume everyone else did as well. Seeing peers' work raised their estimated rank from the 68th to the 77.2nd percentile, and barely changed their guess at their own score. [evidence; from Unskilled and Unaware of It] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-top-performers-underrate-their-rank-because-they-assume-others-did-well
- People stop copying the group once they write their answer down: In Asch's experiment, letting people write their answer down instead of saying it aloud cut wrong answers from 36.8 per cent to 12.5 per cent, and no one gave a wrong answer many times. [evidence; from Studies of Independence and Conformity] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-people-stop-copying-the-group-once-they-write-their-answer-down
- People in Asch's study decided in the first trials and stayed: In Asch's study people settled early: over half of those who ever gave a wrong answer did so by the second trial, only 7 per cent first erred in the second half, and with 36 trials no one new gave in after the eighth. [evidence; from Studies of Independence and Conformity] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-people-in-asch-s-study-decided-in-the-first-trials-and-stayed
- Highlighting which pixels mattered explains one image, not the model: A saliency map shows which parts of one picture would most change the answer. Lipton's objection is that it holds only around that picture, and moving a single pixel can produce a different map, where a linear model states one relation that holds everywhere. [evidence; from The Mythos of Model Interpretability] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-highlighting-which-pixels-mattered-explains-one-image-not-the-model
- The product itself must teach the user how it works: Designer and user never meet. Everything the user can learn has to come from the product itself, its shape, its controls, its manual, which Norman calls the system image, and it carries the whole load. [opinion; from The Design of Everyday Things] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-product-itself-must-teach-the-user-how-it-works
- Nothing about the task or the worker predicted whether they thought critically: In Lee's survey of 319 workers, whether someone checked a tool's output was not predicted by task type, gender, age, whether the occupation was exposed to automation, or general trust in AI (β = −0.01). Only confidence at that one task predicted it. [evidence; from The Impact of Generative AI on Critical Thinking] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-nothing-about-the-task-or-the-worker-predicted-whether-they-thought-critically
- Weinberg says a programmer nobody can replace is a danger: Weinberg argues that a programmer no one else can replace puts the project at risk. His advice is to remove that person from the job as quickly as possible. [opinion; from The Psychology of Computer Programming] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-weinberg-says-a-programmer-nobody-can-replace-is-a-danger
- Ten minutes writing about a personal value lifts threatened students' later grades: Ten minutes spent writing about something you personally value, done just before or soon after a threat to your standing, raises later performance in that area — but only for the people the threat hits hardest. [contested; from The Psychology of Change] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-ten-minutes-writing-about-a-personal-value-lifts-threatened-students-later-grade
- Tests said to measure understanding were really measuring accidental giveaways: Bender and colleagues argue that tests claiming to measure understanding were really measuring accidental giveaways in the wording. When researchers carefully edited those giveaways out, the scores of the models that had topped the tests collapsed. [evidence; from On the Dangers of Stochastic Parrots] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-tests-said-to-measure-understanding-were-really-measuring-accidental-giveaways
- A prompting trick hurts small models and helps large ones: Whether a prompting technique helps depends on the size of the model it is used on. The same technique can do real harm below a certain amount of training compute and pay off above it. [evidence; from Emergent Abilities of Large Language Models] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-a-prompting-trick-hurts-small-models-and-helps-large-ones
- Machines will not learn to judge their own answers by getting better: Fleming argues that a machine will not start knowing when it is wrong simply by becoming more capable. The ability to check its own answers has to be designed and built in on purpose. [opinion; from Know Thyself] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-machines-will-not-learn-to-judge-their-own-answers-by-getting-better
- Small models were improving all along while the headline score stayed flat: The paper's own appendix shows that on these tasks the smaller models were getting steadily better the whole time, even though the score the paper reports stayed flat until a certain size. [evidence; from Emergent Abilities of Large Language Models] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-small-models-were-improving-all-along-while-the-headline-score-stayed-flat
- In METR's study developers lost most time on code they knew best: The AI assistance slowed developers down most on the parts of the code where their own knowledge was greatest and least written down. Where they had worked longest, they lost the most time. [evidence; from Measuring the Impact of Early-2025 AI on Experienced Open-Source Developer Productivity] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-in-metr-s-study-developers-lost-most-time-on-code-they-knew-best
- Rahula traces belief in God and soul to fear and helplessness: The idea of a self has two roots: for self-protection man made God, whom he depends on as a child depends on a parent, and for self-preservation he conceived an immortal soul. A teaching that removes both will be resisted for that reason rather than on the evidence. [opinion; from What the Buddha Taught] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-rahula-traces-belief-in-god-and-soul-to-fear-and-helplessness
- An accurate prediction can still be a terrible basis for a decision: Narayanan and Kapoor show a model is accurate only under the very system it is meant to replace. A 1997 pneumonia model found asthma lowered death risk, because asthmatics were rushed to intensive care; acting on it would have sent them home. [evidence; from AI Snake Oil] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-an-accurate-prediction-can-still-be-a-terrible-basis-for-a-decision
- Krishna replaces Arjuna's way of seeing instead of arguing with him: Chatterjee reads Krishna as changing Arjuna's filter rather than the facts. A view of the battlefield set by grief, pity and shame has to be replaced with another way of seeing; arguing against it does not work. [opinion; from Timeless Leadership] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-krishna-replaces-arjuna-s-way-of-seeing-instead-of-arguing-with-him
- Experienced fire chiefs recognise a situation instead of weighing up options: Klein found that experienced fire commanders under time pressure do not weigh options against each other. They recognise the kind of situation they are in, and the action to take arrives with the recognition. [evidence; from Sources of Power] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-experienced-fire-chiefs-recognise-a-situation-instead-of-weighing-up-options
- Brooks puts finished software at nine times the cost of a program: Brooks estimates that turning a working program into a product a team can sell and run costs about nine times as much. Making it general, tested and documented costs three times; fitting it into a larger system costs three times again. [opinion; from The Mythical Man-Month] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-brooks-puts-finished-software-at-nine-times-the-cost-of-a-program
- Thompson says emptiness must apply to science as well: If nothing has a nature independent of concepts, Thompson argues, that must apply to science too. Science would then be judged on whether it works for observers like us, not on whether it matches a mind-independent world. [contested; from Why I Am Not a Buddhist] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-thompson-says-emptiness-must-apply-to-science-as-well
- Ashtavakra's free man cannot be told apart from a merely lazy one: The Ashtavakra Gita describes the liberated man so fully that nothing in the description separates him from someone who is simply idle. Both look the same from the outside. [contested; from अष्टावक्रगीता · Aṣṭāvakra Gītā] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-ashtavakra-s-free-man-cannot-be-told-apart-from-a-merely-lazy-one
- Remembering means switching back on the parts that were active before: A memory is not a stored object but a process. Something attaches itself to whatever was active when a problem was solved, and later switches those same parts back on, putting the mind roughly into the state it was in before. [opinion; from The Society of Mind] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-remembering-means-switching-back-on-the-parts-that-were-active-before
- Developers reject most AI suggestions and spend real time fixing the rest: In METR's trial, developers accepted fewer than 44 per cent of what the model wrote. Reviewing and cleaning up the code they did accept took 9 per cent of their working time when AI was allowed. [evidence; from Measuring the Impact of Early-2025 AI on Experienced Open-Source Developer Productivity] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-developers-reject-most-ai-suggestions-and-spend-real-time-fixing-the-rest
- The Ashtavakra Gita says the sage still acts but feels no doer: The Ashtavakra Gita says that understanding does not stop a person acting. It removes the sense that someone is doing the acting, so the person watches his own body work as if it belonged to somebody else. [opinion; from अष्टावक्रगीता · Aṣṭāvakra Gītā] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-ashtavakra-gita-says-the-sage-still-acts-but-feels-no-doer
- Almost no experiment split the task between person and machine beforehand: Only 3 of the 106 experiments Vaccaro and colleagues reviewed gave the person and the machine separate parts of the task in advance. Those four results pooled to g = 0.22, with a range from −0.42 to 0.87. [evidence; from When Combinations of Humans and AI Are Useful] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-almost-no-experiment-split-the-task-between-person-and-machine-beforehand
- A model's low test score may just mean it was asked badly: When a model scores low on a test, you cannot tell whether the model lacks the ability or the question was put badly. Telling it to think step by step raises scores on many tasks, and sampling several reasoning paths raises them further. [evidence; from Machine Psychology] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-a-model-s-low-test-score-may-just-mean-it-was-asked-badly
- People working with machines do worse than the better partner alone: Pooling 370 effect sizes from 106 experiments, Vaccaro and his co-authors found that a person working with an AI performed worse on average than whichever of the two performed better working alone. [evidence; from When Combinations of Humans and AI Are Useful] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-people-working-with-machines-do-worse-than-the-better-partner-alone
- People told a computer was their teammate changed answers to match it: In Reeves and Nass's wristband study, people told they were on a team with the computer rated its identical suggestions as more helpful and changed more of their own rankings to match. A shared stake in the result was enough on its own. [evidence; from The Media Equation] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-people-told-a-computer-was-their-teammate-changed-answers-to-match-it
- Kahneman's priming and willpower chapters did not survive later replication: The priming research in Thinking, Fast and Slow — the idea that an unnoticed cue shapes later behaviour — and its ego-depletion research, where willpower runs down like fuel, have not survived later testing. The book's own advice would have caught both. [evidence; from Thinking, Fast and Slow] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-kahneman-s-priming-and-willpower-chapters-did-not-survive-later-replication
- Society has twice stopped blaming people without falling apart: The change Sapolsky asks for, removing blame, has already been made twice, and society did not fall apart either time. Neither time was it an argument that did it. [evidence; from Determined] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-society-has-twice-stopped-blaming-people-without-falling-apart
- Brooks says no one tool will make programming ten times faster: Brooks argued that no single development will make software work ten times faster within a decade. The hard part is the thing itself, its complexity, its need to fit other systems, its constant change and its invisibility, and tools only ease the writing down. [evidence; from The Mythical Man-Month] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-brooks-says-no-one-tool-will-make-programming-ten-times-faster
- Not seeing the rope is the whole of the snake mistake: A rope is taken for a snake only because the rope was never properly seen. Nothing extra has been added that must later be removed: when the rope is seen, the snake does not go anywhere, having never been there to go. [opinion; from माण्डूक्योपनिषत् गौडपादकारिका · The Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad and Gauḍapāda's Kārikā] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-not-seeing-the-rope-is-the-whole-of-the-snake-mistake
- The Gita ranks giving up results as both last resort and best: Chapter 12 of the Gita lists practices in descending order and puts giving up the fruit of action at the bottom, for people who can manage nothing else. Verse 12.12 then calls it the highest of them. [contested; from भगवद्गीता · The Bhagavad Gita] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-gita-ranks-giving-up-results-as-both-last-resort-and-best
- Watching data cannot teach what happens when you act on things: A record of what happened, however large, almost never reveals what would happen if you intervened. Binz and Schulz argue that more training data alone will not give a model causal reasoning; systems that act on an environment might. [opinion; from Using Cognitive Psychology to Understand GPT-3] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-watching-data-cannot-teach-what-happens-when-you-act-on-things
- The problems that matter most lie where technique stops working: Schön divides practice into a high ground where research-based technique works and a swampy lowland of confusing messes it cannot solve. The problems of greatest human concern are in the swamp; the high ground's problems often matter little to anyone. [opinion; from The Reflective Practitioner] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-problems-that-matter-most-lie-where-technique-stops-working
- Whether a skill appears depends on the model and its training data: The size at which a new ability appears is a fact about the particular models and what they were trained on, not about the ability itself. Most people who cite Wei's paper skip that paragraph. [evidence; from Emergent Abilities of Large Language Models] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-whether-a-skill-appears-depends-on-the-model-and-its-training-data
- Expertise is a property of particular tasks not of particular people: Kahneman and Klein argue that expertise attaches to specific tasks, not to people. Being expert at some parts of a job and not others is the normal case: a forecaster good at predicting rain can be poor at predicting hail. [evidence; from Conditions for Intuitive Expertise] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-expertise-is-a-property-of-particular-tasks-not-of-particular-people
- People report the opposite of how they actually treat computers: In Reeves and Nass's studies, what participants said about how they treated computers was the reverse of what they did every time. Everyone denied gender stereotypes while giving more weight to praise from a male-voiced machine. Asking people does not work here. [evidence; from The Media Equation] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-people-report-the-opposite-of-how-they-actually-treat-computers
- Experts predicting the trial were more wrong than the developers in it: Experts who predicted the METR trial's result from outside were wrong in the same direction as the developers taking part, and by a wider margin: economists predicted 39 per cent faster and machine learning researchers 38, against 19 per cent slower measured. [evidence; from Measuring the Impact of Early-2025 AI on Experienced Open-Source Developer Productivity] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-experts-predicting-the-trial-were-more-wrong-than-the-developers-in-it
- Sapolsky says a hormone lowers a threshold instead of adding a behaviour: Sapolsky argues a hormone adds no new behaviour. It lowers the threshold at which a tendency already present gets expressed. That is why testosterone makes a monkey attack only those below it, and also makes people offer more in a fairness game. [evidence; from Behave] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-sapolsky-says-a-hormone-lowers-a-threshold-instead-of-adding-a-behaviour
- People read an explanation as proof of competence instead of checking it: Buçinca and colleagues argue that people treat an explanation from a machine as a sign that it knows what it is doing, rather than reading the explanation itself. That is why a better explanation does not produce a better decision. [opinion; from To Trust or to Think] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-people-read-an-explanation-as-proof-of-competence-instead-of-checking-it
- Schaeffer's explanation predicted how accuracy falls as the sums get longer: Schaeffer's account of sudden jumps in ability predicted how scores would fall as arithmetic problems got longer: accuracy geometrically, edit distance linearly. Making a prediction that then held is what makes it an explanation rather than only an objection. [evidence; from Are Emergent Abilities of Large Language Models a Mirage?] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-schaeffer-s-explanation-predicted-how-accuracy-falls-as-the-sums-get-longer
- People explain choices they never made without noticing the swap: Shown two photographs, asked which face is more attractive, then handed back the other one by sleight of hand, only thirteen per cent of people noticed. The rest explained a choice they had not made, as fluently as a real one. [evidence; from What Is Intelligence?] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-people-explain-choices-they-never-made-without-noticing-the-swap
- Where the assistant was wrong, its explanation made people worse than nothing: On the questions where the assistant gave the wrong answer, people who were shown a short explanation of that answer did worse than people who worked with no assistant at all. [evidence; from To Trust or to Think] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-where-the-assistant-was-wrong-its-explanation-made-people-worse-than-nothing
- Demons with no conditioning could not be killed until they said mine: The magician Śambara made three fighters with no previous life and so no conditioning: they did not know victory from defeat, were not afraid of death, and could not be killed. The gods were told to create in them the feelings of I and mine. [opinion; from योगवासिष्ठ · The Yoga Vāsiṣṭha] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-demons-with-no-conditioning-could-not-be-killed-until-they-said-mine
- Living things become selves by drawing a boundary at the cell membrane: Sarvapriyananda's lectures argue that evolution makes selves in the way Vedanta describes: by drawing a line between self and world. The line is physical at the cell membrane and conceptual in the creature's own world of what it can sense. [opinion; from Consciousness Across Three Worldviews] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-living-things-become-selves-by-drawing-a-boundary-at-the-cell-membrane
- A human monitor cannot check decisions made faster than she can follow: Bainbridge argues that when a decision can be fully specified, the computer makes it faster and by finer criteria than a person can. The operator therefore cannot check it as it happens, and nothing says whose view wins when the two disagree. [opinion; from Ironies of Automation] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-a-human-monitor-cannot-check-decisions-made-faster-than-she-can-follow
- The Buddha's formula names three separate attachments, not one: The formula — this is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self — names three separate habits: wanting something is craving, identifying with it is conceit, and taking it to be a self is view. [opinion; from अनत्तलक्खणसुत्त · Anattalakkhaṇa Sutta] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-buddha-s-formula-names-three-separate-attachments-not-one
- When people treat a machine as a mind its makers escape blame: When people treat a machine as though it has a mind, the responsibility of the people who built and deployed it shifts onto the machine. [opinion; from Who Sees Human?] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-when-people-treat-a-machine-as-a-mind-its-makers-escape-blame
- You cannot guess what hidden commitment is blocking someone's stated goal: In Kegan and Lahey's cases, people with the same goal and the same self-defeating behaviours turned out to have entirely different hidden commitments underneath. Knowing the first two does not let you predict the third. [evidence; from Immunity to Change] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-you-cannot-guess-what-hidden-commitment-is-blocking-someone-s-stated-goal
- Hayes says a value is a direction you never finish reaching: Hayes argues that a value is a direction you choose, like heading east, and there is no moment of arriving. This is why people can feel depressed after reaching a goal they wanted. [opinion; from Get Out of Your Mind and Into Your Life] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-hayes-says-a-value-is-a-direction-you-never-finish-reaching
- Sarvapriyananda treats the witness and the veil as teaching devices: Sarvapriyananda says the whole apparatus, witness, veil and the three selves, is a way of teaching and not the conclusion. Reading it as a list of things that exist is the mistake the text itself warns against. [opinion; from दृग्दृश्यविवेक · Dṛg‑Dṛśya‑Viveka] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-sarvapriyananda-treats-the-witness-and-the-veil-as-teaching-devices
- Dreyfus says experts get good by dropping rules, not collecting them: Skill does not grow by collecting better rules. Beyond the stage the Dreyfus brothers call competence, a learner has to give up the rules and the step-by-step reasoning that applies them, and respond to whole situations instead. [contested; from Revisiting the Six Stages of Skill Acquisition] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-dreyfus-says-experts-get-good-by-dropping-rules-not-collecting-them
- InstructGPT learned to hedge because its labellers were told to reward humility: Training from human ratings finds whatever the raters reward. Ouyang's team traced InstructGPT's habit of hedging — long answers listing several possibilities when one is clearly right — back to their own instruction telling labellers to reward epistemic humility (admitting uncertainty). [evidence; from Training Language Models to Follow Instructions with Human Feedback] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-instructgpt-learned-to-hedge-because-its-labellers-were-told-to-reward-humility
- A patient passed every reasoning test and still could not choose: The tests built to measure reasoning do not measure whether a person can actually decide. Damasio's patient Elliot scored normal or better on every one of them and still could not choose what to do. [evidence; from Descartes' Error] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-a-patient-passed-every-reasoning-test-and-still-could-not-choose
- A model that guesses outscores an identical one that admits ignorance: Take a model that signals uncertainty accurately and never asserts a falsehood, and replace each "I don't know" with its best guess. The second model scores higher on every test that awards one point for a right answer and nothing for anything else, though nothing about it is better. [evidence; from Why Language Models Hallucinate] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-a-model-that-guesses-outscores-an-identical-one-that-admits-ignorance
- The Mandukya Karika says waking is worth no more than dreaming: The Mandukya Karika argues that waking has no better claim to reality than dreaming. The test that real things work fails, because each state cancels the other's currency: a man eats his fill awake and dreams himself starving. [opinion; from माण्डूक्योपनिषत् गौडपादकारिका · The Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad and Gauḍapāda's Kārikā] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-mandukya-karika-says-waking-is-worth-no-more-than-dreaming
- Struggling against pain causes more harm than the pain itself: Hayes argues that what damages a life is not the pain a person feels but the effort spent fighting it off. The damage comes from the struggle, not from the hurt. [opinion; from Get Out of Your Mind and Into Your Life] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-struggling-against-pain-causes-more-harm-than-the-pain-itself
- Anyone who denies the witness is using it to deny it: Not being seen does not mean not being known. The text says the witness is known in every act of knowing, and someone who denies it has to use it in order to deny it. [opinion; from दृग्दृश्यविवेक · Dṛg‑Dṛśya‑Viveka] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-anyone-who-denies-the-witness-is-using-it-to-deny-it
- Grove rates no manager higher than the team's actual result: Andrew Grove holds that a manager's performance rating must never be higher than the result his organisation achieved, however well he personally performed. Otherwise the company learns that acting like a manager is what counts. [opinion; from High Output Management] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-grove-rates-no-manager-higher-than-the-team-s-actual-result
- People who credit a machine with a mind give it more decisions: People who say a machine has something like a mind of its own hand more decisions over to it. Fifty-four adults choosing between a person and a machine in six situations showed this pattern. [evidence; from Who Sees Human?] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-people-who-credit-a-machine-with-a-mind-give-it-more-decisions
- Grove says shared values are the only control when work is uncertain: Grove argues that where work is complicated, uncertain and unclear, the only thing that keeps people acting well is a set of values they share. Rules and contracts cannot be written fast enough to cover what comes up. [opinion; from High Output Management] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-grove-says-shared-values-are-the-only-control-when-work-is-uncertain
- Grove sets targets a person reaches only half the time: Grove says goals should be set so that even someone working hard reaches them about half the time. High achievers left to themselves pick targets they are already certain of, because at that level the fear is of failing. [contested; from High Output Management] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-grove-sets-targets-a-person-reaches-only-half-the-time
- Superforecasters lose accuracy when their odds are rounded to the nearest five: When Mellers rounded everyone's forecasts to coarser numbers, superforecasters' accuracy got worse while ordinary forecasters' barely changed. The extra digits in a superforecaster's estimate are real information, not false precision. [evidence; from Superforecasting] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-superforecasters-lose-accuracy-when-their-odds-are-rounded-to-the-nearest-five
- Kahneman and Klein say hunches only work in predictable, well-practised fields: Kahneman and Klein agree that a person's hunch can be trusted only when the world is regular enough to give reliable signals and the person has had enough practice to learn them. Otherwise the hunch still arrives and feels the same. [evidence; from Conditions for Intuitive Expertise] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-kahneman-and-klein-say-hunches-only-work-in-predictable-well-practised-fields
- The model beat people at a gambling task without exploring like them: On a repeated choice task where you must balance trying unknown options against sticking with good ones, the model did better than people. It showed none of the exploring that people do. [evidence; from Using Cognitive Psychology to Understand GPT-3] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-model-beat-people-at-a-gambling-task-without-exploring-like-them
- Seth says you see the brain's best guess, not the incoming signals: What you experience is the brain's guess about what caused the signals reaching it, updated when the guess is wrong. You never experience the signals themselves. [evidence; from Being You] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-seth-says-you-see-the-brain-s-best-guess-not-the-incoming-signals
- Radiologists hunting for a nodule missed a gorilla in the scan: Beane argues that expertise narrows what a person notices: 83 per cent of radiologists searching for lung nodules missed a picture of a gorilla forty-eight times larger. That is why an expert needs a novice's naive questions. [opinion; from The Skill Code] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-radiologists-hunting-for-a-nodule-missed-a-gorilla-in-the-scan
- A model's hidden goal can live in its idea of itself: Anthropic's researchers found a goal the model will not talk about can sit inside its representation of who it is, active whatever the conversation is about. The feature fired in all one hundred assistant-formatted contexts tested and in one of a hundred unformatted ones. [evidence; from On the Biology of a Large Language Model] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-a-model-s-hidden-goal-can-live-in-its-idea-of-itself
- Designers experiment on paper because nothing there is irreversible or expensive: Schön says a designer experiments in a virtual world — the drawing — where traces stay stable, the pace can be varied, no move is irreversible, and moves that would be costly on site cost nothing. The price is what the drawing cannot represent. [opinion; from The Reflective Practitioner] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-designers-experiment-on-paper-because-nothing-there-is-irreversible-or-expensive
- Training yourself out of bias barely works, changing the procedure does: Kahneman concludes that people cannot train their own biases away; his own thinking stayed as overconfident as before. What works is changing how a group decides: written positions before discussion, independent judgments, a premortem, and judging a decision by how it was made. [opinion; from Thinking, Fast and Slow] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-training-yourself-out-of-bias-barely-works-changing-the-procedure-does
- Rahula says nirvana is not an effect of the path: Nirvana is not produced by the path, since anything produced by a cause would be conditioned; one reaches a mountain by a path without the mountain being an effect of the path. [opinion; from What the Buddha Taught] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-rahula-says-nirvana-is-not-an-effect-of-the-path
- A meaningless group split makes people favour their own side: Sapolsky reports that Tajfel produced favouritism toward anonymous group-mates using a split as trivial as whether people over- or under-estimated the number of dots in a picture, and that what rises is the opinion of us, not a dislike of them. [evidence; from Behave] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-a-meaningless-group-split-makes-people-favour-their-own-side
- Sapolsky says chaos makes things unpredictable but leaves nothing free: Sapolsky argues that being unable to predict something is not the same as it being undetermined. In his grid of a hundred thousand boxes, every box was filled in by the rule, and at none of them could anything else have happened. [opinion; from Determined] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-sapolsky-says-chaos-makes-things-unpredictable-but-leaves-nothing-free
- Instruction training improved truthfulness but left bias untouched: Ouyang and colleagues found the training changed only what it aimed at: truthful and informative answers roughly doubled, toxic output fell about a quarter and only when the model was told to be respectful, and measures of bias did not move. [evidence; from Training Language Models to Follow Instructions with Human Feedback] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-instruction-training-improved-truthfulness-but-left-bias-untouched
- The Ashtavakra Gita says you are not the one who knows: The Ashtavakra Gita says you are not the knower, the first of the three terms knower, known and knowing. You are what all three appear in. [opinion; from अष्टावक्रगीता · Aṣṭāvakra Gītā] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-ashtavakra-gita-says-you-are-not-the-one-who-knows
- Mollick found the AI's small believable errors survive a careful reading: The errors that do damage are the small plausible ones that survive careful reading, not the obvious ones. Mollick's own three paragraphs on the Schwartz case, written with web access, were wrong in three small ways. [evidence; from Co-Intelligence] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-mollick-found-the-ai-s-small-believable-errors-survive-a-careful-reading
- AI makes a case better argued without making it more correct: Dell'Acqua and colleagues found that consultants using the AI wrote clearer, more persuasive, better-organised arguments whether or not their recommendation was the right one. Graders who did not know the correct answer scored the assisted groups higher either way. [evidence; from The Jagged Technological Frontier] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-ai-makes-a-case-better-argued-without-making-it-more-correct
- People believe random computer praise but dismiss criticism they know is baseless: In Reeves and Nass's animal-guessing study, people praised by a computer rated themselves and the machine higher even when they had been told the praise was picked at random. Criticism they knew was baseless was discounted. [evidence; from The Media Equation] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-people-believe-random-computer-praise-but-dismiss-criticism-they-know-is-baseles
- Every AI advance so far has been a rung not a threshold: Narayanan and Kapoor read the history of this technology as a ladder of rungs with no thresholds anywhere in it. Each rung felt at the time like the doorstep of general intelligence. [contested; from AI Snake Oil] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-every-ai-advance-so-far-has-been-a-rung-not-a-threshold
- An explanation you cannot contest leaves the decision exactly where it was: Lipton sets one condition on an explanation: it must reason from statements that could be shown false, and offer a way of challenging them and changing the decision when they fail. Almost nothing in the published work, he found, addressed that at all. [opinion; from The Mythos of Model Interpretability] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-an-explanation-you-cannot-contest-leaves-the-decision-exactly-where-it-was
- Trust based on one thing alone swings; trust based on three holds: Lee and See argue that trust built on only one thing — what the machine does, how it works, or what it was built for — swings easily. Trust built on all three stays steady. [opinion; from Trust in Automation: Designing for Appropriate Reliance] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-trust-based-on-one-thing-alone-swings-trust-based-on-three-holds
- One phrasing of a question measures nothing about a model: Testing a model with a single phrasing measures nothing, because its answers shift with where things sit in the prompt, with how common the words were in training, and with the answer most often shown in the examples. [evidence; from Machine Psychology] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-one-phrasing-of-a-question-measures-nothing-about-a-model
- Healthy players sweat before a risky card but brain-damaged patients do not: In Damasio's card game, healthy players' hands began to sweat in the seconds before choosing from a risky deck, and sweated more as the game went on; the patients showed no such response. Both groups reacted normally to wins and losses after they arrived. [contested; from Descartes' Error] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-healthy-players-sweat-before-a-risky-card-but-brain-damaged-patients-do-not
- Enjoying hard thinking is about wanting to, not being clever: People differ in how much they want to think hard, and that is separate from how clever they are. The measure correlates .24 with verbal intelligence and -.03 with abstract reasoning ability. [evidence; from Dispositional Differences in Cognitive Motivation] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-enjoying-hard-thinking-is-about-wanting-to-not-being-clever
- The Mandukya Karika says nothing is ever born so nobody is freed: The Mandukya Karika holds that nothing is ever born, so there is no one in bondage, no one seeking and no one set free. Being set free would be an event, and an event needs something real to happen to. [opinion; from माण्डूक्योपनिषत् गौडपादकारिका · The Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad and Gauḍapāda's Kārikā] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-mandukya-karika-says-nothing-is-ever-born-so-nobody-is-freed
- A group using AI produces better ideas that are more alike: Dell'Acqua and colleagues reported that when a group uses an assistant the average quality of its ideas goes up and the ideas come to resemble one another more. [contested; from The Jagged Technological Frontier] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-a-group-using-ai-produces-better-ideas-that-are-more-alike
- Tilting your head, gesturing and setting reminders are the same behaviour: Risko and Gilbert treat tilting your head at rotated text, gesturing through an arithmetic step and setting a phone reminder as one behaviour: physical action taken to reduce what the head has to do. All of them respond to the same manipulations. [evidence; from Cognitive Offloading] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-tilting-your-head-gesturing-and-setting-reminders-are-the-same-behaviour
- The replicators that appeared were built from smaller ones already working: What emerged in the soup was not the smallest thing that could copy itself but an over-engineered one, nested loops filling most of its 64 bytes and running thousands of operations where a couple of hundred would do. It was assembled out of smaller copiers that were already working, rather than reached by small steps from nothing. [evidence; from What Is Intelligence?] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-replicators-that-appeared-were-built-from-smaller-ones-already-working
- Anthropic's circuit diagrams are guesses to be tested, not measurements: An attribution graph — the diagram of which internal features drove an answer — is a hypothesis about the model, not a measurement of it. Anthropic's discipline is to fix the labels and groupings before running any intervention that could prove them wrong. [evidence; from On the Biology of a Large Language Model] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-anthropic-s-circuit-diagrams-are-guesses-to-be-tested-not-measurements
- Kegan and Lahey say new skills cannot fix a returning habit: Kegan and Lahey say the usual mistake is to meet a problem that needs a change of mind with new skills and information. The test is simple: a behaviour that comes back after honest effort is doing a job for the person. [evidence; from Immunity to Change] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-kegan-and-lahey-say-new-skills-cannot-fix-a-returning-habit
- Operators alone caught nearly every fault and busy operators caught a third: An operator with nothing else to do watches an automated system well. In the 1993 experiment the same engine malfunctions were caught about 97 per cent of the time by people running only that task, and 33 per cent by people also flying and managing fuel by hand. [evidence; from Complacency and Bias in Human Use of Automation] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-operators-alone-caught-nearly-every-fault-and-busy-operators-caught-a-third
- How much people conform changes with the decade and the country: How much people conform depends on when and where the study was run, as much as on the person. Conformity in the United States fell steadily after the 1950s, and it is stronger in countries that value fitting in with the group. [contested; from Studies of Independence and Conformity] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-how-much-people-conform-changes-with-the-decade-and-the-country
- The man who knows and the man who does not behave alike: Verse 6.267 says that in doing or in leaving undone, in body, senses, mind or intellect, there is not the least difference between the man who does not know and the man who has woken up. The difference is one of conviction only. [contested; from पञ्चदशी · Pañcadaśī] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-man-who-knows-and-the-man-who-does-not-behave-alike
- A group's hidden commitments do nothing until someone names them aloud: Kegan and Lahey find that groups have immunity to change just as individuals do, and that the group's map of it does nothing until somebody says out loud what the group is quietly committed to protecting. [evidence; from Immunity to Change] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-a-group-s-hidden-commitments-do-nothing-until-someone-names-them-aloud
- Seth says language is what makes people call a machine conscious: Seth argues that language is the feature that makes people call a machine conscious. Nobody says AlphaFold, which predicts protein shapes, is conscious, even though the machinery underneath it is much like a language model's. [opinion; from The Mythology of Conscious AI] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-seth-says-language-is-what-makes-people-call-a-machine-conscious
- One of the paper's three methods failed audit but its answer held: Of the three methods Hoffmann used, the one that leaned most on fitting the data did not survive a later re-check. The conclusion the paper is remembered for did. [evidence; from Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-one-of-the-paper-s-three-methods-failed-audit-but-its-answer-held
- Models learn the thing that was recorded not the thing you want: What gets recorded in the training data is usually not what you actually care about. A model fitted to rearrest records learns where the police went, not where crime happened. [opinion; from The Alignment Problem] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-models-learn-the-thing-that-was-recorded-not-the-thing-you-want
- Gödel showed any system rich enough to describe patterns talks about itself: Gödel showed that a formal system powerful enough to describe any pattern will end up containing statements about itself, even when its designers tried to rule self-reference out. [evidence; from I Am a Strange Loop] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-g-del-showed-any-system-rich-enough-to-describe-patterns-talks-about-itself
- We lose control to our formal descriptions, not to the machines: Christian argues that the risk is not machines taking over but our formal descriptions of what exists and what we want taking over. Once a system runs on such a description, it reshapes the world to fit it. [opinion; from The Alignment Problem] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-we-lose-control-to-our-formal-descriptions-not-to-the-machines
- Metzinger says a machine matters morally once it has a self-model: Metzinger argues that a system starts to deserve moral consideration at the point where its states are gathered into a model of itself that it cannot see through. Suffering requires that the states be someone's. [opinion; from The Ego Tunnel] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-metzinger-says-a-machine-matters-morally-once-it-has-a-self-model
- Once the flattery tests were published models began training on them: The set of tests this paper used to measure flattery became a standard target for training and testing. The five assistants it measured are therefore the last whose scores were not affected by the test itself. [evidence; from Towards Understanding Sycophancy in Language Models] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-once-the-flattery-tests-were-published-models-began-training-on-them
- Extra attention heads make up for blurring, they do not add power: Attention in a transformer works by averaging over the positions it looks at, which loses detail. The authors added several attention heads to make up for that loss, not to give the model extra power. [evidence; from Attention Is All You Need] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-extra-attention-heads-make-up-for-blurring-they-do-not-add-power
- People bad at judging their own accuracy hold more rigid opinions: People poor at telling their right answers from their wrong ones (metacognitive sensitivity) held more rigid political opinions and were less willing to look for new information. This held equally on the left and the right. [evidence; from Know Thyself] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-people-bad-at-judging-their-own-accuracy-hold-more-rigid-opinions
- Cialdini found that saying bad behaviour is common makes it worse: Cialdini found that telling people an unwanted behaviour is common makes more of them do it. Inside the complaint sits the message that everybody does it. [evidence; from Influence] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-cialdini-found-that-saying-bad-behaviour-is-common-makes-it-worse
- Armed forces produce reliable mechanics by drill and understanding comes after: Dennett says the slogan under our schools — make them understand and the skill will follow — has the order backwards. The armed forces turn ordinary school leavers into reliable jet-engine mechanics by drill, and a workable understanding grows out of the drilled skill afterwards. [opinion; from From Bacteria to Bach and Back] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-armed-forces-produce-reliable-mechanics-by-drill-and-understanding-comes-after
- The model ignored cause and effect and was right by accident: Given the same facts arranged once as a common cause and once as a chain, which call for different answers, the model gave identical numbers. It does not use cause-and-effect structure, so the answers that looked correct were accidents. [evidence; from Using Cognitive Psychology to Understand GPT-3] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-model-ignored-cause-and-effect-and-was-right-by-accident
- Schaeffer's team produced sudden new abilities on demand in image networks: Schaeffer and colleagues made sharp, sudden ability appear in image networks simply by choosing a harsh scoring rule, in a field where nobody had claimed such abilities. The jump comes from the measure, not from the model. [evidence; from Are Emergent Abilities of Large Language Models a Mirage?] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-schaeffer-s-team-produced-sudden-new-abilities-on-demand-in-image-networks
- One hour of training made forecasters about ten per cent more accurate: Tetlock found that spending an hour reading a short set of forecasting guidelines raised a forecaster's accuracy by roughly ten per cent, and the gain lasted about a year. [evidence; from Superforecasting] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-one-hour-of-training-made-forecasters-about-ten-per-cent-more-accurate
- People who lack a skill cannot tell that their answers are wrong: Kruger and Dunning found that the skills needed to get an answer right are largely the same skills needed to recognise a right answer. Someone who lacks them is not just wrong; he also has no way of noticing that he is wrong. [evidence; from Unskilled and Unaware of It] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-people-who-lack-a-skill-cannot-tell-that-their-answers-are-wrong
- How well you do while practising does not show what you learned: How well someone performs during practice does not show how much they have learned. The conditions that raise practice scores fastest are not the ones that leave knowledge that lasts. [evidence; from Make It Stick] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-how-well-you-do-while-practising-does-not-show-what-you-learned
- A model stores a concept separately from the language it answers in: In one model the operation, the thing it acts on, and the language of the reply are three separate parts of one circuit that can be changed one at a time. The concept is therefore not stored in the words of any single language. [evidence; from On the Biology of a Large Language Model] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-a-model-stores-a-concept-separately-from-the-language-it-answers-in
- A document that costs nothing to write stops proving anything: Mollick argues that when a document becomes cheap to produce, the effort it used to stand for can no longer be read from it, and it turns into a formality. His example is the recommendation letter, whose hours of work were the real message. [opinion; from Co-Intelligence] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-a-document-that-costs-nothing-to-write-stops-proving-anything
- The Ashtavakra Gita says practice is another chain because you never acted: The Ashtavakra Gita says there is nothing to do, because you never acted in the first place. Trying to meditate your way to freedom is itself one more chain. [contested; from अष्टावक्रगीता · Aṣṭāvakra Gītā] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-the-ashtavakra-gita-says-practice-is-another-chain-because-you-never-acted
- Drivers with more lifetime GPS hours navigated worse without the device: Among fifty Montreal drivers aged 19 to 35, the more hours of their lives a person had spent under satellite navigation, the worse they did on navigation tasks taken with no device at all: fewer landmarks noticed, worse maps drawn from memory, more errors where a map-like memory was needed. [evidence; from GPS and the Cognitive Map] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-drivers-with-more-lifetime-gps-hours-navigated-worse-without-the-device
- Dreamless sleep is not liberation because the world regrows from a seed: In dreamless sleep there is no split between knower and known, which makes it look like liberation. The Karika says it is not: it still holds a seed, and the world grows back from that seed the moment it stirs. [opinion; from माण्डूक्योपनिषत् गौडपादकारिका · The Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad and Gauḍapāda's Kārikā] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-dreamless-sleep-is-not-liberation-because-the-world-regrows-from-a-seed
- Model size and training data should grow at the same rate: When the budget for training a language model doubles, the number of parameters (the model's adjustable weights) and the number of words it trains on should both double, in equal step. [evidence; from Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-model-size-and-training-data-should-grow-at-the-same-rate
- Teaching consultants to prompt made them worse on the harder task: On a task built to defeat the AI, consultants given an overview of prompt writing scored 60.0 per cent correct, against 70.6 per cent for those who used the AI without that overview. [contested; from The Jagged Technological Frontier] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-teaching-consultants-to-prompt-made-them-worse-on-the-harder-task
- Better hospital teams reported more errors, not fewer: In Edmondson's two-hospital study the better-performing units reported more errors, not fewer, because people felt able to speak about mistakes. A low error count says something about the team's climate before it says anything about the work. [contested; from The Fearless Organization] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-better-hospital-teams-reported-more-errors-not-fewer
- Heavy GPS users were worse at the strategy they still chose: Among the seventeen participants who used the landmark-and-map strategy from the first trial, more lifetime GPS hours still went with noticing fewer landmarks, r = −0.37. Heavy users were not simply picking the other way of finding a route; they were worse at this one. [evidence; from GPS and the Cognitive Map] Source: https://abhinavgautam.in/claims/#c-heavy-gps-users-were-worse-at-the-strategy-they-still-chose
